# Changelog of the data structures

Changes to the tables, schemas and scripts (not to individual claims). Newest first.

## 24 November 2026 — US branch spelling Armored (branch `rc1-data-fixes`, from main `817306c9`, RV16)

Scott approved the rc1 data-fix branch (24 November 2026). 19 US units had `branch` `Armoured` (the British vocabulary spelling) while their unit names use “Armored”.

- **Vocabulary:** `Armored` added to `branch` for US armored formations. `Armoured` remains the spelling for British, Commonwealth and other non-US armoured and panzer formations.
- **Units and claims:** all 19 US units (`US-ARM-002D`–`US-ARM-014D`, `US-ARM-016D`, `US-ARM-020D`, `US-CCA-002D`, `US-CCR-004D`, `US-TDB-001B`, `US-TF-BUTLER`) and their 525 claim rows: `branch` old value `Armoured`, new value `Armored`; reason: the US Army spelling, matching the unit name (rc1 review RV16). Annotated in each `unit_note` and claim `notes`. Unit ids are unchanged. No UK, Canadian or Polish row was changed.

## 24 November 2026 — Derived commander_on_date columns (branch `commander-on-date`, from main `d2ceff6b`)

Scott approved part 1 of the rc1 review item RV10 (24 November 2026): a derived commander on the claim date in the build claims export. No `data/claims/` row was edited; the source-stated `commander` field is unchanged. Part 2 (research for units with no tenure) was deferred (roadmap 428). Tightening inferred tenure starts is roadmap 429.

- **Build columns:** `commander_on_date`, `commander_on_date_person_id`, `commander_on_date_source` (`claim` / `tenure`) and `commander_on_date_basis` (`stated` / `narrative` / `inferred_start` / `inferred_end` / `inferred_start_end`) on `build/all_claims.csv`, `build/all_claims.json` and `build/claims.geojson`. Lookup rules are in `scripts/commanders.py` (`attach_commander_on_date`) and `schema/README.md`.
- **Version:** `schema_version` 1.1.0 (additive derived columns) and `data_version` 1.1.0-rc1. `CITATION.cff` follows `data_version`.
- **Tests:** scenarios 362–365 (Taylor via tenure, Erskine with an inferred start, a claim with no tenure, a named claim and the C0862 vacancy).
- **Vocabularies:** `commander_on_date_source` and `commander_on_date_basis` added to `schema/vocabularies.json` (61 to 63). The live counts block in `docs/review/README.md` was refreshed to match.
- **Counts in this build:** 2,572 claims filled from the claim itself, 5,801 from a covering tenure (5,413 of those flagged `inferred_*`), 4,397 left blank. 620 of 696 tenures have `valid_from_basis` `claim_date` or `inferred`.

## 24 November 2026 — rc1 documentation review fixes (branch `rc1-docs-fixes`, from main `eb96edd8`)

Docs-only follow-up to the v1.0.0-rc1 first-user review. No claim, unit, commander or operation row was changed.

- Leftover MIT and dual-licence wording removed from `docs/reuse_and_attribution.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `HANDOFF.md`. The whole repository remains CC BY-SA 4.0.
- Coverage and citation wording now state the surveyed Western Front focus (6 June 1944 to 8 May 1945) and the actual claim-date span in the files (16 September 1939 to 31 May 1945). `CITATION.cff` title and the `build.py` fallback used in `build/manifest.json` say 1944–1945.
- Front-page README: claim-vs-unit counts clarified; `scope` filter described as it actually works (`theater` is the Western Front filter; every unit in this release is `in_scope`); a ready-to-paste citation, a commanders join example, and limitations for operation participation and claim `commander` were added.
- Reuse-guide family counts refreshed from `data/references.csv` (2,215 references on 24 November 2026). `docs/json_fields.md` strength fill count updated (39 of 12,770).
- `HANDOFF.md` labelled maintainer-only and kept off the front page. `add101.py` moved to `maintainer/`. Personal `C:\Users\scott\...` paths removed from the WebUI docs. WebUI `package.json` version and licence aligned with 1.0.0-rc1 / CC BY-SA 4.0.

- C0184 (21st Panzer, 28 June): old value `"Panzer IV"`, new value `panzer_iv`.

## 24 November 2026 — British infantry and armoured War Establishment templates (branch `british-toe`, from main `f57fc630`)

Scott chose to start the British TO&E follow-up from the free sources already in hand (24 November 2026). No official British Personnel Staff Table or verified Joslen page was available; figures are taken only from the sourced pages, disagreements are recorded rather than silently preferred, and unsourced keys (including British armoured personnel) are left blank. No claim or command-relation row was changed.

- **References:** `R2220` AHQ Report No. 57 (DHH, 22 December 1952), official Canadian authorized compositions as at 31 May 1945 and confirmation that Canadian formations used British war establishments; `R2221` Nafziger 939BXIA (facts only, citing Joslen) for the 1944/5 infantry division; `R2222` Nafziger 939BXAA (facts only, citing Joslen) for the March 1944 armoured division, Organization No. VII; `R2223` Polish Institute and Sikorski Museum file A.XII.1/48 E, reorganization of the 1st Polish Armoured Division onto the new-type British pattern, understood complete by 1 November 1943. Ellis, *Victory in the West*, vol. I, Appendix IV Part II remains `R670` for structure.
- **Templates:** `TT0014` British Infantry Division, 1944/5 War Establishment — personnel 18,347, 72 artillery pieces (25-pdrs), 110 anti-tank guns (78 6-pdr + 32 17-pdr), three brigades and nine battalions. `TT0015` British Armoured Division, March 1944 — 246 medium (cruiser) tanks, 48 artillery pieces, 54 anti-tank guns, 24 tank destroyers (17-pdr M10s), one infantry brigade of three battalions; **personnel left blank** because Nafziger prints none and the circulating 14,964 figure has not been verified. Inferred `valid_from` dates are annotated: 1944-01-01 (old value blank, reason: first day of the year in Nafziger’s “1944/5” heading) and 1944-03-01 (old value blank, reason: first day of the named month).
- **Assignments (TE10):** 19 `unit_toe` rows, `UT0108`–`UT0126`. Ten British infantry divisions on `TT0014` at confidence 0.3; the 50th ends 15 December 1944 and the 59th 18 October 1944 (Nafziger/Joslen dates, annotated); the 52nd is conformance `unknown` because of its mountain and airlanding training. Three Canadian infantry and two Canadian armoured divisions point at the British templates with conformance `modified`, because AHQ 57’s official 31 May 1945 totals (18,075 / 18,093 infantry; 14,579 / 14,781 armoured) disagree with 18,347 and fill a personnel total the British armoured template leaves blank. Guards, 7th and 11th Armoured, and 1st Polish Armoured, are on `TT0015` from 1944-03-01; the Polish row starts on the March 1944 edition rather than 1 November 1943, so those equipment figures are not backdated (old value 1943-11-01, new value 1944-03-01, reason annotated in the row). The 79th Armoured Division and both airborne divisions remain unassigned.
- **Tests and follow-ups:** scenario 352 narrowed to ships and air; scenarios 354–356. Roadmap 425’s British/Canadian/Polish bullet is partly satisfied; remaining official-table work is roadmap 426 (Joslen verification, TNA WO 24 staff tables, airborne personnel).

## 24 November 2026 — Authorized TO&E templates and unit assignments (branch `toe-templates`, from main `a3afddd7`)

Scott approved the Task 3 proposal (TE1–TE16, 24 November 2026, "Please proceed") as the third of the four-phase v1.0 public-release plan. No claim or command-relation row was changed.

- **Schema (TE1, TE2, TE4, TE11, TE13):** new `data/toe_templates.csv` (`TT0001` onward) and `data/unit_toe.csv` (`UT0001` onward), with Frictionless schemas, `schema/json/authorized_strength_json.schema.json`, and vocabularies `formation_type`, `authorized_count_key` (including `tanks`), `authorized_structure_key` and `toe_conformance`. `open` was added to `relation_end_basis` for a blank template or assignment `valid_to` (it is not used on command relations). No type column was added to `units.csv`.
- **Templates (TE3, TE7, TE12):** 13 edition rows, seeded only from official public-domain sources verified in this pass: Wilson, *Maneuver and Firepower*, CMH Pub 60-14 (`R2218`) for US infantry 15 July 1943 (14,253) and January 1945 (14,037), US armored 15 September 1943 (10,937 men, 263 tanks) and the 1942 configuration retained by the 2d and 3d Armored Divisions (14,630 men, 360 tanks) plus January 1945 (10,700), and US airborne T/O 71 of 15 October 1942 (8,505) and the 16 December 1944 tables (12,979); TM-E 30-451, 15 March 1945, Chapter II (`R2219`) for German infantry 1944 Type (12,352), Old Type (17,200), Volksgrenadier (10,072), army panzer (13,725), army panzergrenadier (13,876) and Fallschirmjäger (15,976). A key the official table does not give is left blank (no invented artillery-piece counts; the TM-E “about 200 tanks” planned 1943 total is not applied to the 13,725 figure). Template `valid_to` is left open even when a later edition exists, so a unit not sourced as reorganized can remain on the older table. British, Canadian and Polish War Establishments, French and Waffen-SS tables, unique organizations (Panzer Lehr, 21st Panzer, von Clausewitz, Erdmann, 79th Armoured, 1st Airborne Task Force) and air establishments are not in this seed (roadmap 425).
- **Assignments (TE8, TE11, TE16):** 107 `unit_toe` rows covering 104 units. US infantry divisions (42) are on the 15 July 1943 table from that edition date, or from the unit `formed_date` when later; the 13 light armored divisions are on the 15 September 1943 table and the 2d and 3d on the 1942 configuration; the 17th, 82d and 101st Airborne are on T/O 71 until 28 February 1945 and on the 12,979 table from 1 March 1945 (Wilson dates the ETO reorganization to March 1945; inferred first-of-month, with old/new/reason in the notes). 30 Volksgrenadier divisions are on the TM-E VG type from the unit `formed_date` or lineage date, not before September 1944. Standard army panzer (2d, 9th, 11th, 116th), the three army panzergrenadier divisions, and seven numbered Fallschirmjäger divisions (not Erdmann) are attached only from the TM-E handbook date 15 March 1945, because earlier German editions differed and a March 1945 handbook total is not applied to D-Day. Confidence is 0.5 where Wilson or a day-level formed/lineage date supports the edition, and 0.3 for month-level or handbook-only attachments. Inferred dates are annotated in the row note and in this entry: 1942-01-01 for the undated 1942 armored configuration; 1945-01-01 for Wilson’s “January 1945” tables (no day given; no assignments); 1944-05-01 for the May 1944 redesignation of the German infantry 1944 type (no assignments); 1944-09-01 for the VG type; 1945-03-01 / 1945-02-28 for the airborne ETO reorganization; and first-of-month where a formed_date is `YYYY-MM`.
- **Build and OOB (TE6, TE14):** `build/toe_templates.csv` and `build/unit_toe.csv` (joined) in the unified `build/` folder. Flagship OOB snapshots gain `authorized_template_id`, `authorized_template_name`, `authorized_personnel` and `authorized_strength_json`, kept separate from `strength_json` and never inherited from a parent. `data/references.csv` gains `toe_count`.
- **Tests and follow-ups:** scenarios 348–353. Roadmap 425.

## 24 November 2026 — Operations places, participation and generated OOBs (branch `operations-oob`, from main `0a88652f`)

Scott approved the Task 2 proposal (OB1–OB16, 24 November 2026, "Approved") as the second of the four-phase v1.0 public-release plan. No claim or command-relation row was changed.

- **Schema (OB2, OB3):** optional `primary_place_id` on `data/operations.csv` (FK to `data/places.csv`); new `data/operation_places.csv` with composite key `(operation_id, place_id)` and vocabulary `operation_place_role` (`primary`, `secondary`, `namesake`, `landing_area`, `objective`, `representative`). No new id series. The validator requires a pin and its `role=primary` row to match, and requires `reference_ids` on every place row.
- **Seeded pins (OB6):** `primary_place_id` was blank on every operation; it is now set on 18 namesake or objective rows, each citing the operation’s existing `reference_ids` and a place that already appears among that operation’s preferred claims: `OP-CHERBOURG` `PL0089`, `OP-CARENTAN` `PL0067`, `OP-BREST` `PL0045`, `OP-MORTAIN` `PL0236`, `OP-PARIS` `PL0271`, `OP-AACHEN` `PL0001`, `OP-METZ` `PL0224`, `OP-HUERTGEN` `PL0586`, `OP-BASTOGNE` `PL0031`, `OP-REMAGEN` `PL0422` (Ludendorff Bridge, Remagen; there is no place row named only Remagen), `OP-NUREMBERG` `PL0476`, `OP-COLMAR-POCKET` `PL0403`, `OP-WELLHIT` `PL0677`, `OP-UNDERGO` `PL0678`, `OP-ASTONIA` `PL0169`, `OP-CHARNWOOD` `PL0057`, `OP-RUHR-POCKET` `PL0640`, `OP-ELEPHANT` `PL0715`. 35 `operation_places` rows in all. Market Garden (Arnhem, Nijmegen, Eindhoven, Oosterbeek, Veghel), Neptune’s five beaches (`landing_area`), the Scheldt (Antwerp, Walcheren, South Beveland, Breskens, Woensdrecht) and Falaise (`namesake` `PL0674` and `representative` `PL0510`) have several places and **no** primary pin — the modal claim location is not used as a pin (Falaise’s busiest preferred claims are at Trun and Saint-Lambert, not Falaise). Each changed operation note records old value, new value and reason.
- **Build counts (OB1, OB4, OB5, OB7):** `build/operations.csv` claim counts are now all-domain, with preferred and ground/air/naval breakdowns, mission counts, unit counts, the sourced pin, and a derived extent (median of preferred coordinates after dropping headquarters rows and points 200 km from the first median; `extent_quality` `focal` / `compact` / `broad` / `none`). Centroids and `build/operations.geojson` Point geometry are published only for `focal` and `compact` operations. Earlier published `claims_direct` figures counted ground claims only (Neptune was 62; it is now 2,049). `build/operation_units.csv` is derived from claims and missions (direct vs `rolled_only`, `most_specific_op_type`); there is no sourced participants table and no command-hierarchy roll-up.
- **OOB exporter (OB9–OB15):** `scripts/export_oob.py` and flagship snapshots in `build/oob/` for 6 June, 18 July, 15 August and 16 December 1944, and 24 March and 7 May 1945 (JSON, CSV, ground Markdown, 14-day located CSV), regenerated on every build. The primary parent reuses `who_controls.py`; additional covering parents are listed (no task-group nesting exception); the 90-day possible carry-forward is unchanged; a unit’s location is its nearest preferred claim (ties prefer on or before the date) and is never inherited from a parent headquarters. Placeholders are included and carry `record_status`. Side uses `allegiance.Resolver`. See `docs/oob_exports.md`.
- **Tests and docs:** semantic scenarios 341–347; scenario 308 updated so a change in the mission table is also expected to refresh `build/operations.csv`, `build/operations.geojson` and `build/operation_units.csv` (missions still never reach claims, command relations, the who_controls grid, or the flagship OOB snapshots); `schema/README.md`, `docs/methodology.md`, `docs/oob_exports.md`, this changelog, `docs/HANDOFF.md`. Follow-ups in roadmap 424.
- **Next free ids:** unchanged (`C12783`, `CR3742`, `PL4897`, `R2218`, `G319`, `PE0608`, `UC0697`, `SC220`, `AT143`, `UL028`, `MSN0099`); next scenario **348**, next roadmap **425**.

## 23 November 2026 — Commanders table, Phase 1 (branch `commanders-table`, from main `6e497077`)

Scott approved the commanders-table proposal (CM1-CM13, 23 November 2026, "I'm good with this") as Task 1 of the four-phase v1.0 public-release plan. New tables seed every already-named `commander` cell (2,572 claims) plus the approved C0862 vacancy end; claim `commander` cells are not rewritten (CM2). Unified `build/` exports include all domains, with a `domain` column (Scott, 23 November 2026: fold the domains into unified build exports).
- **Tables and IDs (CM1, CM4, CM11):** `data/people.csv` (`PE0001`-`PE0607`, 607 people), `data/unit_commanders.csv` (`UC0001`-`UC0696`, 696 tenures), `data/unit_commander_claims.csv` (2,610 links: `asserts_start` / `asserts_end` / `observed_during`). Optional `nationality` when clear; no birth or death dates in Phase 1.
- **Vocabularies:** `commander_role` (`commander`, `acting_commander`, `temporary_commander`, `deputy_commander`, `embarked_commander`), `name_completeness` (`full`, `surname_only`, `incomplete`), `commander_claim_role`.
- **Date model (CM3):** same interval columns as `command_relations.csv`. A name on date X without appointment or relief language is known-in-command (`claim_date`), not a take-command date; an unsourced succession uses `inferred_from_next_claim` + `change_undated` and never invents an end from the next officer's first sighting alone.
- **Conflicts (CM7):** existing `G###` series; new **G318** (Funck preferred from noon 21 August, C2202, vs Eberbach alternate on C0725/C0726). G001 (Dollmann death date), G027 (Schlemm/Blumentritt March 1945 dates), and G003/G004 (LXXXIV Corps Fahrmbacher/Choltitz/Marcks) are modeled on the tenures.
- **Build (CM10, CM12, CM13):** `data/references.csv` gains `commanders_count`; unified `build/people.csv` and `build/unit_commanders.csv` (all domains and all statuses, with `conflict_group_id` visible); `commander_person_id` on `build/all_claims.csv`, `build/all_claims.json`, and `build/other_domains/claims.csv` (`PE####` joined with `;` in id order when a claim links more than one person); both `commander` and `commander_person_id` on `build/claims.geojson`.
- **Follow-ups:** roadmap 423 (note-only commanders, surname-only completions, and related checks). Next free: `PE0608`, `UC0697`, `G319`, scenario 341, roadmap 424.

## 23 November 2026 — FMS B-597 (Pickert, III. Flakkorps) (branch `fms-b597`, from main `c6d3ac90`)

Scott accepted all sixteen B-597 recommendations (Q1-Q16, 23 November 2026, "I'm good with them"). B-597 is the German original of Pickert's 1947 manuscript on III. Flakkorps (May to 14 September 1944) with Pemsel's comment (typed "Hemsel") and four Anlagen, and a copy of the corps' wartime report of 20 September 1944, on Fold3 (NARA M1035, fiche 0587G). Private reading notes: `sources/FMS_B-597_notes.md` (not committed).
- **References (Q1):** `R2216` (the 1947 manuscript, comment and Anlagen; Fold3 image 160237235, pages 51-102) and `R2217` (the 20 September 1944 Erfahrungsbericht; image 160237287, pages 103-124), both `fms_german_manuscript`, one family (same author and headquarters; neither raises the other or another FMS row). Fiche 0587G was read; the next-fiche target of B-596 names fiche 0574, noted in the citation.
- **Places:** `PL4895` Meaux, Seine-et-Marne (48.9603, 2.8883) and `PL4896` Baron-sur-Odon, Calvados (49.1286, -0.4825), 3 km, `R001` (English Wikipedia article coordinates through the API).
- **New claims (Q4-Q7, Q11), all 0.3, preferred, no conflict group, parent blank (old value none, new value the claim, reason in each note):** `C12775` III. Flakkorps headquarters east of Meaux, 5 June 1944 (10 km; disagrees with `C11837` Paris on 1 June, no group, Q4); `C12776` the corps through the Paris area on the march, 7 June (vicinity, 10 km, transit); `C12777` arrival west and south-west of Caen, 8 June (10 km); `C12778` forward command post about 5 km north-east of Thury-Harcourt, 19 July (10 km); `C12779` main body east and south-east of Caen, 19 July (10 km); `C12780` the Seine crossing at Rouen, 24 August (10 km); `C12781` Flak-Sturm-Regiment 1 west of Bayeux, 6 June (25 km: a written exception to G9's 10 km so that the precision takes in the Isigny sketch and the comment, Q7); `C12782` I SS Panzer Corps headquarters at Baron-sur-Odon, about 9 June 1944 (3 km, approximate date, Q11). `C12778` and `C12779` keep Pickert's date and note that Goodwood opened on 18 July 1944 (Q6).
- **Raised (corroboration rule):** `C11823` (Luftgaukommando Westfrankreich, Étampes, 1 June 1944): confidence old value 0.5, new value 0.7; reference_ids old value `R1925;R004;R1855;R001`, new value `R1925;R004;R1855;R2216;R001`; reason: B-597 ms -6- (Gef.Stand Étampes, to 5 June 1944) is a second family agreeing with Holm (Q2). `C11838` (III. Flakkorps, Évrecy, 9 June 1944): confidence old value 0.3, new value 0.5; location_qualifier old value blank, new value `just east of`; reference_ids old value `R1937;R001`, new value `R1937;R2216;R001`; reason: B-597 ms -11- and Anlage 3 is the first counted family (German Wikipedia is not a family) and gives the day (Q3).
- **Cited, confidence unchanged (Q2):** `C8332` (Luftflotte 3, Paris, 6 June; 0.7; reference_ids old `R845;R1855;R002`, new `R845;R1855;R2216;R002`; same FMS family as B-283), `C0059` (Panzer Group West, 9 June; 0.7; old `R141;R449;R001`, new `R141;R449;R2216;R001`), `C0068` (Panzer Group West, La Caine, 10 June; 0.5; old `R133;R077;R761;R002`, new `R133;R077;R761;R2216;R002`; undated in B-597 and same family as B-466), `C11839` (III. Flakkorps, Caen, 18 June; 0.3; old `R670;R001`, new `R670;R2216;R001`; no date agreement). Each row's source and source_locator gain the R2216 link and locator (old and new values in the notes).
- **Disagreement notes, no value changed:** `C11837` (Paris against east of Meaux, Q4), `C11840` (Cochem against Traben-Trarbach about 10 September 1944, L8 keeps Cochem, Q10), `C11841`-`C11843` (Bayeux on 24 June against west of Bayeux at the start of the invasion and Bayeux British from 7 June, Q8; roadmap 422).
- **Relations (Q12, Q13):** no new relation (B-597: cooperation, not subordination, so `supporting` stays). 13 evidence links: `CR2868` (`C12775`, `C12776` observed_during), `CR2869` (`C12778`, `C12779` observed_during), `CR2870` (`C12780` observed_during), `CR2871` (`C12781` observed_during; `C12779` listed_by_higher_unit), `CR2872`-`CR2874` (`C12777` and `C12779` listed_by_higher_unit; `C12775` is not linked to `CR2873` because 5 June is before its valid_from). `CR2869` ordered_date old value blank, new value 1944-06-06 (the order received on the evening of 6 June, ms -8-); valid_from stays 1944-06-09; annotated in the note.
- **Unit notes (Q9, Q14):** `GER-FLAKK-003C` (the sentence "FMS B-597 ... has not been read (open question)" replaced, old value quoted in the note: Pickert from about 24 May against Holm's 28 May; command post east of Meaux; Anlage 1 corps troops, Ln.Abt., the three Flakkampfgruppen from about 20 June; comment author probably Pemsel); `GER-FLAKSR-001` to `-004` (Sturm title shortly before the invasion; Anlage 1 three Abteilungen against Holm; regiment 1 detached west of Bayeux and back several weeks later; regiments 2-4 at the Somme mouth stay placeholders under G9). Old text kept; B-597 text appended.

- **Docs:** roadmap 414 (B-597 open item closed), new roadmap 422 (Bayeux 24 June recheck, 19 or 18 July, light 90 and 95, Sainte-Honorine-du-Fay date, Traben-Trarbach exit, the speed warning); `docs/HANDOFF.md` row; `docs/normandy_air_naval_plan.md` entry notes. ## 19 November 2026 — Luftwaffe ground G-b follow-up: Bayeux as an area, Flak-Regiment 22 and 141 pages (branch `normandy-lw-ground-b`)

Scott accepted all eight G-b recommendations (19 November 2026). Two of them change data on this branch.

- **Q5, claims `C11842` and `C11843` changed:** 266 and 497 re-formed at Bayeux on 24 June 1944. Confidence: old value 0.5, new value 0.3. `precision_km`: old value 5, new value 10. `location_basis`: old value `documented_on_date`, new value `operational_area`. Reason: Bayeux was in Allied hands from 7 June 1944, so Holm's "Bayeux" is read as the Bayeux area, not the town (G9: one named town at 10 km, 0.3). The notes on both rows carry the old and new values. Flak-Sturm-Regiment 1 at Bayeux (`C11841`, inferred, 0.3) changed in a second follow-up commit: `precision_km` old value 5, new value 10; reason: to match its battalions 266 and 497 above, because Bayeux was in Allied hands from 7 June 1944 (Scott agreed, 19 November 2026). Its `location_basis` stays `inferred`, not `operational_area`: the staff's place is inferred from its battalions, and `inferred` is the weaker basis.
- **Q3, Holm's Flak-Regiment 22 and Flak-Regiment 141 pages read:** these are new references `R1950` and `R1951`. Flak-Regiment 141 is the regiment whose only battalion is I./141 (formed 26 August 1939 at Lüdenscheid). It is not gemischte Flak-Abteilung 141, which became I./Flak-Regiment 46 in December 1941. Each page gives one town in June 1944, so both battalions leave placeholder status:
  - `GER-FLAKA-022-2`: `record_status` old value `placeholder`, new value `active`. `unit_name` old value "II./Flak-Regiment 22 (Flak battalion)", new value "II./Flak-Regiment 22 (mixed Flak battalion)", because Holm has it mixed from 15 November 1938. `unit_note` rewritten from the page, with the old value and the reason in the note.
  - `GER-FLAKA-141-1`: `record_status` old value `placeholder`, new value `active`. `unit_note` rewritten in the same way.
  - **Claims `C11850`-`C11851` (2, both 0.3):** II./22 at Arras in June 1944, joining Flak-Sturm-Regiment 3 as its second battalion. I./141 at Amiens in June 1944, joining Flak-Sturm-Regiment 4. Holm gives only the month, so both are dated 1 June, as with the other G-b battalions. The Sturm regiment pages (`R1940`, `R1941`) are cited as relation evidence. Holm's own 1 June 1944 rows for the two battalions (under 16. Flak-Division and 18. Flak-Brigade) are noted on the claims.
  - **Relations `CR2884`-`CR2885` (2):** II./22 to Flak-Sturm-Regiment 3 and I./141 to Flak-Sturm-Regiment 4, both `attached`. Each runs from 6 June 1944 (R004, `assignment_table`) to 30 September 1944 (the corps exit, inferred), the same pattern as the other battalions.
- **Placeholders:** six remain. They are Flak-Sturm-Regiment 2-4, light 80, I./35 and light 98; their regiment or battalion pages give no single town and day in the window.
- **Tests:** scenario 322 updated. It now expects 11 active and 6 placeholders, confidence 0.3 only on `C11837`-`C11851`, and the two new battalion relations. It also gets two new checks, one for Q5 and one for Q3.
- **Docs:** this entry; roadmap 414 (the G-b follow-up; open items now light 90 and 95, B-597, the February-March 1944 corps parent); `docs/normandy_air_naval_plan.md` G-b entry notes.
- Next free: `C11852`, `CR2886`, `R1952`, `PL4626`, `G267`, `SC220`, `AT143`, `UL027`, `MSN0099`, scenario 323, roadmap 415.

Old value none, new value these rows; reason: Scott approved recommendations E1-E11 (16 November 2026). No new class rows: Bangors use existing SC121, Algerines SC120, Halcyons SC122, Hunt 1916 ships of the 4th use existing SC216, and the 40th (Catherine / Auk, including Magic and Pylades) uses existing SC054 (decision E11). Flotilla units remain placeholders without their own claims. MMS, BYMS, trawlers and other small craft stay in chunk 3. Italy is unchanged (decision E8).
- **Nationality (decision E10):** Recruit and Rifleman are entered as Royal Navy ships (`UK-AM-RECRUIT`, `UK-AM-RIFLEMAN`). Rifleman has a Royal Navy ship page describing Operation Neptune with her flotilla. Recruit has no individual page and appears only as HMS on the Algerine-class list. Plucky's possible SANF(V) commanding officer is not treated as the ship's nationality. Guysborough is entered as `CAN-AM-GUYSBOROUGH` (HMCS): the Wikipedia title is HMS Guysborough, but the page says she was loaned to the RCN, commissioned on 22 April 1942, and served in the 14th Minesweeping Flotilla in June 1944. The other 14th and all 31st Canadian Bangors are HMCS. The 16th flotilla ships, though some were built in Canada, are HMS on the class list and are entered as UK. No `south_africa` claims folder was created.
- **Claims `C9719`-`C9829` (111):** a 6 June claim for each of the 89 assault-list ships (Elgin's 6 June Omaha row is held at 0.3 because Wikipedia records severe mine damage on 4 May 1944 and does not mention Normandy); a 4 May sea-position damage claim for Elgin; 25 June Cherbourg-outer-defences claims for the eight ships of the 9th Minesweeping Flotilla; loss or damage claims for Persian (23 June), Friendship (5 July), Cato (6 July), Magic (6 July, her only claim), Pylades (8 July, two claims), Vestal (10 August), Loyalty (22 August), Gleaner (25 August), Britomart, Hussar and Salamander (27 August, Salamander damaged beyond repair), and a non-loss 27 August claim for Jason, who was present off Cap d'Antifer but is not named as hit. Magic and Pylades have no invented 6 June assault claim.

The eight ships of the 9th also have a 25 June attached relation to `US-TG-129` for the Cherbourg bombardment clearance sweep (attached, not assigned, so it does not contradict the standing Force J assignment). Magic and Pylades have no flotilla or Force S relation, because they are not on the A(1) 40th list and no page names a flotilla.
- **Places `PL4194`-`PL4195`:** hand-worked sea positions for Elgin (nine nautical miles east of Portland Bill) and for Loyalty (50°09′N 00°41′W). The 27 August RAF strike uses existing `PL1467` (La Poterie-Cap-d'Antifer) as the operational area; NHB's "Seine Bay" is treated as the coarser official wording, not as a second place. Cherbourg sweeping uses existing `PL0091` (Cherbourg outer defences), not the 1 km city point.

## 15 November 2026 — allegiance follow-up (branch `allegiance-followup`, stacked on PR #97 and #96; roadmap 384, Scott t415u)

Three parts, one commit each. The parts are listed below, newest first.

- **Part 3, `alliance` column retired.** Consumers found by search of scripts, validator, tests, docs, the build outputs and the grid tool (`/workspace/UnitLocationData-tools`, no use): (1) `scripts/unit_refs.py`, the opponent check of `engaged_with` (compared the two nations' `alliance` values); (2) `scripts/validate.py`, the header, the vocabulary and the not-empty checks of the nationalities table and two docstrings; (3) `schema/vocabularies.json` vocabulary `alliance`; (4) semantic scenario 273's expectation; (5) docs: `schema/README.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/review/README.md` (regenerated), `scripts/common.py` and the historic `scripts/migrate_normalize.py` (comment only; the one-off migration is not re-run). No build output, claim file or the grid used it. **Replaced by** `allegiance.Resolver` (unit override, then nation allegiance on that date, then blank): the `engaged_with` check now asks whether the two units are on the same camp (Allied and co-belligerent against Axis; neutral, a gap in the table or a blank date is not checked; a month or year is checked at both ends and counts only when both agree) **on the claim date**, where it compared one value per nation for the whole war. **Old values, removed with the column (old value, new value, reason: the single value cannot say that a nation changed sides; the dated table and the overrides replace it):** `ALL` Allied, `AUS` Allied, `BEL` Allied, `CAN` Allied, `CZ` Allied, `FR` Allied, `GER` Axis, `IT` Axis (provisional), `NL` Allied, `NOR` Allied, `NZ` Allied, `POL` Allied, `RSI` Axis, `SAF` Allied, `UK` Allied, `US` Allied; new value: no column (the sides on a date come from `data/nation_allegiance.csv`; `ALL` has none, being a combined headquarters). The vocabulary `alliance` is removed. `nationalities.csv` now has the columns `code, name, adjective, alt_adjectives, kind, note`. Difference to know: the old check treated `ALL` as Allied; `ALL` now has no side, so an `ALL` unit is never flagged. **Answer changes: none** (validate: 0 errors on the same 9,450 claims; grid compare in the PR comment). Scenarios 273 and 274 test the resolver and the check (1,863 expectations).
- **Part 2, unit-level overrides.** New `data/unit_allegiance_overrides.csv` (`unit_id`, `side`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `reference_ids`, `note`; schema `schema/unit_allegiance_overrides.schema.json`; side vocabulary `allegiance_side` reused), **header only**: no unit of the dataset has a recorded side different from its nation's. Checks in `scripts/allegiance.py` (`check_overrides`, called by `validate.py`): unit exists, side valid, real dates inside WW2, no overlap per unit, references exist, sorted. New `allegiance.Resolver` (override, then nation allegiance, then blank; `camp` folds co-belligerent into Allied and neutral into none). Scenario 274. **Candidates left for Scott (none entered, no source of the dataset gives a side different from the nation's):** `GER-SSGR-030D` (30th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS (Russian No. 2), nationality Germany, mutinied September 1944 per CMH; still German side, an override is needed only if part of it is recorded changing sides) and `GER-SSGR-034D` (34th SS Volunteer Grenadier Division Landstorm Nederland, Dutch collaborationists on the German side, same side as Germany so no override); Ost battalions, the Indian Legion and other foreign volunteers serving with the German forces have no unit record yet.

The two `IT` rows no longer say "no code yet". The split between `IT` and `RSI` is written in the note of `IT`: `IT` is the King's forces (Axis to 8 September 1943, co-belligerent from 13 October 1943), `RSI` the Social Republic's own army, navy, air force and party and police formations; a formation on both sides keeps its `IT` record to 8 September 1943 and gets an `RSI` re-formation with a lineage link (a convention for Scott to confirm). **No existing unit was reassigned: the dataset names no RSI unit** (a search of the unit table and claim files for the Social Republic, Monterosa, San Marco, Decima, Littorio, the Black Brigades and the like found none; the other "Italian" mentions are the Franco-Italian border). ## 14 November 2026 — Parent division answers for two Kampfgruppen (branch `kg-division-answer`, from `main` `1298290c`)

Scott decided (14 November 2026) that `GER-KG-MEYER` and `GER-KG-002PZ`, and only those two, answer `who_controls` with their parent division, not with the corps link. A per-unit decision, not a change of the general rule (the organic fallback of the earlier entry below is unchanged for every other unit).

- **Old value.** `GER-KG-MEYER` on 6 June 1944 and later answered with `CR0026` (`reserve` to `GER-COR-084C`, LXXXIV Corps) and an empty operational chain; `GER-KG-002PZ` from 27 June 1944 answered with `CR0017` (`unknown` to `GER-PZ-047C`, XLVII Panzer Corps) and an empty chain. Both explicit non-organic relations blocked the organic fallback.
- **New value.** `GER-KG-MEYER` answers with `CR0027` (organic to `GER-INF-352D`, `organic_fallback`) and the chain goes on up (LXXXIV Corps, Seventh Army, Army Group B, OB West); `GER-KG-002PZ` answers with `CR0016` (organic to `GER-PZ-002D`, `organic_fallback`) and the chain goes on up (XLVII Panzer Corps, Panzer Group West). The corps relations are printed as a `note:` saying they were set aside.
- **Reason.** Scott decision 2026-11-14: the parent division answers for these Kampfgruppen. For `CR0017` the source lists the corps with the parent division without saying how it relates to the Kampfgruppe; for `CR0026` the source lists the Kampfgruppe as corps reserve, which stays in the data as sourced.
- **Mechanism (data-driven, matches the table conventions).** New table `data/who_controls_overrides.csv` (columns `relation_id`, `effect`, `decided_by`, `decided_on`, `old_value`, `new_value`, `reason`) with two rows, effect `defer_to_organic_parent` (new vocabulary `who_controls_override_effect`); registered in `schema/relations.schema.json` as `command_relation_overrides` (primary key `relation_id`, foreign key to `command_relations`); `scripts/command_relations.py` loads it; `scripts/validate.py` checks the header and values, sorted and unique rows, that each relation is preferred and non-organic and that its subject has a preferred organic relation; `scripts/build.py` copies it to `build/who_controls_overrides.csv`; `scripts/who_controls.py` skips a listed relation when it answers for the relation's subject (so any other non-organic relation that covers the date still wins) and prints the note. Chosen over a new column on `command_relations.csv` because it changes no existing table, header or derived file, keeps the decision with its old value, new value and reason in one place, and cannot be applied by accident to other rows.
- **Kept as data.** `CR0017` and `CR0026` are unchanged rows in `data/command_relations.csv` and `build/command_relations.csv`; only their `note` gained a `Review:` annotation (old value, new value, reason). The 90-day rule of scenarios 260 and 261 still reads the reserve relation as before; the organic relations `CR0027` (last listed 6 June 1944) and `CR0016` (27 June 1944) follow the same 90-day cutoff, so each answer now ends 90 days after its listing.
- **Checks.** Scenario 268; the Kampfgruppe Meyer expectation of scenario 266 (reserve line kept, empty chain) is replaced, because it is the case Scott decided otherwise (no other expectation changed). Roadmap 382.
- **HANDOFF rule 24 added:** private source reading notes are stored only in the Drive folder `WWII Unit Locations/source notes` (folder id later moved to `docs/HANDOFF_private.md`), one file per source named `<source>_notes.md` in the uppercase canonical form, never committed.

## 14 November 2026 — End of CR1282, US XXI Corps under the French First Army (branch `cr1282-end`, from `main` `69fdf0e8`)

Scott approved settling the end of `CR1282` (US XXI Corps, `operational_control` under the French First Army from 23 January 1945), left open on 13 November (`small-fixes-1113`) because no source read then dated it.

- **`CR1282` end date.** Old value: `valid_to` blank, `valid_to_basis` `open_at_last_claim`, `end_unknown` true. New value: `valid_to` 1945-02-16, `valid_to_earliest` 1945-02-15, `valid_to_basis` `narrative`, `end_unknown` false. No end hour is documented. Reason: the Sixth Army Group G-3 Section Final Report (`R453`, p. 43, a primary report; PDF copy at trailblazersww2.org, which the dataset already used) says: "Regrouping of 6th Army Group commenced 15 February when 75th and 79th Infantry Divisions were released. XXI Corps reverted to control of Seventh Army and was given a sector on the left." It gives no separate day for the reversion, so 15 February is the earliest. Three secondary web sources give 16 February: Wikipedia (`R160`), the trailblazersww2.org XXI Corps history (`R1166`, new) and the bigpigeon.us ETO unit subordination page (`R1167`, new); they probably share one origin and count as one weaker family. The last day of the relation is therefore 15 or 16 February: certain through 15 February, possible on 16 February, and neither day is chosen. The official history (`R425`, Riviera to the Rhine ch. 29: "by the end of February ... returned north") and de Lattre (`R686`) give no day and do not contradict the range. The `CR1282` note was updated with old value, new value and reason (its earlier last sentence, "end left open until ...", is marked superseded).
- **New claim `C9452`** (US XXI Corps, 18 February 1945, Morhange, `PL2253`, existing place, confidence 0.3, event `hq_move`). Why: the validator requires a linked claim that states a relation's end (`CR1282` link `asserts_end`, `stated_effective_to` 1945-02-16, `stated_effective_to_earliest` 1945-02-15). The XXI Corps history says the corps "returned to Seventh Army control on February 16th and moved to Morhange two days later"; the 18 February day is that statement counted forward, so the row has one weak family for the place (`R1166`), `R453` and `R160` for the reversion, `R1167` as a third secondary witness. **Conflict kept, not resolved:** the 12th Army Group maps of 13 February (`C5746`, near Orschwiller) and 20 February (`C5877`, 0.3, Sainte-Croix-aux-Mines) place the headquarters elsewhere; a map can lag a move, so `C5877` is unchanged. Old value none, new value the row. One new validator warning: the claim lists `FR-ARMY-001A` after its end on purpose (it states the end).
- **No new relation.** The corps had been assigned to the US Seventh Army and the 6th Army Group throughout (`CR0201`, `CR0200`, from 27 December 1944), so the reversion is the end of the operational control, not a new assignment.
- **References.** `R1166` trailblazersww2.org, History: XXI Corps (family `trailblazersww2_org`); `R1167` bigpigeon.us, ETO Unit Subordination (family `bigpigeon_us`, new); both cited by `C9452`.
- **who_controls.** The French First Army line no longer appears for XXI Corps from 17 February 1945 (16 February is `possible`: ends that day at an undocumented hour, end between 15 and 16 February). Before this change the open interval was `possible` as a stale carry-forward and so stayed at the head of the chain until 27 April, and in the chains of divisions under XXI Corps; the Seventh Army (`CR0201`) now heads the chain.
- **Grid** (`wc_grid.py`, which now includes the organic-only units; baseline `grid_organic_subjects.json`, main `69fdf0e8`, versus this branch): 19,890 answers, **26 changed, 0 new keys, no cell changed between answered and unanswered.** By unit: `US-COR-021C` 13 (3 on 29 January to 12 February: French line `possible` to `certain`; 10 on 19 February to 23 April: French line gone, Seventh Army at the head), `US-ARM-012D` 5 (1 on 5 February possible to certain; 4 on 2 to 23 April, French line gone), `US-INF-063D` 4 (26 February to 19 March, French line gone), `US-INF-003D` 2 (29 January and 5 February, possible to certain), `US-INF-004D` 2 (26 March and 2 April, French line gone).

## 14 November 2026 — Organic fallback in who_controls (branch `organic-fallback`, from `main` `53fd242`)

Scott approved a lookup-rule change so that a unit with only an organic relation on a date is answered through its organic parent. Lookup rule only: no claim, relation, unit or place was added or changed.

- **Old behaviour.** `organic` relations are not in `build/command_relations.csv`, so `who_controls` printed "no relationship interval covers ..." (exit 1) for any date on which a unit had no non-organic relation. Example: `US-CCA-002D` from 5 November 1944 (day 91 after the 6 August XIX Corps listing) to VE-Day, although `CR0176` (organic to `US-ARM-002D`, last listed 1 March 1945) covers it.
- **New behaviour.** At any level of the operational chain where **no non-organic relation of any kind** (operational_control, attached, assigned, unspecified_subordination, reserve, administrative_control, unknown with a named higher unit) covers the date, the lookup falls back to the unit's organic parent, read from the new derived file `build/organic_relations.csv` (preferred `organic` relations, same columns and the same `last_listed_date`), and goes on up the chain from that parent as normal (the parent may fall back too). An explicit non-organic relation always wins, even a `possible` stale one: `US-CCA-002D` on 1 August 1944 is still the 29th Division attachment (`CR1313`), and on 20 August the possible XIX Corps relation. The organic relation obeys the same `OPEN_CARRY_FORWARD_DAYS = 90` rule (certain to its last listing, possible for 90 days, then dropped). A fallback answer is marked: the interval line ends `[organic_fallback: no operational, attachment or other non-organic relation covers this date]` and the chain level reads `(organic_fallback, certain|possible)` in place of the relationship. An explicit `unknown` placeholder without a higher unit does not block the fallback and is printed as a `note:` line. Exit code is 0 for a fallback answer.
- **Reason.** An organic parent is a sourced fact; a combat command or Kampfgruppe was in its division's chain of command unless a source says otherwise. The old rule left such units unanswered for the rest of the war off a long-stale listing.
- **Not covered (kept as before, by design).** A unit whose only non-organic relation is a `reserve`, `administrative_control` or an `unknown` with a named higher unit keeps that line and gets no fallback, because that relation is itself a non-organic superior (`GER-KG-MEYER`, corps reserve; `GER-KG-002PZ`, unknown `GER-PZ-047C`). No source-based case was changed to make a test pass.
- **Build.** `scripts/command_relations.py` `derived_rows(..., organic=False)` gained an `organic` switch; `scripts/build.py` writes `build/organic_relations.csv` (35 rows, all domains). `build/command_relations.csv` is unchanged and still excludes `organic`.
- **Unit types affected.** The 35 organic relations belong to 35 subject units: Kampfgruppen and Fallschirmjäger/Volksgrenadier regiments (battle_group), combat commands (`US-CCA-002D`, `US-CCR-004D`), Fallschirmjäger battalions, British brigades (`UK-TNK-031B`, `UK-INF-056B`), Dutch Stoottroepen regiments and battalions, and air groups and a squadron (`GER-JGGR-026-2/3`, `US-FS-390`). In the standard grid only 4 of them are subjects (the others have no non-organic relation, so they are not in the grid): 28 of the 35 produce fallback answers on a weekly check (445 cells).
- **Grid** (`wc_grid.py`, main `53fd242` rebuilt as baseline versus this branch): 18,690 answers, **63 changed, 0 new keys, 0 previously answered cell changed**; all 63 were unanswered before: `US-CCA-002D` 28 (6 November 1944 to 8 May 1945), `UK-INF-056B` 13 (21 August to 13 November 1944), `UK-TNK-031B` 13 (4 September to 27 November 1944), `NL-INF-STBRB-001` 9 (1 January to 26 February 1945). `US-CCA-002D` after 4 November 1944 now resolves through the 2nd Armored Division then XIX Corps (possible), Ninth Army, 12th Army Group, SHAEF. A separate weekly check of all 35 organic subjects (not part of the standard grid) found 445 fallback cells over 28 units, 382 of them for 24 units that are not grid subjects.
- **Checks.** Scenario 266 (23 expectations): fallback applies when nothing else does; an explicit attachment beats it; a possible stale explicit relation beats it; reserve is not overridden; fallback repeats up the chain; 90-day rule on the organic relation; unknown-placeholder note. Roadmap 380.

## 14 November 2026 — Combat Command A, 2nd Armored Division, after 28 July 1944 (branch `small-fixes-1113`)

The unit had only two claims, the last on 28 July 1944 (`C0515`), so the 90-day cutoff left it unanswered from late October 1944. Official histories already in the references (Blumenson, Cole, MacDonald) name CCA after that date. Wikipedia's 2nd Armored Division article was opened and does not name these CCA actions, so each new row has one source family (the US Army official history).

- **New claims `C9447`–`C9451`:** 1 August 1944 at Tessy-sur-Vire, attached to the 29th Division (`C9447`, Breakout-15 p303-304, `R396`); 6 August on Hill 219 west of Vire as XIX Corps reserve (`C9448`, Breakout-23 p449-451, `R1165`, new, and Breakout-24 p471, `R402`); 25 August entering Elbeuf with the division again (`C9449`, Breakout-28 p580, `R405`); 24 December taking Buissonville (`C9450`, Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 18 p440-441, `R388`); 1 March 1945 reaching the outskirts of Krefeld after crossing the Nord Canal (`C9451`, The Last Offensive ch. 9 p174, `R538`). New places `PL4179` (Tessy-sur-Vire) and `PL4180` (Buissonville). Claim `parent_unit_id` is the 29th Division on `C9447` and XIX Corps on `C9448`; later rows leave it blank because the parent is the organic division (`units.csv` and `CR0176`).
- **`CR1313`:** attached to the 29th Infantry Division from 1 August to 6 August 1944. Breakout-15 p304 says CCA reverted to 2d Armored Division control on 2 August when Tessy was secured; the same day Breakout-23 p449 has the 29th, with CCA attached, attacking toward Vire, recorded as a same-day mission change rather than a gap.
- **`CR0177`:** last listed old value 28 July 1944 (`C0515`), new value 6 August 1944 (`C9448`). End still `open_at_last_claim`: the sources show CCA still a separate XIX Corps element on 6 August (the rest of the division left for VII Corps shortly after midnight, 6 August), and they next place CCA with the division at Elbeuf on 25 August, without a reunion day. `C0515` notes were updated to replace the earlier reading that the end of the temporary arrangement was not documented.
- **who_controls:** the 29th attachment is an active relation for 1-6 August, and the XIX Corps listing now runs 90 days from 6 August rather than from 28 July. After the split, later claims are organic only; `organic` is excluded from who_controls, so Elbeuf, Buissonville and Krefeld do not themselves keep an operational chain in the grid. No assigned-to-division relation was invented to close that gap.

Scenario 265; roadmap 379.

## 14 November 2026 — Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten unit and Stoottroepen organic parent (branch `small-fixes-1113`)

Scott approved adding Prince Bernhard's Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten (Netherlands Forces of the Interior) as a unit on this branch, so that the Stoottroepen have a sourced administrative/organic superior after the XXX Corps placement of 18 September 1944 could no longer cover the later claims.

- **Sources (not inference).** NIMH, *De oprichting van de Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten* (`R1163`, new, page opened 14 November 2026): on 31 August 1944 SHAEF authorised the formation of the BS; Prince Bernhard became its commander-in-chief, under Eisenhower; on 5 September 1944 (Dolle Dinsdag) the BS was established by Royal Decree, uniting the LKP, RVV and OD; the organisation was temporary and was dissolved on 8 August 1945. A second family, Dutch Wikipedia, *Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten* (`R1164`, new, opened the same day), also dates the official founding to 5 September 1944 and names Bernhard as commander; it gives the dissolution only as August 1945 and does not name an Allied superior. The veterans' site binnenlandsestrijdkrachten.nl (opened, not given its own id) cites Koninklijk Besluit Staatsblad E62 of 5 September and Bernhard's appointment as Bevelhebber der Nederlandse Strijdkrachten on 3 September. The 22 September split of the BS south of the great rivers into Stoottroepen and Bewakingstroepen, and the early May 1945 London strength return, were already in the dataset from de Jong, deel 10a (`R894`, pp. 561-563, 757-758). NIMH also names the Stoottroepen as the armed branch of the BS (a second family for that component relationship). Lodders and Kraandijk, *Militaire Spectator* 1994 (`R1162`, already in the dataset) remain the source for the later split: Limburg under the Koninklijke landmacht section of Bernhard's staff from 2 January 1945 and into the KL in January; Brabant companies employed by the British from 11 October 1944 and into the KL in May, after which Commando Zuid was abolished.

- **What changed.** New unit `NL-BS-000H` (echelon `other`, following the headquarters-style `000H` ids; `record_status` placeholder, because no opened source names a place for the 5 September decree and a location claim is not invented; `formed_date` 5 September 1944, not 22 September). `parent_unit_id` of the BS is left blank: NIMH's statement that Bernhard was under Eisenhower is not corroborated by the second family, and is not entered as a relation to SHAEF. No headquarters claims are added (London is not a place in the dataset; Brussels and the November 1944 Breda headquarters are described as the Bevelhebber's staff on a single secondary site, without a day). `units.csv` `parent_unit_id` of `NL-INF-STOOT` and `NL-INF-BEWAK` is left blank: a fixed organic parent would have to appear on every claim that already lists a relation, including `C9384` (18 September, still stoottroepen of the OD, parent XXX Corps), which predates the 22 September split. New relations `CR1311` (Stoottroepen, start 22 September 1944 from `C9386`, last listed 1 May 1945 on `C9388`) and `CR1312` (Bewakingstroepen, start 22 September from `C9389`, last listed 1 May on `C9393`) are `administrative_control` to `NL-BS-000H`; both `open_at_last_claim`, no end date invented from the January/May KL transfers or from the 8 August 1945 dissolution of the BS. `organic` was considered, because these are component arms of the BS, but organic relations are excluded from `build/command_relations.csv` and from `who_controls`, which is what this pass is meant to answer; `administrative_control` is the schema class for an administrative superior. HANDOFF describes that class as temporary and ordinarily expecting an end; no end day is invented here. `parent_unit_id` on `C9386` and `C9388` (and on `C9389` and `C9393`) old value: blank; new value: `NL-BS-000H`. `C9385` and `C9387` stay blank (19 September is before the split; the Peel action does not name the BS). `C9384` still lists XXX Corps (`CR1285`); that relation is unchanged and still last listed 18 September. The 2 January 1945 Limburg staff-section transfer is noted on `NL-INF-STOOT-LIM` and is not given a new parent unit.

- **Tests.** Scenario 264 covers the new administrative listing (the Stoottroepen answered under the BS on 18 December 1944 and on VE-Day). Scenario 263 is unchanged: the XXX Corps interval still drops on 18 December. Roadmap 378.

## 14 November 2026 — Stoottroepen post-September 1944 superiors (branch `small-fixes-1113`)

The 90-day stale-possible cutoff left the Stoottroepen (`NL-INF-STOOT`) unanswered from 18 December 1944, because `CR1285` (unspecified subordination to XXX Corps, `open_at_last_claim`) was last listed only on 18 September 1944 (`C9384`), even though the unit has later claims through 1 May 1945 (`C9385`-`C9388`) that had been left with a blank `parent_unit_id`. Unlike the 79th Armoured Division, those later rows are not listings of the same standing Allied assignment.

- **Sources (not inference).** De Jong, *Het Koninkrijk*, deel 10a (`R894`, already on the claims): pp. 542-545 record only the six Eindhoven companies placed at the disposal of XXX Corps on 18 September and accepted by Horrocks; footnote 2 says they "at first" helped cover that corps' flanks and were also used at the end of October at the Peel (`C9387`). P. 556 is van Kooten's Limburg recruitment after Bernhard appointed him, not an XXX Corps listing (`C9385`). Pp. 561-563 is the formal BS organisation of 22 September, with Borghouts commander of the Stoottroepen der BS south of the great rivers (`C9386`). Pp. 757-758 is a London war-department strength return for early May 1945 and names no Allied parent (`C9388`). Bernhard's policy (p. 556) was to place stoottroepen at the disposal of Allied commanders in general; a later passage on 21st Army Group concerns supply to the BS, not operational command of this formation. A second family, Lodders and Kraandijk, "50 jaar regiment Stoottroepen", *Militaire Spectator* 163 (1994) no. 9, pp. 402-411 (`R1162`, new, PDF opened): Commando Limburg, by its direct relationship with the Americans, took increasing distance from Commando Zuid and Brabant (p. 405); the Limburg battalions were employed alongside the Americans from shortly after their formation and came under the Koninklijke landmacht section of Prince Bernhard's staff on 2 January 1945 (p. 406); the English employed Brabant companies as combat units at the front from 11 October 1944, and an English army commander delayed the Brabant transfer into the Koninklijke landmacht until May 1945, after Limburg had transferred in January, at which point Commando Zuid was abolished (pp. 405-409). Other pages were opened and are consistent with that split but are not used to invent a parent: the Nederlands Veteraneninstituut interview article "Onder het commando van het Amerikaanse 9e Leger" (read 14 November 2026) says Commando Brabant was under British command and Commando Limburg under American command, and describes some Limburg elements later serving with US Ninth Army (a veteran's path from mid-January 1945, not a dated assignment of the whole regional command from September); the regimental site stoottroepers.nl (read 14 November 2026) says the Limburg stoottroepers were embedded in the US Army and that the Brabant stoottroepers, like the Zeeland volunteers of 14 Regiment Infanterie, belonged to the British 21st Army Group, without a date range; English Wikipedia names Prince Bernhard's founding order and the 5 May 1945 strength, not an Allied parent. The NIMH article "De Stoottroepen in oktober 1944" at the previously indexed URL returned HTTP 404 on 14 November 2026 (curl and a browser user-agent); it was not opened and is not cited, including search-index quotations that would have named 21st Army Group for the Brabant companies in early October. Stacey, *The Victory Campaign* (`R668`), and the Dutch Defence canon / other NIMH pages already in the dataset (`R1159`, `R1160`) were searched and do not name a later superior for `NL-INF-STOOT`. Netherlands District (`UK-DIST-NETH`) is not attested for this unit.

- **What changed.** `parent_unit_id` on `C9384` old value: blank; new value: `UK-COR-030C`. That is the six-company placement already recorded as `CR1285` (`asserts_start` on this row). `last_listed_date` of `CR1285` remains 18 September 1944; the end stays `open_at_last_claim` (no end date is invented). `C9385`, `C9386`, `C9387` and `C9388` are unchanged, including blank `parent_unit_id`: no opened source supports XXX Corps, 21st Army Group, a British or Canadian army or corps, US Ninth or First Army, or Netherlands District as the parent of the formation on those dates. No new command relation is added, because the sources describe a split (Limburg with the Americans, Brabant employed by the British) without naming a numbered Allied formation as a dated superior of `NL-INF-STOOT` as a whole, and "the American army" or "British command" is not a unit in the dataset. Prince Bernhard's Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten is the administrative superior from 22 September but is not in the dataset as a unit and was not created in this commit. Locations and confidence are unchanged. `R1162` is added as a reference (not attached to a claim).

- **Tests and remaining gap.** Scenario 263 covers the unchanged listing window (possible on 18 September 1944 because the placement starts that day at an undocumented hour, and possible thereafter through 17 December because that is also the only listing day; dropped on 18 December and on 1 May 1945 and VE-Day) and the `C9384` parent fill. The unit therefore remains unanswered from 18 December 1944 under the 90-day cutoff; that is a documentation gap, not an invented end. Combat Command A, 2nd Armored, is unchanged. Roadmap 377.

## 13 November 2026 — Stale `possible` carry-forward cutoff (branch `small-fixes-1113`, fourth task)

`scripts/who_controls.py` used to carry an `open_at_last_claim` relationship forward as `possible` at any distance from its `last_listed_date`. On VE-Day that left 101 German units still answering off listings 90+ days old (including June 1944 Kampfgruppen such as Meyer, Heintz, Boehm, Frey and Weidinger), plus named leftovers from the de Jong pass: the 79th Armoured Division (`UK-ARM-079D`, last listed 6 June 1944, with claims through 12 April 1945) and the Stoottroepen (`NL-INF-STOOT`, last listed 18 September 1944, with claims through 1 May 1945). The earlier design said there was no day threshold, because a threshold would invent a fact about how long an assignment lasted.

- **Reading cutoff, not an invented end.** `OPEN_CARRY_FORWARD_DAYS = 90` in `scripts/who_controls.py`. An open interval is still `possible` on the 90th day after its last listing and is dropped on the 91st: the interval no longer covers the date. No end date is written into `data/command_relations.csv`, and no new 'stale' or `UNKNOWN` state is added. Sourced ends are never capped; an inferred end stays `possible` only inside its already bounded interval; a later relation that still covers the date continues to answer. Allied relations still in force on 8 May 1945 stay `open_at_last_claim` in the tables (HANDOFF rule 18).

- **Why 90, not 60.** 90 days is the same threshold already used to flag stale-relation repair candidates (methodology, command-chain repair, 9 November 2026). On the pre-cutoff grid, carry-forward ages at the weekly dates plus 8 May (4,777 interval-date pairs) had a median of 62 days, 75th percentile 131, maximum 358 (158th Reserve Division, last listed 15 May 1944). On VE-Day, 115 units had a maximum carry-forward of 90+ days (Germany 101, France 3, UK 5, US 5, Netherlands 1); 132 units were at 60+ days. The 17 units in the 61-90 day band include late-war divisions last listed in February or early March and still in action in April and May (11th Panzer, last listed 8 March, claims through 4 May; 15th Panzergrenadier; 6th Fallschirmjäger; US 94th Infantry; 2nd Canadian Armoured Brigade). A 60-day cutoff would have dropped those on VE-Day. 90 days removes the 101-German-unit leftover and the named June and September cases without doing that.

- **What the cutoff does not drop.** Units with a sourced end (already certain through `valid_to`). Units kept alive by a later relation: the 7th Armored Division loses its stale First Army and 12th Army Group assignments 91 days after 23 January 1945, but remains answered through `CR1280` (III Corps, last listed 30 March); XXI Corps loses the still-open Riviera operational-control interval `CR1282` (last listed 26 January) from 27 April, but remains answered through `CR0200`/`CR0201` (last listed 22 April). The three daily probe units are unchanged. The Irene Brigade (`NL-INF-IRNEB`) is unchanged (last listed 8 May 1945 after the third task on this branch).

- **Documentation and tests.** The rule is updated in `schema/README.md` ("Reading a command interval"), `docs/HANDOFF.md` (staleness bullet and rule 18), `docs/methodology.md`, and roadmap 352 (pointer) and 376. Scenario 0 now checks the 90th day as `possible` and the 91st as dropped for the 7th Armored Division's First Army assignment. Scenarios 260 (stale drop: Kampfgruppe Meyer on the 91st day and on VE-Day; 79th Armoured likewise) and 261 (non-drop: Meyer on the 90th day; 7th Armored still answered via III Corps on 26 April) cover the new cutoff.

- **Grid (vs the post-task-3 grid, 18,640 answers).** 3,112 cells changed, 0 new keys. 1,738 go from an answer to no covering interval (Germany 1,568, UK 97, US 45, Netherlands 22, France 6), mostly divisions (955) and regiment/battle groups (331). 9 still answer after losing a stale own interval: the 7th Armored Division and XXI Corps on 30 April-8 May, Kampfgruppe Heintz on 11 September 1944, and Panzer-Brigade 105 on 18 and 25 December. 1,270 further cells still answer but their printed operational chain changes, because a higher headquarters was itself cut off (often 12th Army Group after 26 March). 95 cells were already unanswered: an open explicit-`unknown` placeholder is also cut off after 90 days, so the specific "no higher headquarters is recorded" message becomes the generic "no relationship interval covers" (for example Panzergruppe West, `CR0045`, from November 1944). On VE-Day, 113 units disappear (Germany 101, France 3, UK 5, US 3, Netherlands 1) and 2 are own-partial (7th Armored, XXI Corps). Daily probes: one chain-only change (`US-ABN-082D` on 17 December 1944 loses First Allied Airborne Army, last listed 17 September, 91 days earlier); none gone. Notable side effects: the 79th Armoured Division is unanswered from 11 September 1944 although it has claims through 12 April 1945 (`CR0064` was last listed on D-Day); the Stoottroepen from 18 December 1944 although they have a 1 May 1945 claim; 12th Army Group itself from 26 March 1945 (`CR0117` to SHAEF last listed 20 December 1944, with later claims that do not list it); Combat Command A, 2nd Armored, from 30 October 1944 (last listed 28 July, no later claims). Those are documentation gaps in the relations, not invented ends. The relations named in roadmap 352 stay open in the tables pending a source read. Versus the main/PR #90 baseline: 3,123 cells (the 3,112 cutoff changes plus the 11 Irene Brigade cells from the third task).

## 13 November 2026 — Princess Irene Brigade after 1 March 1945 (branch `small-fixes-1113`, third task)

The brigade's command relations and locations from about March 1945 to 8 May 1945 were largely unrecorded. `CR0933` (Second Army) already ended on 1 March 1945 by inference from Wikipedia, because Netherlands District was not then a unit; the District is now the placeholder `UK-DIST-NETH` (added 9 November 2026). No new place. Conflict group `G128` unused.

- **`C9445` and new `CR1310` (2 March 1945).** Wikipedia (`R676`) has the brigade put under Netherlands District (Major-General A. Galloway, headquarters at Tilburg) on 2 March 1945. New claim `C9445` (old value none): command change, parent `UK-DIST-NETH`, still on Walcheren (`PL0549`, inferred from de Jong deel 10a, `R894`, p. 477 n., mid-November 1944 to early April 1945), confidence 0.3 (one source family for the command change). New relation `CR1310`: assigned to `UK-DIST-NETH` from 2 March 1945, open at the last claim (`end_unknown` false); Allied units active on 8 May 1945 need no end row. Evidenced by `C9445` (`asserts_start`); `C1607` and `C9446` are observed during it. Kind `assigned`, the kind already used for the 4th Commando Brigade and the 33rd Armoured Brigade under the same District. Stacey pp. 585-586 has Dutch and Belgian units under the District on the line toward Tiel and has the District under Crerar from 13 April, but he does not date the Irene Brigade's own assignment; the District's higher command remains unrecorded (roadmap 371) and is not opened here. `CR0933` dates are unchanged; its note now records that the District is a unit and that the inferred 1 March end is matched by `CR1310`. `CR1284` (alternate Second Army start) is left open, so that scenario 238 is unchanged.

- **`C1607` (Hedel, 25 April 1945).** `reference_ids` old value `R676;R002`, new value `R676;R894;R002`. de Jong 10a p. 477 n. has the brigade committed at Hedel and Heusden after early April (he says he will return to that in deel 10b; deel 10b does not narrate the fighting). The footnote agrees the brigade was at Hedel after early April but does not date 25 April; confidence stays 0.5, no raise. `parent_unit_id` stays blank: the immediate superior named by Wikipedia, the 116th Infantry Brigade Royal Marines, is still not a unit of the dataset. The note no longer says that Netherlands District is not a unit.

- **`C9446` (The Hague, 8 May 1945).** New claim (old value none): the brigade enters The Hague (existing place `PL3529`), officially received by the burgemeester and cheered on the Groenmarkt; confidence 0.5; two official families, de Jong deel 10b p. 1426 (`R895`, including the illustration caption for 8 May) and the Dutch Ministry of Defence (`R1159` NIMH, 'Capitulatie en afronding'; `R1160` Defence historical canon: three days after the 5 May capitulation, as the first Allied unit). Activity `transit`, stated. Parent blank (those sources do not name a higher formation for the entry). English Wikipedia's unsourced '9 May' sentence is not entered as an alternate: de Jong, NIMH and the canon agree on 8 May, and the Wikipedia infobox photograph is itself captioned 8 May.

A start of the Hedel bridgehead on 22 or 23 April is likewise not stated as a day in Wikipedia (only 'three days' before the 25 April withdrawal already in `C1607`) or in the official histories. The existing Heusden place `PL2117` is the village of Asten, not the fortress town on the Bergse Maas, and no new Heusden place was added.

- **References.** New `R1159` (NIMH) and `R1160` (Defence canon), one family `netherlands_defence`. Semantic scenario 259; scenario 19's 25 April expectation is updated (the brigade is now under the District, which is a unit). Grid: 18,640 answers, 11 changed, 0 new keys, all `NL-INF-IRNEB` on 5, 12, 19 and 26 March, 2, 9, 16, 23 and 30 April, and 7 and 8 May 1945 (no relation to assigned to `UK-DIST-NETH`, certain; 8 May also shows activity transit from `C9446`). ## 13 November 2026 — CR1303 re-check against the full NHHC Operation NEPTUNE ch. 9 page (branch `small-fixes-1113`)

The air-naval pilot had entered `CR1303` (HMS Warspite assigned to Bombarding Force D, `UK-BF-D`, from 6 June 1944, end open) from a search snippet of NHHC Operation NEPTUNE ch. 9, because the earlier fetch of the page had been cut off (roadmap 375 (g)). The full chapter was re-read on 13 November 2026 from [the NHHC page](https://www.history.navy.mil/research/library/online-reading-room/title-list-alphabetically/o/operation-neptune-invasion-normandy/chapter-9-neptune-assaults.html) (already `R902`).

- **Relation confirmed, values unchanged.** Type `assigned`, superior `UK-BF-D`, start 1944-06-06 (`claim_date` / `inferred`), end open (`open_at_last_claim`). Evidence remains `C9426` (`observed_during`). The chapter does not date the end of the assignment.
- **The confirming passages.** Ch. 9 para 63: Warspite was already anchored in her bombarding position with Ramillies, Roberts and Arethusa as Force S approached the lowering position. Section E, "Force S — SWORD Area", p. 553 n. 2, the FORCE S table: Bombarding Force D lists Warspite under Mauritius (flag of Rear Admiral Patterson), with Ramillies, Roberts, Arethusa, Frobisher, Dragon and Danae. Approved by Scott (13 November 2026, "Yes" to an air schema pass before the Normandy pass). Details in `docs/air_naval_pilot.md` section 9.

Scenario 255.
- **Pilot units re-echeloned** (`units.csv`, the repeated `echelon` column of their claim files, and a `Review:` line in each `unit_note`): GER-FLK-002C `corps` -> `air_corps`; GER-JGK-002C `corps` -> `air_corps`; GER-LFL-003A `army` -> `air_force`; GER-JG-026 `regiment/battle_group` -> `air_wing`; GER-JGGR-026-2 and GER-JGGR-026-3 `battalion` -> `air_group`; US-FG-366 `regiment/battle_group` -> `air_group`; US-FS-390 `battalion` -> `air_squadron`; US-TAC-009C `corps` -> `air_division`. Reason: the ground equivalents were stand-ins; ids are unchanged. 21 claim rows carry the new value. The hierarchy and the grid are unaffected (air units are in `build/other_domains/`).
- **`data/aircraft_types.csv`.** New table (`AT###`), schema `schema/aircraft_types.schema.json`, `validate.check_aircraft_types`, `schema/json/performance_json.schema.json` (registered in `fields.json`), vocabularies `aircraft_role` and `aircraft_performance_key`, build output `build/other_domains/aircraft_types.csv`, uncited-reference warning extended. `check_capabilities` takes the key vocabulary. Seeded with 102 rows (AT001-AT102): 28 US, 29 UK, 42 Germany, 3 Canada; 51 rows carry figures from the Specifications section of the Wikipedia page of the type (`R1096`-`R1147`, 52 references, one per page); the others are family rows, the three Canadian variants and the L-4 (the page figures are for the civil Cub). Scenario 256.

This is also the equipment link: the claim's `as_of` dates it. No design change to the claims table. Scenario 257.

Three new warnings: a claim dated the day after a relation ends lists it as the end evidence (`C9439`, `C9440`, `C9442`); the three are expected.

Approved by Scott (13 November 2026, "Let's do the schema pass now"): build the section 5-6 proposals of `docs/air_naval_pilot.md`. Details in its section 8.

- **Scope marker.** New unit column `scope` (vocabulary `scope`: `in_scope`, `out_of_scope`; blank is `in_scope`). `build.py` routes a unit that is air, naval or `out_of_scope` with its claims and relations to `build/other_domains/` (`common.other_output_unit_ids()`); coverage and the main `units.*` leave it out. Old value: only `domain` separated claims. New value: `domain` or `scope`. No unit is marked yet. The main `build/units.csv` and `units.json` keep their old columns (the five other-output columns are dropped from them); `docs/coverage.md` and the other main outputs are unchanged.

Seeded with 200 rows `SC001`-`SC200` (US 65, UK 64, Germany 39, France 18, Netherlands 7, Poland 6, Canada 1) from 184 English Wikipedia class pages (`R912`-`R1095`, accessed 13 November 2026); 197 rows carry figures (each with its own `reference_id`, infobox text as written, nothing entered that a page does not give); the Hunt, Type VII and Type IX family rows hold no figures and their sub-types do. Unseeded remainder: roadmap 375 (l). The validator's "not cited" warning now counts ship-class citations.

Approved by Scott (12 November 2026). New general rule, recorded as `docs/HANDOFF.md` standing rule 21 and in the decision log, `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Add a new unit"), `docs/methodology.md` (new "Irregular forces" section) and `schema/README.md` (after the independent-units rule).

- **Rule.** Old value: no general rule for irregular or resistance forces (only the small-unit and independent-unit rules of 4 November 2026). New value: resistance groups, partisan bands and other irregular forces get unit entries only once they are organised into formal military units with a command chain (for example the Dutch Stoottroepen); loose cells and networks (for example the Dutch KP, OD and RVV) are not entered as units, even when they had a paper organisation or a regional commander. Existence, dates and strength figures for organisations that are not entered stay in the private notes. The small-unit rule still applies to the formal units. Reason: Scott approved this as a general rule when agreeing to enter the Stoottroepen and not the KP, OD or RVV.

## 12 November 2026 — de Jong 10a-1 follow-up: Polish 550-man second lift at Grave and the Betuwe bank, 25-26 September 1944 (branch `dejong-10a1`)

Approved by Scott (12 November 2026). Source `R894` (de Jong, *Het Koninkrijk*, deel 10a, p. 401, family `niod_dejong_koninkrijk`), printed page cited, paraphrase only. - **New claims (2, `C9379`-`C9380`; old value none, new value the row):** as above.
- **New place:** `PL4149` Betuwe bank of the Neder Rijn, Gelderland (area, precision 10 km; representative point from GeoNames Driel, `R782`).

## 12 November 2026 — de Lattre leftovers, chunk 2: the infantry divisions (branch `delattre-leftovers`)

Approved by Scott (roadmap 374, step 3). Source and method as in chunk 1: de Lattre, *The History of the French First Army* (`R686`, family `delattre_french_first_army`), entered from the private pass-2 reading notes (printed page for every line, paraphrase only); the borrow-only copy was not re-opened, and each new row says so. Before the rows were written, every event line was read again against the notes for its page, and several details first planned from memory were dropped or reworded (the Gémonval row is the 14 November attack, not a capture on 15 November; Rougemont-le-Château on 24 November is an attack, not a capture; several named-regiment rows were set to 0.3). `0.5` = one family, an exact named place on a stated day, whole division; `0.3` = only a regiment, group, brigade or company of the division, a span or inferred day, or an inferred attribution.

- **Correction of an earlier row, `C9269` (5th Armoured Division, Sigmaringen, 24 April, chunk 1):** the first version attributed Linarès's group to the 5th Armoured Division. De Lattre appoints Linarès, his chief of staff, to command the 2nd Moroccan Division on 13 April (p. 454), and p. 488 has the 2nd Moroccan Division splitting the Swabian Jura, so Linarès's group is the 2nd Moroccan Division's. The note carries the old and new event definition; `location_qualifier` old value "Linarès's group and the cavalry regiment", new value "cavalry regiment and Mozat's column only"; `current_activity` old value "Groups enter Sigmaringen", new value "Cavalry regiment enters Sigmaringen"; confidence unchanged at 0.3. The 2nd Moroccan Division has its own 0.3 row at Sigmaringen (`C9294`).
- **Supporting citation (1 row):** `C1641` (3rd Algerian Division, Speyer crossing, 31 March, already 0.9): cited, no change.
- **New claims (39, `C9275`-`C9313`; old value none, new value the row):**
  - 1st Free French Division (12 rows, `C9275`-`C9286`): Toulon (23 August, 2nd Brigade), Paray-le-Monial (7 September, detachment), Montbard (12 September, Savary squadron), the road from Lure (20 September), Lyoffans (25 September), Frédéric-Fontaine (28 September), Éloie, the Ballon d'Alsace and Rougemont-le-Château (23-24 November), Rhinau (2 January), Saint-Hippolyte (23 January, the Ill crossing, typed `arrival` beside the general attack row `C1635` and a map row), Grussenheim (28 January, with Vésinet's combat command of the 2nd Armoured Division, which resolves the open question on `C1648`) and Marckolsheim (1 February). Commander Brosset to the autumn and Garbay from 23 November.
  - 2nd Moroccan Division (8 rows, `C9288`-`C9295`): Gémonval (14 November), Héricourt (17 November), Cernay (20 January), Wittelsheim (3 February, 0.3: attributed through the commander named for the corps front), Chalampé (9 February), Pforzheim (6 April), Sigmaringen (24 April, Linarès's group, 0.3) and the St Anton end of the Arlberg tunnel (6 May, a detachment, day inferred).
  - 3rd Algerian Division (6 rows, `C9296`-`C9301`): Orbey (20 December), Kilstett (6 January, northern sub-sector), Scheibenhardt on the Lauter (19 March, the first fighting on German soil, which fills a month where the French own-nation share was nil), Speyer (30 March, the three units ordered to cross), Pforzheim (16 April, two regiments of the 716th Volksgrenadier Division surrender) and Weil der Stadt (20 April).

  - 4th Moroccan Mountain Division (2 rows, `C9310`-`C9311`): the Cernay pincer (30 January) and Soultz (4 February, Loth's Spahi group, typed `arrival` beside the Cernay row `C2047`).
  - 5th Armoured Division (1 row, `C9312`): Dornbirn (2 May, a Combat Command 5 element). 2nd Armoured Division (1 row, `C9313`): Montbard (12 September, the 1st Spahis, the other side of the first contact between the two armies).

## 10 November 2026 — Lifespan check as a validator warning (branch `lifespan-check`)

- **Why:** Scott approved roadmap 370(b) on 10 November 2026: add the consistency-fix-1 lifespan audit to the validator as a warning first, not an error.
- **Validator (`scripts/validate.py`):** new `check_lifespan` / `lifespan_issues`. A non-alternate claim dated before the unit's `formed_date` or after an end row (`destruction`, or `destroyed` / `disestablished` set) or more than 7 days after a lineage successor date is a WARNING (unit id, claim id, date, life bounds). An activation row after an end row starts a new life; alternate rows are ignored; an `absorbed_into` lineage link is not read as the successor's formation. A 3-day tail after an end row and a 7-day window around a lineage date are allowed (a month-precision lineage date expands to the last day of the month when testing "after the successor"). The exit code is unchanged, so `run_checks.sh` and CI still pass. Surrender alone is not treated as an end: many surrender rows record an enemy capitulation the unit accepted, not the unit's own end (treating them as ends would have flagged 9 further units, including Allied ones such as the 3rd Canadian Infantry Division and US VII Corps).
- **Current data:** 1 warning, `GER-INF-JUTLAND` `C8908` (10 April 1945), more than 7 days after lineage successor `GER-VG-019D` from 3 August 1944 (`UL014`). This is the known leftover of roadmap 370(a) (no place for the 9 March 1945 re-formation, so no activation row); not a false positive; no data changed.
- **Tests:** `scripts/semantic_tests.py` scenario 208 (the check reports only `C8908`; alternates after a brigade end, a re-formation, and `absorbed_into` are not flagged).
- **Docs:** roadmap 370(b) closed; new roadmap 373 (switch the warning to a hard error after a source pass or two shows no false positives); `docs/methodology.md` "Review guardrails"; `docs/HANDOFF.md` section 5.
