## 9 November 2026 — Theater per claim row; other-front rows (branch `placeholders-14-theater`, commit A)

- **Why:** Scott, 9 November 2026: "For the out of theatre data, I do want to keep those." Claim rows on other fronts were kept with the unit's theater (`western_europe`) and a note, because `theater` had to repeat `data/units.csv`; roadmap 362 proposed a per-claim theater and per-front operations.
- **Schema:** `schema/claims.schema.json` `repeatedColumns.fields` old value `unit_name, nationality, echelon, branch, theater`, new value `unit_name, nationality, echelon, branch` (reason: a row may be on another front than the unit's primary theater); the claim `theater` description now says the row's own theater and that it must equal its operation's.
- **Vocabulary `theater`:** new values `balkans` (Yugoslavia, Albania, Greece, Bulgaria, Aegean), `scandinavia` (Norway, Denmark), `home_germany` (the Reich of the time as a rear or home area: forming, training, refitting, replacement army). Descriptions: `western_europe` old value "from the Normandy landings ...", new value also the 1940 campaign, the 1940-1944 occupation and staging in Britain; `mediterranean` old value "Italy, Sicily, the Balkans and Greece, ...", new value "Italy, Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica ..." (the Balkans moved to `balkans`); `eastern_front` adds Slovakia and German territory reached by the Red Army; `other` drops "home-front units" (now `home_germany`). Vocabulary `country` gains HU and SK.
- **Operations:** 6 new holding umbrellas in `data/operations.csv` (date_basis `derived`, dates in the notes): `OP-FRONT-EASTERN` 1939-09-01 to 1945-05-11, `OP-FRONT-MEDITERRANEAN` 1940-06-10 to 1945-05-02, `OP-FRONT-BALKANS` 1940-10-28 to 1945-05-15, `OP-FRONT-SCANDINAVIA` 1940-04-09 to 1945-05-08, `OP-FRONT-NORTH-AFRICA` 1940-06-10 to 1943-05-13, `OP-HOME-GERMANY` 1939-09-01 to 1945-05-08.
- **Validator (`scripts/operations.py`):** new errors: a claim's `theater` differs from its operation's; an operation's theater differs from its parent's. The "no CMH campaign streamer covers the date" error now applies to `western_europe` rows only (old value: every row dated 6 June 1944-11 May 1945). ## 9 November 2026 — Command-chain repair, Western Front (branch `wf-health-fixes`, commit 1 of 3)

- **Why:** the Western Front health audit (9 November 2026) found standing relations left open long after their last listing, so `who_controls` answered "possible" for months where the sources already give the chain, and units with claims but no command relation. Scott approved the repair on 9 November 2026 ("Yes, start the fixes in that order").
- **Stale relations:** an open relation (`open_at_last_claim`) with preferred claims of its unit more than 90 days after its last listing, 6 June 1944 to 9 May 1945. Before: **64 relations, 672 claim-dates** (the audit gave 44 and 431 but did not record its method; this count is the one used here, `stale.py` in the private scratch). After: **20 relations, 56 claim-dates**, each a roadmap item (349, 352).
- **US divisions (CMH ETO-OB tables already cited, re-read through the Wayback Machine):** 12 divisions (4th, 26th, 28th, 29th, 35th, 36th, 76th, 79th, 87th, 90th and 102nd Infantry, 6th Armored). Standard table-end rule: a relation ends the day before the first row that no longer lists it (basis `assignment_table`); later runs are new relations (V-013: start at the first row of the run). Corps-column cells are `unspecified_subordination`; a cell marked "(Opns)"/"(Operations)" is `operational_control` and "(Adm)"/"(Admin)" `administrative_control` (my reading of the qualifier, flagged for Scott). 100 new relations (`CR1084` onward). 95 new claims (`C8508`-`C8602`), one `subordinate_assignment` row per table row after the last listing of the earlier chain, at the command post the same page lists (precision 10 km, confidence 0.5; 0.3 and 25 km where the command post in force could not be placed). 48 new places `PL3846`-`PL3893` (OpenStreetMap Nominatim, R002), existing places reused where the town already exists (`PL2391` Oermingen, `PL3341` Sibret, `PL2668` Mendig for Niedermendig). Where a closed relation had no new claim in its run, the closing date is stated on its latest existing ETO-OB link (CR0155 on C0277, CR0246 on C0547, CR0259 on C0411, CR0282 on C0435, CR0434 on C0605).
- **III and VIII Corps:** `CR0179` (III Corps -> Third Army) closed on 11 February 1945, earliest 10 February (basis `inferred`: Bradley's order of 10 February, The Last Offensive p. 96, R657; First Army tables from 12 February); new III Corps -> First Army 11 February (latest 12 February) to 18 April (table end, earliest 4 April) and III Corps -> Third Army from 19 April (99th, 86th Infantry and 14th Armored Division tables; p. 424). `CR0189` (VIII Corps -> Third Army) closed on 21 April 1945 (6th Armored Division table); new VIII Corps -> First Army 22 April to 10 May (earliest 5 May) and VIII Corps -> Ninth Army from 6 May (latest 11 May). ## stacey-victory-campaign: Stacey, The Victory Campaign, chapter XIX (Operation "Blockbuster" and the end of the Rhineland battle, 22 February - 11 March 1945) (3 November 2026)

## loc-12ag-maps: HQ 12th Army Group situation maps, pass 1 (31 October 2026)

Scott approved a pass over the Library of Congress series *HQ 12th Army Group situation maps* (public domain, 416 daily sheets 6 June 1944 to 26 July 1945) on 31 October 2026: one sheet a week at the 1200 hrs situation, in batches, one commit per batch, on branch `loc-12ag-maps` from `main` `62e97c3`. The maps are a separate source family (contemporary Allied situation maps): Allied units from their own reports and German units from G-2 estimates.

Rules applied (accepted by Scott): one reference for the series with the sheet id and situation date in each claim's `source_locator`; division points read as the main body and corps or army symbols as the headquarters at a precision of 10 km; German units at confidence 0.3; Allied units at 0.5, or 0.7 when another source family has the unit within 10 km on the same or the next day; no command relation and no parent from the maps (every new row has a blank parent); no front-line trace; units shown en route, marked as elements, unlocated or doubtful, and brigades and regiments stay in the private reading notes; placeholder units get no first claim; a unit shown between documented dates gets a claim; a disagreement with an existing row is logged as an open question and the existing row is unchanged. Commander is `unknown` on every new row because the maps name none. Reading notes are private.

### Rule of 31 October 2026: map rows are coarse filler

Scott on 31 October 2026 decided that the situation-map rows are coarse filler and never outrank a text row: from now on a map row is set to 0.7 (two source families) only when an existing non-map row of the unit agrees **within 5 km** (old value: within 10 km) on the same day (US: within three days). Applies to new rows from village pass 3 on; earlier rows are not changed. `tools/loc12ag` generation and the `R781` reliability note now say so (reliability_note old value "0.7 when another family agrees within 10 km on the same or the next day", new value adds the 5 km rule and its date). 54 of the 106 earlier map rows at 0.7 rest on agreement of 5-10 km (roadmap point 40, for Scott's decision).

## fms-german-6: two more FMS manuscripts (B-745, B-151; 31 October 2026)

Scott approved reading B-745 on Fold3 and B-151 from the Internet Archive and one data branch for the two on 31 October 2026, one commit per manuscript. Branch `fms-german-6` from `main` `1082707`. B-745 is read in the German original. B-151 is read in the US Army English translation from the Internet Archive because neither B-151 nor its sequel B-151a is on the Fold3 M1035 fiche and the German original is held only at the Bundesarchiv; the item was catalogued as B-151a but every page is B-151. Both are US Government works; the claims paraphrase them in English. The reading notes stay private and are not in this repository.

Rules applied (accepted by Scott): no command relation and no parent from a single manuscript (every new row has a blank parent); no Allied dates from the manuscripts; strengths stay in the reading notes; no front-line traces; confidence 0.5 for one source, 0.7 when a second source family agrees, 0.3 for arrivals, approximate days, doubtful readings and map positions; disagreements with existing rows stay open points and no existing row is changed. No first claim is given to a placeholder unit (the 257th Volksgrenadier and 106th Infantry Divisions and Divisions Nr. 405 and 905 stay placeholders).

### B-745 (Brandenberger, Nineteenth Army, 1 April-5 May 1945, German original)

- **New reference** `R779` (B-745; archive_document, family `fms_german_manuscript`). Reliability: 8 of 12 checkable facts agree with the dataset (67%).
- **New places** `PL1112` to `PL1137` (26; OpenStreetMap Nominatim): the Nineteenth Army command posts of Anlage 4 from Dettenbach to Pfunds and the corps and division command posts of 1 and 9 April.
- **New claims** `C2248` to `C2274` (27; 2 at 0.3 and the rest at 0.5; each note carries old value none, new value and reason): the Nineteenth Army command post at Dettenbach on 1 April and its eleven moves to Jungingen, Mühlingen, Ravensburg, Schlier, Kempten, Burgberg, Lermoos, Ehrwald, Karrösten, Pians and Pfunds; the LXIV Corps at Ödsbach (1 April) and Enzklösterle (9 April) and near Landeck on 5 May (0.3, sketch); the XVIII SS Corps at St. Trudpert (1 April) and Schonach (21 April); the LXXX Corps at Neckarrems (9 April) and Münsingen (22 April, 0.3, sketch); the Twenty-fourth Army at Engen (1 April) and Eglofs (26 April); the 716th Division at Waldrennach, the 559th at Mundelsheim, the 198th at Kleinbottwar and the 47th at Monrepos; the 16th Volksgrenadier Division assembled south of Gültlingen (18 April); the 189th Division attack from Laichingen (22 April).
  - Parent blank on all 27 (inferred value: old none, new blank, reason: no command relation from a single manuscript).
- **No existing row changed.** No relation, no conflict group (next `CR1067`, `G034`).
- **Coordinate exceptions:** two speed exceptions added for `C1217` (a Lexikon table row with a representative point at Donaueschingen on 26 April) against the new command posts `C2254` (Kempten) and `C2255` (Burgberg); old value none, new value an explained exception, reason: the table row is not a headquarters position.
- **Disagreements recorded, no value changed:** Brandenberger taking command on 1 April (arrived 28 March) in B-745 against 26 March in `C1190`; the LXXX Corps under the Nineteenth Army from 9 April in B-745 against 8 April in `C2123`; the XVIII SS Corps staff dissolved at 2200 on 26 April in B-745 against 27 April in `C1273`; the Twenty-fourth Army shipping its troops across Lake Constance in the night to 26 April in B-745 against 21 April in `C1219`.
- **Semantic scenario 51.**

### B-151 (Manteuffel, Fifth Panzer Army, September-16 December 1944, English translation from the Internet Archive)

- **New reference** `R780` (B-151; archive_document, family `fms_german_manuscript`). Reliability: 6 of 8 checkable facts agree with the dataset (75%).
- **New places** `PL1138` to `PL1142` (5; OpenStreetMap Nominatim): Le Hohwald, Manderscheid in the Bernkastel-Wittlich district, Dackscheid, Kyllburg, Gerolstein.
- **New claims** `C2275` to `C2281` (7; 3 at 0.3 and the rest at 0.5; each note carries old value none, new value and reason): Fifth Panzer Army headquarters at Le Hohwald on Manteuffel's arrival (11 September), at Königshoven on the Aachen front (22 October), the operations staff to Manderscheid (23 November) and the forward move to Dackscheid (15 December); the LVIII Panzer Corps at Eisenschmitt (23 November, 0.3, approximate day); the XLVII Panzer Corps staff complete at Kyllburg (8 December, 0.3, arrival); the LXVI Corps headquarters at Gerolstein (4 November, 0.3, corps number printed as 65).
  - Parent blank on all 7 (inferred value: old none, new blank, reason: no command relation from a single manuscript).
- **New place rather than reuse:** `PL1066` (Manderscheid, used by `C2179`) has the coordinates of the Manderscheid near Arzfeld in the western Eifel; B-151 places the army staff near Eisenschmitt and Gerolstein, which fits Manderscheid in the Bernkastel-Wittlich district, so the new row uses the new place `PL1139` and `PL1066` and `C2179` are unchanged (open point).
- **No existing row changed.** No relation, no conflict group (next `CR1067`, `G034`).

## official-history-pass-2: US gaps, a German refit span and the pilot-division labels (31 October 2026)

Scott approved official-history pass 2 on 31 October 2026, as one branch with one commit per source. Branch `official-history-pass-2` from `main` `13be4a4`.

### Chunk 1, US gaps (The Last Offensive)

- Source: the US Army official history (CMH), MacDonald, The Last Offensive (`R568` chapter 18 and `R569` chapter 19, HyperWar text); paraphrase with printed pages. No new reference.
- New place: `PL1055` Berchtesgaden, Bayern (OpenStreetMap Nominatim).
- 1 new claim: C2160, 101st Airborne, 8 May 1945, Berchtesgaden: garrison point (inferred), 0.3. Old value of each activity column: none (the row is new). Reason: the division raced for Berchtesgaden on 4 May (p. 442) and was arranging an SS surrender on 7 May (p. 473); no place is given for 8 May, so the last named objective is used and the state is inferred.
- Semantic tests: new scenario 42; scenario 34 and the batch filter (`NOT_OHP`) now leave out pass 2 rows (`OHP2`). Old filter: rows whose notes name the official-history pass. New filter: the same less `C2160`. Reason: the pass 2 notes also name the official-history pass, and the pass 1 totals stay as approved.
- Still open (no dated source in The Last Offensive): 8 May rows for the 70th and 106th; the open spans of the 11th Armored (23 December 1944), 26th (29 January 1945), 70th (17 February 1945), 104th (23 February 1945) and 106th (15 March 1945); the undated rests listed in the roadmap.

### Chunk 2, German refit spans (Lexikon der Wehrmacht)

- Source: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 9. Panzer-Division (`R610`); short dated facts only, paraphrased. Pages read: 9th, 2nd, 21st and 116th Panzer and the 226th Infantry; only the 9th Panzer page dates a late-1944 refit (the 116th Panzer refit in the Eifel has no date).
- New place: `PL1056` Rheydt, Mönchengladbach (OpenStreetMap Nominatim).
- 3 new claims, `C2161` to `C2163` (old value of each activity column: none, the rows are new):
  - C2161, 9th Panzer, 27 October 1944, Venlo: in_line start (stated), 0.3. Relief attack for the 15th Army in the Venlo-Sittard area (27 to 30 October); representative point.
  - C2162, 9th Panzer, 31 October 1944, Rheydt: refitting start (stated, derived start day), 0.3. Short refit in the Rheydt area after the attack.
  - C2163, 9th Panzer, 15 November 1944, Geilenkirchen: in_line start (stated), 0.5. Defensive fighting for Geilenkirchen from 15 November; ends the refit span by the implicit-end rule.
- Not changed: the 226th Division (Dünkirchen) stays blank. Its only row is a month-level listing, and scenario 32 keeps listings unlabelled.
- Semantic tests: scenario 42 extended (`OHP2` now covers `C2160` to `C2163`).

### Chunk 3, labels for the pilot divisions

- 59 existing rows labelled; no new claims, places or references. Old value of each activity column: blank. New values and reasons are in each row's `Activity:` note. Rows of the 4th Canadian Armoured (18), 1st Polish Armoured (31), British 1st Airborne (2), British 50th (6) and French 3rd Algerian (2) Divisions; 53 stated and 6 inferred.
- Rubric as before: the division fighting, capturing, landing or relieving another division in the line is `in_line` (point, stated); orders, arrivals or part of the division in action are `in_line` inferred (0.3 cap); command changes stay blank (`C1339`, `C1560`).
- Spans: `C1340` (Suitcase, 20 October 1944) is an `in_line` start and ends the 4th Canadian Armoured refit span of 4 September (`C1818`); `C1342` (Army Reserve at Boxtel, 23 December 1944) is a `reserve` start, ended by the `in_line` start `C1389` (Elephant, 26 January 1945); `C1579` (1st Polish Armoured at Wilhelmshaven, 6 May 1945) is a `garrison` start. The British 1st Airborne refit (`C1816`) and the 1st Polish Armoured line span (`C1553`) stay open (no dated end in the sources).
- Semantic tests: scenario 26, 4th Canadian Armoured on 1 December 1944: old expectation no answer (open refit span past 30 days); new expectation `in_line`, certain, inferred, 0.3 (the Suitcase line span ended by the Boxtel reserve); reason: the pilot rows are now labelled. Scenario 42 counts 63 rows and checks the new spans.

## fms-b701-armygroupb: Army Group B from Foreign Military Studies B-701 (Reichhelm; 30 October 2026)

Scott approved the reading of the Army Group B manuscript and a data branch on 30 October 2026. One branch from `main` `535b12c`. Ids start after the branches `fms-b703-armygroupg` (merged as PR #56; `C2116` to `C2126`, `PL1032` to `PL1038`, `R767`, `G033`) and `fms-b811-15army` (merged as PR #57; `C2127` to `C2134`, `PL1039` to `PL1044`, `R768`); the branch `fold3-links` (merged as PR #55) changes citations only. Scott approved the 36 proposed changes on 30 October 2026 after a read-only check of the five manuscripts against the dataset and de Lattre (`R686`). One branch from `main` `664d9eb`. Sources: Botsch, B-766 (16 September-17 November 1944) and B-263 (8 November 1944-10 January 1945); Brandstaedter, B-463 (4 January-21 March 1945); Thumm, B-468 (1 November-31 December 1944) and B-550 (6 December 1944-28 January 1945); NARA M1035, read on Fold3. These are US Government works, and the claims paraphrase them in English. The reading notes stay private and are not in this repository.

  - B-263: 62%.

  - B-468: 60%.

## delattre-ellis-decisions: Scott's answers to the six open points of the de Lattre and Ellis batch (30 October 2026)

Scott accepted all six recommendations on 30 October 2026 ("Let's take your recommendations for the questions"). One branch from `main` `ca1a105`. Printed pages of de Lattre, *The History of the French First Army* (1952), paraphrase only.

- **Retired claim.** French 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division, Briançon, 14 October 1944 (Wikipedia, confidence 0.3), the first entry in `data/retired_claims.csv`. Old value: a preferred row at Briançon on 14 October; new value: retired, replaced by the new row below. Reason: de Lattre (pp. 130-131, 161, 187, 191) puts the division's Alpine fighting in mid-September 1944 and the division on the Doubs front by late September, so the 14 October date does not fit.
- **New claim.** French 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division, Abriès (Queyras, Hautes-Alpes), 15 September 1944, de Lattre p. 161 (with pp. 130-131 for the Alpine context): the commander of the division's 3rd Moroccan Tabor Group is killed near Abriès. Representative point for the Alpine sector, precision 10 km, confidence 0.3, activity in_line (inferred, capped at 0.3).
- **Places.** New place Abriès, Hautes-Alpes (OpenStreetMap Nominatim). The place Briançon, Hautes-Alpes is removed: its only claim was retired (old row: Briançon, Hautes-Alpes, point 44.8984, 6.6436, precision 3 km, FR, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, OpenStreetMap Nominatim); its id is not to be reused.
- **Kept, no value changed.** The Rouffach row of 5 February 1945 (the one-day difference with de Lattre stays stated in the row); the German 15th Panzergrenadier (Saarbrücken) and 9th Panzer (Arnhem) Lexikon rows of 15 October 1944 at 0.3 beside the Venlo rows; the British 5th Infantry Division unit record.
- **No row, by decision.** Constance on 26 April 1945 for the French 1st Armoured Division (entered by a corps group of the I Corps, which is not modelled); the German 269th Division (no firm day in de Lattre). Recorded in `docs/roadmap.md`.

## source-fixes-delattre-ellis: corrections and new positions from the de Lattre and Ellis reading notes (30 October 2026)

Scott approved this batch on 30 October 2026 ("Please proceed"), after the reading-method branch was merged. One branch from `main` `647d774`. Sources: de Lattre, *The History of the French First Army* (1952), printed pages and paraphrase only, and Ellis, *Victory in the West*, vol. II, printed pages. The reading notes stay private and are not in this repository. Every changed row carries a `Review (source fixes from de Lattre and Ellis, 30 October 2026 ...)` sentence with the old value, the new value and the reason.

### Changed rows

- French 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division, Briançon, 14 October 1944: confidence 0.5 to 0.3, de Lattre added. Reason: de Lattre has the division retake Briançon and Modane by mid-September (pp. 130-131, 161) and its regiments on the Doubs and Lure front by late September (pp. 187, 191). Kept as an open question.
- French 4th Moroccan Mountain Division, 12 January 1945: place Vieux-Thann to Lure; location basis inferred to documented on date; confidence 0.3 to 0.5; activity transit (stated) to reserve (inferred). Reason: de Lattre p. 342 has the division still at Lure on 12 January (in army reserve since 20 December, p. 299); it attacks at Vieux-Thann only on 20 January (p. 345, an existing row).
- French 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division, Karlsruhe, 3 April 1945: conflict group blank to new group 28, status preferred to alternate, confidence 0.5 to 0.3. Reason: de Lattre pp. 434-437 has the division at Bruchsal on 2 and 3 April and gives Karlsruhe on 4 April to the 9th Colonial Division. The new Bruchsal row is the preferred row of the group (a coordinate exception documents the deliberate conflict).
- French 5th Armoured Division, Dannemarie, 24 November 1944: activity reserve to in_line (inferred, point). Reason: de Lattre p. 268 has its combat command 4 clearing the Seppois roads and reaching Altkirch that day; the evening relief of p. 275 is a regrouping for the next attack. Semantic scenario 33 expectation changed to match.

## official-history-pass-1: 8 May 1945 rows, span closures and blank divisions from the official histories (30 October 2026)

Scott approved the official-history pass on 30 October 2026, after the Canada and France batch was merged (PR #47). Branch `official-history-pass-1` from `main` `1431a82`. Each chunk is its own commit; every commit passes the full checks.

Sources: the US Army official history (CMH, The Last Offensive, chapters already cited), the Ninth Army history *Conquer: The Story of Ninth Army, 1944-1945* (1947, public domain; new reference `R760`), the Canadian official history by Stacey (`R668`, short quotations with printed pages) and de Lattre's history of the French First Army (`R686`, page numbers and paraphrase only; the reading notes stay outside the repository). Ellis's British official history is not available as public text and was not used.

Every row is a new claim with its activity values set; nothing existing was changed (old value of each activity column: none, the row is new). Rows dated 8 May 1945 whose place or state the source does not give for that day are inferred and capped at 0.3, and each says why in its `Activity:` note.

Semantic tests: scenarios 26 to 32 now count only their own batch's rows (`NOT_OHP`): old filter, every activity row of the batch's units; new filter, the same rows less those whose notes name the official-history pass; reason, this pass adds rows to units of those batches, and the batch totals stay as approved.

## activity-rollout-1: 28th Infantry Division refit at Neufchâteau (29 October 2026)

Scott asked for this on 29 October 2026. Source: the CMH combat chronicle, 28th Infantry Division (R724). 2 new claims; no existing row changed; no new place or reference. Next ids: claim C1905, place PL0954, reference R734.

- C1903, 22 December 1944, Neufchâteau (PL0248): refitting start (stated), 0.5. The chronicle says the division withdrew to Neufchâteau for reorganization. Reorganization is recorded as refitting, because the design folds rest into refitting.
- C1904, 2 January 1945, Verdun (PL0361, a representative point for the Meuse line from Givet to Verdun, 50 km): refitting end (stated), 0.5. The move to the Meuse line ends the refit. It is recorded as the end of the refit, not an in_line start: the next state row is 95 days later, and the chronicle has rehabilitation after 6 March, so a start would overstate the line service.

The refit after the Hürtgen (before 16 December 1944) is still deferred to the official-history pass.

Scott accepted the follow-up's recommendations. R725 was drafted and dropped before commit; it is unused and is not to be reused. 16 new claims (C1887-C1902), 3 new places (PL0951 Salzburg, PL0952 Kufstein, PL0953 Kitzbühel). Next ids: claim C1903, place PL0954, reference R734. No existing row changed.

- C1897 90th Infantry Division: en route to Prague, in_line point (stated), 0.3 (the place is inferred).

Still without an 8 May row: the 29th, 30th and 83rd Infantry Divisions and the 2nd Armored Division. Their chronicles stop before VE Day (the 29th on the Elbe until 4 May, the 30th at an Elbe contact, the 83rd leaving the Barby bridgehead on 6 May, the 2nd Armored halted on the Elbe on 20 April).

## activity-rollout-1 follow-up: rest and refit periods, span closures and closing rows (29 October 2026)

Scott approved a follow-up pass on the same branch for the same 30 US divisions. 66 new claims (C1821-C1886), 13 new places (PL0938-PL0950; Blankenburg reuses PL0649), 5 new references (R718-R722, the Wikipedia articles of the 8th, 35th, 45th, 80th and 95th Infantry Divisions). Next ids: claim C1887, place PL0951, reference R723.

Source: the English Wikipedia article of each division, whose Second World War text follows the CMH combat chronicle. One source family per row, so confidence is 0.5 where the source gives a date and names the place, and 0.3 where the date or the place is inferred (each note says which). No row is 0.7 or 0.9. Every new row has an `Event support` quotation and an `Activity:` sentence.

Rules used:

- Occupation duty is recorded as `garrison`.
- A closing row at 8 May 1945 is added only where the source places the division on or until VE Day. It ends an open span (`end`) or is a `point`. 17 of the 30 divisions have one. The 3rd, 28th, 29th, 30th, 36th, 79th, 83rd and 90th Infantry Divisions and the 2nd, 7th, 10th and 12th Armored Divisions have none, because the source does not say where they were or what they were doing on that day.
- A batch-1 `start` whose implicit span would run for more than 90 days with no source is changed to a `point`.

Changes to existing rows (the reason is in each row's `Activity:` note):

- 2nd Infantry Division C0046, 5th Armored C0262, 6th Armored C0271, 35th Infantry Division C0424, 80th Infantry Division C0458: activity_span changed from start to point. The next state row is 104 to 262 days later.
- 95th Infantry Division C0661: point to start. The source has the division holding the Ruhr line until the end of the war. C1881 closes the span.
- 12th Armored Division C0630: point to start. This ends the St. Avold refit (C1848).

## activity-rollout-1: activity status, rollout batch 1 (29 October 2026)

Scott approved the rollout on 29 October 2026 in batches of about 30 units. Batch 1 covers 30 US divisions: the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th, 28th, 29th, 30th, 35th, 36th, 45th, 69th, 79th, 80th, 83rd, 89th, 90th and 95th Infantry Divisions and the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 10th, 12th and 14th Armored Divisions (the US divisions with the most rows; the pilot units are not touched).

113 existing rows are annotated (89 stated, 24 inferred): 110 in_line, 3 reserve, no refitting, garrison or transit. No new claim, place, relation or reference; next ids unchanged (C1821, PL0938). No location, date or confidence value changed. Every changed row has an `Activity:` note with the old value (blank), the new value and the reason. Row confidence is unchanged; activity confidence is computed at query time (`scripts/activity.py`).

Reading rules used in this batch:

- A row whose cited source describes the division itself fighting on the date (attacking, landing, capturing, defending) is `in_line`, `point`, `stated`.
- A row dating the division's entry into combat or into the line is `in_line`, `start`, `stated` (open; read as possible for at most 30 days).
- A row describing only part of the division (a combat command, task force, regiment, battalion or patrol) is `in_line`, `point`, `inferred` (main-body rule; capped at 0.3).
- A row naming reserve in words is `reserve` (`point`, or `start` for the 4th Armored pulled back into reserve on 10 January 1945).
- Command post moves, command changes and arrivals without combat are left blank: they do not show the state.
- The 6th Armored containing Lorient (15 August 1944) is `in_line`, not `garrison`; garrison is kept for the fortress garrisons.
- The 4th Armored's entry into combat (17 July 1944) is a point, not a start: a start would run unbroken to its reserve start of 10 January 1945.
- Disputed rows (89th Division Moselle crossing) are left blank.

- **Kampfgruppen Chill, Peiper and von der Heydte (10 claims, C1794 to C1803).** These are new units. `GER-KG-PEIPER` is organic to the 1st SS Panzer Division (`CR1062`), and `GER-KG-CHILL` is organic to the 85th Infantry Division (`CR1061`). `GER-KG-HEYDTE` (Luftwaffe) has no relation.

- **Panzer-Brigade 103 has no claims.** It served on the Eastern Front only.

## brigades-us-1944-45: Brigades Batch 2, US independent brigades, regiments, battalions and task forces (29 October 2026)

Batch 2 of the 35 approved brigades (rows 13 to 19 of the planning list). Each period and claim was checked against the US Army official histories (Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine; Blumenson, Breakout and Pursuit; Cole, The Ardennes; MacDonald, The Last Offensive) and Wikipedia; where the planning list (written from memory) differed from the sources, the sources were followed and the difference is listed below. Confidence follows the rubric (0.9 exact place and two source families; 0.7 exact place and one official history; 0.5 one family with an approximate place, or Wikipedia alone; 0.3 representative point or approximate date). Command relations: a corps or army headquarters is `assigned` (or `operational_control` where the source says "direct control"), a division or task force is `attached`; starts and ends not dated by a source are inferred from the row dates and annotated.

- **Dragoon airborne units (25 claims, C1714 to C1738).** New units `US-ABTF-001D` (1st Airborne Task Force, echelon division: a provisional airborne division), `US-PRCT-517` (517th Parachute Regimental Combat Team), `US-PIB-509` (509th Parachute Infantry Battalion) and `US-PIB-551` (551st Parachute Infantry Battalion). 1st Airborne Task Force (4): the Le Muy landing, the east-flank sector of 25 August, the southern third of the Alpine front in mid-October, the dissolution in November. 517th (11): Le Muy, Les Arcs, Saint-Cézaire, Col de Braus, Sospel, Soissons, Soy (1st Battalion), Manhay (3rd Battalion), Trois-Ponts under the 82nd Airborne Division, Stavelot under the 106th Division, Kleinhau under the 78th Division. 509th (4): Le Muy drop, Le Muy taken, the 3rd Armored Division sector, Sadzot. 551st (6): Le Muy drop, Draguignan, Nice, Werbomont, Rochelinval, inactivation at Juslenville. 16 new places; eight new references (R692 to R699). Inferred values, each annotated in the record (old value: none, the row is new; new value as stated; reason):
  - 1st Airborne Task Force, 25 August and mid-October 1944: representative points (Nice, the south end of the sector; Sospel), confidence 0.3; 15 October stands for "mid-October".
  - 1st Airborne Task Force, dissolution: 23 November 1944 (Wikipedia) is used; Clarke and Smith say about the 25th; Soissons (Wikipedia) is the place, confidence 0.3.
  - 509th, 23 December 1944: a representative point (Manhay) in the 3rd Armored Division sector, confidence 0.5.
  - The attachments to the 1st Airborne Task Force of the 517th and 509th close on 17 November 1944 and of the 551st on 21 November (the day before the attachment to the 101st Airborne Division that Wikipedia gives); division attachments in the Ardennes close the day before the next row under another division.
- **Corrections found against the sources (airborne):** the task force was named on 12 July 1944 (Clarke and Smith; Wikipedia 11 July) and dissolved in November 1944, so it is not in the Ardennes; the 551st was a separate battalion (1st Battalion, 551st Parachute Infantry), inactivated on 27 January 1945, not carried into the spring; Draguignan fell on 16 August (Clarke and Smith; Wikipedia says 15 August); the 517th was with the 13th Airborne Division from 15 February 1945, which ends its independent period (no row after 5 February); a planned row for the 551st raid at "Noirfontaine" (27-28 December 1944, Wikipedia) was dropped because the only place of that name found (Noirefontaine near Bouillon) is far from the 82nd Airborne front.

- **1st Special Service Force, Task Force Butler and Task Force A (20 claims, C1739 to C1758).** New units `US-SSF-001B` (1st Special Service Force, recorded as US; the Canadian component is not split), `US-TF-BUTLER` (Task Force Butler, officially the Provisional Armored Group, VI Corps) and `US-TDB-001B` (Task Force A, whose headquarters was the 1st Tank Destroyer Brigade). 1st Special Service Force (5): Levant, Port-Cros, Villeneuve-Loubet, the Alpine front in mid-October, the disbandment near Villeneuve-Loubet. Task Force Butler (6): Le Muy, Sisteron, Aspres, Marsanne, the Condillac Pass, Loriol. Task Force A (9): Miniac, Châteauneuf, Saint-Brieuc, Guingamp, Morlaix, Saint-Michel-en-Grève, Paimpol, the base of the Crozon peninsula, Douarnenez. 17 new places; one new reference (R700). `C1758` (Douarnenez, 20 September 1944) is in `data/operation_exceptions.csv` under the Siege of Brest, one day after its end, because Blumenson calls it the final action of the Brest operations. Inferred values, each annotated in the record (old value: none, the row is new; new value as stated; reason):
  - 1st Special Service Force, mid-October 1944: a representative point (Menton), confidence 0.3; 15 October stands for "mid-October".
  - 1st Special Service Force, disbandment: 5 December 1944 near Villeneuve-Loubet (Wikipedia) is used; Clarke and Smith give 6 January 1945 as the formal date. The attachment to the 1st Airborne Task Force ends on 23 November 1944 with the task force.
  - The Seventh Army's direct control of the force (and of the 1st Airborne Task Force) is recorded as `operational_control` (Clarke and Smith, ch. 3, p. 45: "direct control of the Seventh Army"); for the force it closes on 25 August, the day before the first row with the task force.
  - Task Force Butler: VI Corps from its assembly on 17 August (row date); under the 36th Division from 23 August (Clarke and Smith: Dahlquist dissolved it as a separate entity that morning but used it again); both relations close at the last row (29 August).
  - Task Force A, 27 August 1944: a representative point (Crozon) for the base of the peninsula, confidence 0.3; the attachment to the 8th Division starts on 15 September 1944 (inferred: Blumenson says mid-September). Task Force B (21-31 August), which combined it with the 38th Infantry, is not a unit in the dataset.
- **Corrections found against the sources (force and task forces):** the 1st Special Service Force landed on Levant and Port-Cros after midnight, so on 15 August (Wikipedia says 14 August), and was not under VI Corps but under the Seventh Army, then the 1st Airborne Task Force; Task Force Butler's life ends with the Montélimar battle (29 August), not with a later pursuit, and from 23 August it was under the 36th Division; Task Force A was a Third Army task force under VIII Corps built on the 1st Tank Destroyer Brigade (not a cavalry group), and it served from 3 August to the fall of Brest (20 September) and was "soon dissolved".

- **Semantic scenario 24 (12 expectations, 368 in all).** It checks the 1st Airborne Task Force under the Seventh Army's direct control on D-day and with no relation after its dissolution, the 1st Special Service Force under the Seventh Army on D-day and with the task force on 26 August, the 517th with the task force at Les Arcs and under the XVIII Airborne Corps and the 82nd Airborne Division on 3 January 1945, the 551st with no relation after its inactivation, Task Force Butler under VI Corps at Sisteron and also under the 36th Division at Condillac, Task Force A under VIII Corps at Morlaix, and the first and last claim ids of the batch.

- **Docs.** `docs/HANDOFF.md` (claim count 1,758, next ids `C1759`, `CR1040`, `PL0907`, `R701`, validator 41 warnings, semantic tests 368) and `docs/roadmap.md` (Brigades Batch 2 and its seven open points). 19 new validator warnings, each explained in its row: 18 "attached entry without a standing parent" for the separate units and `US-SSF-001B` line 6 (the disbandment row asserts the earlier end of the task-force attachment).

## brigades-uk-can-1944-45: Brigades Batch 1, British and Canadian independent brigades (29 October 2026)

Scott approved 35 independent brigades in three batches; this is Batch 1 (rows 1 to 12 of the planning list). Each period and claim was checked against Ellis (Victory in the West), Stacey (The Victory Campaign) and Wikipedia; where the planning list (written from memory) differed from the sources, the sources were followed and the difference is listed below. Command relations follow the batch convention: a corps is `assigned`, a division `attached` (temporary), and a move into the 79th Armoured Division `organic`. Ends not dated by a source are closed at the next claim (basis `inferred_from_next_claim`). One commit per item.

- **Armoured and tank brigades (32 claims, C1658 to C1689).** 4th Armoured (5), 6th Guards Tank (5), 8th Armoured (5), 27th Armoured (4), 31st Tank (2), 33rd Armoured (4) and 34th Tank (7). Four placeholders became active (27th, 33rd, 6th Guards, 34th). 13 new places; two new Wikipedia references (R687, R688). Inferred values, each annotated in the record (old value: none, the row is new; new value; reason):
  - 27th Armoured Brigade, 29 July 1944, break-up: a representative point in the Caen sector, confidence 0.3, because no source places the brigade on the day; the date is Ellis's and the Wikipedia regiment list's (29 July), not the 27 July of the Wikipedia lead.
  - 31st Tank Brigade, 4 September 1944, transfer to the 79th Armoured Division: confidence 0.3, a representative point in the Caen sector because no source places the brigade on the day (its regiments were converting to Crocodiles); the relation to the 79th is `organic` from that date.
  - 34th Tank Brigade, 6 November 1944, Willemstad: confidence 0.3, the objective named by Wikipedia stands for the brigade's position.
  - 34th Tank Brigade, 15 July 1944: the XII Corps relation is inferred from Stacey naming Greenline as the XII Corps operation (p. 169), starting on the row date.
  - 6th Guards Tank Brigade, 27 March 1945: the attachment to XVIII Airborne Corps starts on the row date (Ellis, vol. II, p. 305, gives no date); the few days under the US Ninth Army are not recorded.
  - Division attachments with no stated end are closed at the next claim under a different parent.
- **Corrections to the planning list (armour):** 27th Armoured Brigade broken up on 29 July 1944 (Ellis; the list said 27 July); 31st Tank Brigade arrived on 19 June 1944 and its independent period ends on 4 September 1944, when it joined the 79th Armoured Division; 33rd Armoured Brigade is shown "from 79th Armoured Division" in Ellis's Rhine order of battle, so its independent period ends early in 1945 (open question); 34th Tank Brigade: Wikipedia puts it in the 79th Armoured Division in February 1945 while Ellis lists it as independent (open question); the 6th Guards and 34th brigades were renamed Armoured in 1945 (unit ids kept).
- **Infantry and commando brigades (17 claims, C1690 to C1706).** New units UK-INF-056B (56th Infantry Brigade, re-formed 15 February 1944) and UK-INF-115B (115th Infantry Brigade); the 1st and 4th Special Service Brigades became active. 56th Infantry Brigade (6): the Gold landing, Bayeux, Tilly-sur-Seulles under the 7th Armoured Division, the opening of Bluecoat at Saint-Germain-d'Ectot, the Orne near Thury-Harcourt under the 59th Division and the move into the 49th Division; 115th Infantry Brigade (1); 1st Special Service (Commando) Brigade (4): Ouistreham, Blackcock, Well and Wesel; 4th Special Service (Commando) Brigade (6): Saint-Aubin, Dunkirk, De Haan, Westkapelle, the last Walcheren strong-point and the take-over of Walcheren. Seven new places. The deferred relation D01 (the 56th Infantry Brigade attached to the 50th Division, claim C0017) is now relation CR0997 and has been removed from `docs/deferred_relations.md`; the name is replaced by the unit id in the `composing_units` of C0017 and C0023. One overlap (CR0998 and CR0999, the handover day of 12 June 1944) is documented in `data/command_relation_overlaps.csv`. Inferred values, each annotated in the record (old value: none, the row is new, unless stated):
  - 56th Infantry Brigade, 20 August 1944: a representative point (Caen sector), confidence 0.3; the attachment to the 59th Division and the XII Corps relation closed on 19 August (old value no end, new value 19 August), because the brigade was integral to the 49th Division from 20 August (Ellis).
  - 115th Infantry Brigade, 23 March 1945: a representative point (Xanten) on the XII Corps Rhine front, confidence 0.3; only the order of battle places it.
  - 1st Special Service Brigade, about 20 January 1945 (Blackcock): the day is approximate (no source read gives it), confidence 0.3; the 1944 relations to I Corps and the 6th Airborne Division closed on 8 September 1944 (old value no end, new value 8 September), when the brigade returned to England (Wikipedia).
  - 4th Special Service Brigade, end of November 1944: the date is taken as 30 November (Stacey says "the end of November"), confidence 0.3; the 3rd Canadian Division attachment of D-Day closed on 15 September 1944 (old value no end, new value 15 September), the day before the Dunkirk row.
  - Corps relations of the brigades start on the row dates where the sources do not date them.
- **Corrections to the planning list (infantry and commandos):** the 56th Infantry Brigade was formed on 15 February 1944 and became part of the 49th Division on 20 August 1944 (Ellis, Appendix IV; Wikipedia), so only 6 June to 20 August 1944 is in scope; the 115th Infantry Brigade arrived in North-West Europe on 12 February 1945, not in April (Wikipedia), and only Ellis's Rhine order of battle places it (TracesOfWar puts "the 115th" at Flushing, which was the 155th Brigade of the 52nd Division); the 1st Special Service Brigade returned to England on 8-9 September 1944 and came back for Blackcock in January 1945, renamed the 1st Commando Brigade.
- **2nd Canadian Armoured Brigade (7 claims, C1707 to C1713).** Le Mesnil-Patry (11 June 1944), Colombelles in Atlantic (18 July), Saint-André-sur-Orne under the 2nd Canadian Division (21 July), the Totalize start line (7 August), Calais (25 September), short of Breda under the Polish Armoured Division (27 October) and the Calcar ridge in Blockbuster (26 February 1945); one new place. The brigade's existing D-Day row (C0001) is unchanged. The II Canadian Corps relation starts at 3 p.m. on 11 July 1944, as Stacey states (p. 166). Inferred values, each annotated in the record (old value: none, the row is new, unless stated): the brigade's relation to Second Army from D-Day (CR0002) and the attachment to the 3rd Canadian Division (CR0001) are closed the day before the next row under another higher unit (old value no end, new value 10 June and 20 July 1944); the other corps and division relations start on the row dates where the sources do not date them; the 26 February 1945 attachment to the 2nd Canadian Division stands for two regiments of the brigade.
- **Corrections to the planning list (Canadian):** the Moyland woods action of 19 February 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 268) gives only that regiments of the brigade were to relieve the Guards tank battalions, with no place for the brigade, so the planned row was replaced by the Calcar ridge row of 26 February (Stacey, p. 492).
- **Semantic scenario 23 (12 expectations, 356 in all).** It checks the 56th Infantry Brigade's moves of 11-12 June 1944 and the end of its independent period, the 27th Armoured Brigade with no relation after its break-up, the 1st Special Service Brigade with no relation while in England, the 4th Special Service Brigade at Walcheren, the 2nd Canadian Armoured Brigade under II Canadian Corps and at Breda, the 4th Armoured Brigade at Verden, and the batch's first and last rows. Writing it showed that the 27th Armoured Brigade's two relations still ran on after the break-up: the I Corps relation (CR0977) now ends on 29 July 1944, stated by the break-up row C1676 (old value no end, new value 29 July 1944, reason the break-up, Ellis vol. I p. 522), and the 3rd Division attachment (CR0978) is closed on the same day as an inferred value (end between 18 and 29 July).

## cleanup-2-late-war-west: clean-up of the late-war Western Front data (29 October 2026)

Scott asked for a review and clean-up pass of the Western Front data (6 June 1944 to 8 May 1945, division level and above, all nationalities) using only the sources already in the data. The audit is `docs/review/cleanup2_audit.md`. One commit per item.

- **Duplicate places merged (4).** Four places were entered twice by different batches: Hébécrevon (Manche), Stolberg (Rhineland), Évrecy (Calvados) and Bains-les-Bains (Vosges). In each pair the older row survives; the newer row is retired in `data/place_merges.csv` (the id is not reused) and its name is kept as an alias of the survivor. Seven claims were re-pointed: the old value is the retired place, the new value is the survivor, the reason is that both rows are the same commune; each claim note says so. Coordinates did not change: for Hébécrevon, Stolberg and Bains-les-Bains the two points were identical; the two Évrecy claims of the British batch keep their own Nominatim point (about 100 m from the Wikipedia point of the survivor) with a `coord_override` that says so.
- **Operation date warning cleared (1 claim).** The 7th Armoured Division row of 8 August 1944 (Mont Pinçon, making for Condé-sur-Noireau) is labelled Operation Bluecoat, whose end date (7 August) comes from the Wikipedia infobox, while Ellis describes the Bluecoat fighting to 8 August. No value changed: the row is listed in `data/operation_exceptions.csv` with that reason, which removes one validator warning (25 to 24).
- **Confidence raised (1 claim).** The First Army (German) row of 8 September 1944, its transfer to Army Group G: old 0.5, new 0.7. Reason: the rubric gives 0.7 to an approximate place with two source families; the CMH (Lorraine Campaign p. 193) and the OKW war diary (Schramm p. 370) both give the day and both describe the army sector that the representative point (Metz, 50 km) stands for. The audit found 227 rows at 0.3 or 0.5 that cite references of two families. The notes of the 76 that state two families were read: in every other one the second family covers only the day, only the unit or only the context, gives a month-level date, or the point is a representative headquarters point (0.3 by the rubric), so none was raised. 67 pair the CMH with the World War II by Day compilation of the same CMH command-post lists, which is not a second family, so they stay. The other 84 were not read one by one; they are an open question in the audit.
- **Resolved open questions removed from the documents (Scott asked for it; documents only, no data changed).** Each was checked against a merged change, Scott's answer or the changelog before it was removed; open questions that are still unresolved were kept, and the remaining items keep their numbers. Removed:
  - `docs/roadmap.md`: the 2d French Armored Division's attachment to XV Corps (written by the French batch); XXII and XXIII Corps as placeholders (activated); the 95th Division's April corps and the 100th Division's April parent (both answered by Scott on 27 October 2026); the AT and CZ country codes (approved by Scott); the 243rd Division's destroyed flag (settled by the clean-up of 28 October 2026, in three lists); the Panzer Lehr and 716th Division conflict groups (settled on 28 October 2026; the other three groups stay open); the 353rd Division's corps (settled by note on 28 October 2026); the end of the 7th Armoured and Guards Armoured attachments to II Canadian Corps (closed by British Batch 1, two lists); extending I Corps in the British batch (done); an operation row for Tractable (added) and for Plunder (added); the 2nd Canadian Division's Boxtel reserve row (written by Canadian Batch 2); the Polish, Belgian, Dutch and Czechoslovak formations and the 11th Armoured Division's attachment to the Canadian corps (Allied contingents batch and British Batch 2, two lists); the XVIII Airborne Corps under Second Army for Plunder (British Batch 2 follow-up); the 43rd Division "Mechelen" row (written as Megchelen); a second British batch (done); the Astonia, Infatuate, Pheasant and Clipper operations (added).
  - `docs/HANDOFF.md`: merging and deleting the handoff and October open-items branches (only `main` exists on GitHub); the list of 27 unfilled US placeholders and the question whether other nations get rows (all done, each batch approved by Scott); the quarterly batch split (both batches approved and merged); where the "Model to 14 September" date came from (settled by the German Batch 2 follow-up: the data never had it).
  - `docs/review/verification_results.md`: the four relations "waiting for Scott" and the list of "new decisions pending" (all decided and applied on 26 October 2026; the decisions themselves stay recorded in the items above them).
  - Kept because still open: the corps that the CMH table entries "X" and "XIV" meant, XXII and XXIII Corps in April and May, the three open German conflict groups, the 243rd Division dissolution row (not approved), combat commands, the commanders table, the outside-review questions, the licence, the 43rd Division's move to VIII Corps on 2 September 1944, and the other open points with their recommendations.

## french-followup-1944-45: de Lattre pass (29 October 2026)

Same unmerged branch `french-followup-1944-45` (head before the pass `a7113df`; `main` `941b8b0` unchanged). Scott approved using Jean de Lattre de Tassigny, *The History of the French First Army* (trans. Malcolm Barnes, Allen & Unwin 1952; archive.org `bwb_W7-ADK-972`, borrow-only). The book was not re-opened: the evidence is the research notes taken from its OCR text layer (about 335 lines, printed pp. 63-525, gap at p. ~263), each line's quote and printed page. A fact only in a note's paraphrase columns, or only in a truncated or garbled quote, is not used on its own; OCR corrections are stated in the row (`ist` = `1st` in CR0959).

### References and documents

- **`R686`** (new): de Lattre, *The History of the French First Army* (1952); `source_type` `unit_history`, `source_family` `delattre_french_first_army` (its own family, independent of CMH and Wikipedia). Now cited by 6 claims.
- **Research notes**: the notes taken from the book (with a header giving citation, method and known gaps) are kept privately by the project owner (Drive, WWII Unit Locations folder), not in this repository; they were briefly committed on this branch and removed in a later commit. `docs/sources.md`: one row for the source.

### Claims

- **`C1644`** (9th DIC, Toulon, 27 Aug 1944): confidence 0.5 to 0.7. de Lattre pp. 76, 92-93 (St Catherine fort 24 August; Ruhfus's surrender 27 August 23.45) is a second family for the city and day; the quotes do not name the division, the note line does.
- **`C1633`** (5th DB, Stuttgart, 21 Apr 1945): confidence 0.3 to 0.5. de Lattre pp. 460-466: "when Stuttgart fell on the 21st April"; the link of the day to the division rests on the note's summary, so not 0.7.
- **`C1634`** (1st DFL, Lyon, 3 Sep 1944): de Lattre p. 128 (08.00 on 3 September) added as a third family; stays 0.7 (city, 10 km).
- **`C1637`** (2nd DIM, Belfort, 25 Nov 1944): de Lattre pp. 243-246 has Belfort fallen by 21 November; Review note, date and 0.7 unchanged (not reconciled).
- **`C1656`** (new, 3rd DIA, Strasbourg, 5 Jan 1945, 0.5): de Lattre pp. 309, 312 and CMH *Riviera to the Rhine* pp. 517, 522, 527.
- **`C1657`** (new, 1st DB, Ulm, 23 Apr 1945, 0.3): CMH *The Last Offensive* p. 431 (French platoon outside Ulm at dusk) and de Lattre pp. 482, 485-486; attribution to the division inferred. New place `PL0851` Ulm (OpenStreetMap).

### Relations

- **`CR0942`** (2DB under the Seventh Army) and **`CR0953`** (2DB attached to the XV Corps): old valid_to 1945-01-27 (inferred); new 1945-01-18 (narrative): de Lattre p. 373, the combat commands Dio and Langlade left the US Seventh Army on 19 January (two of three; the third is not dated). `C1647` now `asserts_end` for both.
- **`CR0938`** (2DB under the First French Army): old valid_from 1945-01-28 (claim date); new 1945-01-19 (narrative, de Lattre p. 373; `C1648` `asserts_start`).
- **`CR0958`** (new): 2DB under the French II Corps from 28 January 1945 (claim date; CMH p. 548 "leaving Leclerc's 2d Armored Division with de Monsabert"; de Lattre pp. 352, 369-371); end unknown, earliest 8 February. No XXI Corps relation was added: the note for p. 394 puts the XXI Corps link only in its paraphrase and the CMH history leaves the division with the II Corps.
- **`CR0959`** (new): 14th DI under the I Corps from 23 April 1945 (de Lattre p. 479, OCR `ist` read as `1st`; p. 459), asserted by `C1655`.
- **`CR0960`** (new): 3rd DIA under the II Corps from 5 January 1945 (de Lattre p. 312); end inferred (day before the Speyer row), unknown.
- Notes only: `CR0951`, `CR0952` confirmed (de Lattre pp. 286, 287, 302); `CR0946` confirmed (p. 123); `CR0947` kept at 1 September, with de Lattre's "officially went into action at midnight of the 5th to 6th September" (p. 134) recorded; `CR0956` consistent (p. 406).

### Not done (and why)

- 1st DFL to the Alps army detachment from 1 March 1945 (p. 405-406): no 1st DFL row after January 1945 and no place in the quote, so no relation can be anchored; open point.
- I Corps activation (5/6 Sep) and II Corps (1 Sep) as claims: no place in the quotes; recorded on `CR0947`/`CR0946` instead.
- 5th DB at Bregenz (p. 498), 4th DMM at Rouffach (pp. 388-390), 9th DIC at Ensisheim (p. 396), 2nd DB near Obernai-Marlenheim in January (p. 331): the quote does not name the place or the unit, or is truncated.

### Scripts

- **`scripts/semantic_tests.py`:** scenario 21 updated (2DB on 1 Feb 1945 now also under the II Corps; C1633 now 0.5); new scenario 22, de Lattre pass: 7 expectations. Total: 344 expectations hold. No other script changed.

## french-1944-45: the French formations (29 October 2026)

New branch `french-1944-45` from `main` (`b021dc2`). It covers the Western Front, 6 June 1944 to 8 May 1945, division level and above; Italy is not covered. Sources: the CMH histories (Blumenson, *Breakout and Pursuit*; Cole, *The Lorraine Campaign*; Clarke and Smith, *Riviera to the Rhine*; MacDonald, *The Last Offensive*) and the Wikipedia unit and battle articles. Five references are new: `R677` (Riviera to the Rhine ch. 30), `R678` (ch. 2), `R679` (ch. 12), `R680` (Wikipedia, 1st Armored Division (France)) and `R681` (Wikipedia, 5th Armored Division (France)). The eleven units were placeholders and are promoted by `promote_placeholders.py`. The nationality folder `data/claims/france` is new. De Lattre's history was not consulted in this pass and is not cited.

### Claims and relations

- **2d French Armored Division (Leclerc):**
  - 12 claims, `C1608` to `C1619`: le Mans (9 August 1944), Ecouche, the Ecouche-Argentan line, Rambouillet, Paris (25 August), Dompaire, north of Rambervillers, Strasbourg (23 November), Erstein, Fessenheim (8 February 1945), Royan (18 April) and Bad Reichenhall (4 May).
  - Corps: `CR0934` XV Corps, attached, 9 to 17 August 1944 (end inferred, earliest 13 August); `CR0935` V Corps, attached, 18 August (first row) to 7 September; `CR0936` XV Corps, attached, 8 September to 26 November (Lorraine p. 185; Riviera p. 454); `CR0937` VI Corps, attached, from 27 November 1944 (end inferred: 7 February 1945, earliest 28 November).
  - Armies (unspecified_subordination, a French division under American command): `CR0939` Third Army, 9 to 17 August 1944 (end inferred); `CR0940` First Army, 18 August to 7 September; `CR0941` Third Army, 8 to 28 September; `CR0942` Seventh Army, from 29 September 1944 (Riviera p. 254; end inferred: 7 February 1945, earliest 28 November); `CR0938` First French Army, from 8 February 1945 (first row; end inferred: 17 April 1945).
  - The Royan and Bad Reichenhall rows have no parent: de Larminat's French Forces of the West are not a unit, and the Last Offensive p. 442 says only "recently attached".
- **First French Army (Army B):** 5 claims, `C1620` to `C1624`: Toulon (20 and 28 August 1944), the activation of the 6th Army Group (15 September, at a representative point, Besancon, 0.3), Karlsruhe (4 April 1945) and Stuttgart (22 April). Relations: `CR0943` Seventh Army, unspecified_subordination, 20 August (first row) to 14 September 1944; `CR0944` Seventh Army, operational_control, 15 to 19 September (Riviera p. 224: Patch directed First French Army operations until 19 September); `CR0945` 6th Army Group, assigned, from 15 September 1944, open.

## allied-contingents-1944-45: the Polish, Czechoslovak, Belgian and Dutch formations (29 October 2026)

New branch `allied-contingents-1944-45` from `main` (`85c5c48`). It covers the Western Front, 6 June 1944 to 8 May 1945; Italy is not covered. Sources: Stacey (`R668`), Ellis vol. I and II (`R670`, `R671`) and the Wikipedia unit articles (`R035`, `R037`, `R039`, `R144`), plus two new Wikipedia references: `R675` (Siege of Dunkirk) and `R676` (Princess Irene Brigade). The five units were placeholders and are promoted by `promote_placeholders.py`. Four nationality folders are new under `data/claims/`: `poland`, `czechoslovakia`, `belgium` and `netherlands`. Each unit is its own commit.

### Claims and relations

- **1st Polish Armoured Division:**
  - 33 claims, `C1547` to `C1579`: 8 August 1944 (Totalize) to 6 May 1945 (Wilhelmshaven). Confidence: 9 at 0.9, 20 at 0.7, 3 at 0.5, 1 at 0.3.
  - Uses the existing `CR0853` (II Canadian Corps, 5 August to 28 September 1944).
  - New `CR0923`: I Corps, attached, from 28 September 1944. The end is inferred: 7 April 1945, earliest 7 January. Ellis p. 285 has the division under Netherlands District, which is not a unit, and the change is undated.
  - New `CR0924`: II Canadian Corps, attached, from 8 April 1945, open.
  - New `CR0925`: First Canadian Army, unspecified_subordination, from 5 August 1944 (inferred from Stacey p. 208), open (Stacey p. 618: it left Crerar's command in mid-June 1945).
- **Polish Parachute Brigade:**
  - 5 claims, `C1580` to `C1584`: Oosterbeek (gliders), Driel (the drop, the crossing and Horrocks's visit) and Nijmegen, 19 to 26 September 1944.
  - New `CR0926`: 1st Airborne Division, attached, 17 to 26 September 1944. Stacey p. 313 says "under command". Both dates are inferred.
- **Czechoslovak Armoured Brigade Group:**
  - 5 claims, `C1585` to `C1589`: Falaise on 30 August 1944, then Dunkirk on 9 October, 28 October, 27 November and 8 May 1945. The last date is representative, at 0.3.
  - New `CR0927`: 21st Army Group, unspecified_subordination, from 30 August 1944, open.
  - New `CR0928`: First Canadian Army, attached, 9 October to 27 November 1944 (Stacey p. 368).
- **Belgian (Piron) Brigade:**
  - 10 claims, `C1590` to `C1599`: the Normandy coast, Brussels, Leopoldsburg, Thorn and Leuven, then Opheusden on 18 April 1945.
  - New `CR0929`: First Canadian Army, 13 August to 1 September 1944 (Stacey pp. 265 and 323).
  - New `CR0930`: Second Army, from 2 September 1944. The end is inferred: 11 April 1945, earliest 17 November 1944.
  - New `CR0931`: I Canadian Corps, from 12 April 1945 (Stacey p. 570; the 1st Canadian Armoured Brigade is not a unit). All three are unspecified_subordination.
- **Princess Irene (Royal Netherlands) Brigade:**
  - 8 claims, `C1600` to `C1607`: Graye-sur-Mer, the Normandy coast, Beringen, Borkel, the Nijmegen bridges (Ellis II p. 42, note), Grave, Broekhoven (Pheasant) and Hedel on 25 April 1945, which has no parent.
  - New `CR0932`: First Canadian Army, 13 August to 1 September 1944.
  - New `CR0933`: Second Army, 2 September 1944 to 1 March 1945. The end is inferred: Wikipedia says Netherlands District took over on 2 March.
- **Places:** 41 new, `PL0786` to `PL0826`.
- **Claim totals:** 61 (Poland 38, Belgium 10, Netherlands 8, Czechoslovakia 5). Confidence: 11 at 0.9, 26 at 0.7, 19 at 0.5, 5 at 0.3.

### Changed values on existing records (old value, new value, reason; each also in the record note)

- **`CR0892` (Belgian brigade under the 6th Airborne Division):**
  - Start: 1944-08-21 (basis claim_date, inferred) changed to 1944-08-13 (basis narrative), because Stacey p. 265 dates the start.
  - End: blank (open_at_last_claim, end unknown) changed to 1944-08-27 (narrative, end_unknown false), because Wikipedia places the brigade under the 49th Division on 28 August.
  - date_basis: inferred changed to narrative.
- **`CR0893` (Princess Irene Brigade under the 6th Airborne Division):**
  - Start: 1944-08-21 changed to 1944-08-13 (narrative), because Stacey p. 265 dates the start.
  - End: blank (open) changed to 1944-09-01 (inferred_from_next_claim, earliest 1944-08-21), because the brigade passed to the Second Army on 2 September.

### Scripts (flag for Scott)

## british-batch2-jan-may-1945, follow-up: the units not covered, and the XVIII Airborne Corps (28 October 2026)

Follow-up commits on the same branch `british-batch2-jan-may-1945` (Scott on 28 October 2026 accepted the Batch 2 recommendations, including the one-line `validate.py` change, and approved a deeper pass; the branch was intact on `origin` at `fbc3875`, not merged; no new branch, no force-push). Sources beyond Ellis: Stacey (`R668`), MacDonald, *The Last Offensive* ch. 14 (`R543`) and ch. 16 (`R566`), and two pages of Stichting Opdat Wij Niet Vergeten (`R673`, `R674`, ownv.nl). Nafziger (generalstaff.org) is blocked to the box by Cloudflare (403); only search snippets were reachable and nothing from it is cited.

### Task 1, claims and relations (each item its own commit)

- **50th Division (`C1539`, `C1540`, `C1541`; `CR0918`; places `PL0782` Neerpelt, `PL0783` Elst):** 17 September 1944 at Neerpelt (0.3: Ellis vol. II p. 32 places only the heavy mortars and one battalion at the bridgehead), 1 October on the Island (0.5; the date is the first day of the attacks, inferred; Ellis p. 98 names no place and Elst is a representative point), 9 November on the Island under II Canadian Corps (0.5; Stacey pp. 428, 430; Ellis p. 159). `CR0918` attaches the division to II Canadian Corps from 9 November (narrative) to 29 November (stated by `C1541`: Ellis p. 159 "On the 29th it was moved back to Belgium", month inferred as November from Stacey p. 430 and Ellis p. 376). Commander of `C1541` is `unknown` (Stacey names Graham, Ellis lists Lyne). The 50th has no row for 29 November or December 1944 ("Belgium" is not a place).
- **3rd Division (`C1542`, `C1543`; `CR0919`; place `PL0784` Well):** 19 January 1945, the Maas front between Venlo and Boxmeer, last day under II Canadian Corps (0.5, precision 25 km; Stacey p. 443, Ellis pp. 238, 240); 25 February at Weeze, relieving the 15th Division in XXX Corps (0.5; Stacey p. 494, Ellis pp. 271, 273). New `CR0919`: 3rd Division in VIII Corps from 3 September 1944 (Ellis vol. II p. 4, note) to 24 February 1945 (end inferred from the next row).
- **43rd Division (`C1544`; place `PL0785` Megchelen; references `R673`, `R674`):** 28 March 1945, 0.7. The "Mechelen" of Ellis p. 293 is the Dutch village of Megchelen (identification from Ellis's sequence and two ownv.nl pages that give the 43rd (Wessex) Division in Megchelen on the morning of 28 March); the row says so in its Context note.
- **49th Division (`C1545`; `CR0920`):** 4 December 1944 on the Island (0.5, Stacey pp. 430, 433, one family). `CR0920` attaches the division to II Canadian Corps from 30 November (start read from "the end of November", latest 2 December) to 14 March 1945 (inferred; I Canadian Corps takes the division at noon on 15 March, Stacey p. 545).
- **59th Division (no claim):** `CR0882` (XII Corps) closed on 23 August 1944, earliest 6 August, basis `inferred_from_next_claim` (Ellis vol. I p. 453: XII Corps "had to shed the 59th Division, unhappily selected for disbandment" and is well on its way by the 24th). No place, so no row.
- **Not written, with reasons:** the 1st Airborne Division (no place and date after Arnhem in the sources read), the 79th Armoured Division (specialist formation; no division-level place or headquarters), the 59th (above), the 50th on 29 November and in December 1944, and any parent for `C1482` (it stays blank; the relations carry the chain).

### Task 2, the one US claim (own commit)

- **`C1546` (US-ABN-018C, 24 March 1945, 0.3, place `PL0437` Diersfordt, parent `UK-ARMY-002A`, `OP-VARSITY`):** the XVIII Airborne Corps controlling the 6th British and 17th US Airborne Divisions for Plunder and Varsity (Ellis vol. II p. 285; MacDonald ch. 14 pp. 298-300, 309, 310; ch. 16 pp. 357, 362, 365). The point is the corps objective (the Diersfordter Forst), not the headquarters (on the west bank of the Rhine, no place named), so 0.3.
- **`CR0921`:** XVIII Airborne Corps attached to Second Army from 9 March ("As of 9 March", CMH ch. 14 p. 298) to 1 April 1945 (stated by `C1546` from ch. 16 pp. 357, 362; read as the day before `CR0922`).
- **`CR0922`:** XVIII Airborne Corps under the US First Army (operational control) from 2 April 1945 (latest 5 April; CMH ch. 16 p. 362, the corps attacks under First Army on 6 April, p. 365), open. It continues `CR0085` after the Second Army attachment. `C1546` states its start, which gives one expected validator warning (the start is after the row date; see the row's Context note).

### Changed values on existing records (old value, new value, reason; each in the record note)

- **`CR0070` (3rd Division in I Corps):** valid_to 1945-02-28 becomes 1944-09-02 (earliest 1944-07-18 unchanged). Ellis vol. II pp. 4, 159, 238 have the division in VIII Corps from 3 September 1944; the day of the change is not dated.
- **`CR0905` (3rd Division in XXX Corps):** valid_from 1945-03-01 becomes 1945-02-25 (Stacey p. 494; Ellis p. 271).
- **`CR0862` (3rd Division attached to II Canadian Corps):** note only; the sentence that the division stays assigned to I Corps is replaced by VIII Corps (`CR0919`).
- **`CR0882` (59th Division in XII Corps):** no end becomes valid_to 1944-08-23 (above).
- **`CR0085` (XVIII Airborne Corps under First Army):** no end becomes valid_to 1945-03-08 (earliest 1944-12-19), because the corps was attached to Second Army from 9 March.
- **`CR0909` and `C1508` (6th Airborne Division, notes only):** the chain on 24 March 1945 changes from XVIII Airborne Corps, US First Army, 12th Army Group, SHAEF to XVIII Airborne Corps, British Second Army (`CR0921`), 21st Army Group, SHAEF (CMH ch. 14 p. 298; Ellis p. 285). CMH ch. 16 p. 357 plans for the British units to pass to Second Army at the end of March, which may end `CR0909` earlier than 16 April; the end is left as it is and says so.
- **`C1482` (49th Division, Zetten, 18 January 1945):** the row is unchanged; links to `CR0888` (I Corps, standing) and `CR0920` (II Canadian Corps) added, with a note.

### Tests, checks and counts

- **`scripts/semantic_tests.py`**: scenario 18 added (17 expectations: the 3rd Division in VIII Corps, attached to II Canadian Corps and in XXX Corps from 25 February; the 50th and 49th Divisions attached to II Canadian Corps; the 59th Division in XII Corps until 23 August; the XVIII Airborne Corps under Second Army on 24 March and under First Army on 10 April; the 43rd Division in XXX Corps on 28 March; the first and last row of the follow-up). 301 expectations in all.

Next free ids: `C1547`, `CR0923`, `PL0786`, `R675`, `G028`.
- **Checks:** `validate` OK (264 claim files, 1,546 claims, 367 units, 24 conflict groups; 20 warnings: the 19 known and the `C1546` one above); `semantic_tests` OK (301 expectations); the full set as listed in the HANDOFF. who_controls grids before and after: 214 of 10,860 answers changed in the standard grid, 138 of 2,469 in the extended grid (12 March to 7 May 1945) and 207 of 2,958 in a new grid for 1 January to 11 March 1945; all explained in `grid_british_batch2.md` (follow-up section). No new keys. ## british-batch2-jan-may-1945: British Batch 2, 22 October 1944 to 4 May 1945 (28 October 2026)

Branch `british-batch2-jan-may-1945`, cut from the British Batch 1 head (`9b4c775`, 1,468 claims, 367 units, 24 conflict groups, 262 semantic expectations); compare it with `main` (`https://github.com/scottstarsman/UnitLocationData/compare/main...british-batch2-jan-may-1945`). Task: British (UK) Army units on the Western Front, 1 January to 8 May 1945, division level and above; same method, scope, sources and rules as British Batch 1 and Canadian Batch 2 (Ellis, *Victory in the West* vol. II, `R671`, with Stacey, `R668`, for the five operations); Scott on 28 October 2026: "Let's start British 45".

### Item 1: operations, a reference and six re-pointed rows

- **Reference `R672` (`data/references_meta.csv`, regenerated into `data/references.csv`):** Wikipedia, Operation Pheasant (end date and the name only; Ellis does not name it).
- **Operations `OP-ASTONIA` (10 to 12 September 1944), `OP-INFATUATE` (1 to 8 November 1944), `OP-PHEASANT` (20 October to 4 November 1944), `OP-BLACKCOCK` (16 to 26 January 1945), `OP-PLUNDER` (23 to 27 March 1945)** appended to `data/operations.csv`, with `operation_relations` rows `OP-VARSITY` supports `OP-PLUNDER`, `OP-PHEASANT` supports `OP-SCHELDT`, `OP-INFATUATE` supports `OP-SCHELDT` (a battle may not be the parent of an operation, so `OP-INFATUATE` has the campaign `OP-CAMP-RHINELAND` as parent). The end of Plunder is inferred and says so in `notes`. `OP-CLIPPER` already existed.
- **`C1459`, `C1460`, `C1461` (British Batch 1, Le Havre), column `operation_id`: changed.** Old value: `OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE`. New value: `OP-ASTONIA`. Reason: Stacey p. 331 names Astonia as the three-day operation against Le Havre in the second week of September 1944.
- **`C1329` (`CAN-INF-002D`), `C1467` (`UK-INF-052D`), `C1036` (`GER-INF-070D`), column `operation_id`: changed.** Old value: `OP-SCHELDT`. New value: `OP-INFATUATE`. Reason: all three describe the Walcheren assault of 1 to 8 November (Stacey p. 407). `C1283` (8 November, Canadian Army) stays under `OP-SCHELDT`. A `Review (British Batch 2, 28 October 2026; ...)` sentence in each note gives the old value, the new value and the reason; a Stacey reference was added to each.

### Items 2 to 6: claims and relations

- **Claims `C1469` to `C1538` (70):** 1944 (flagged additions to Batch 1, `C1469` to `C1472`: XII Corps on 22 October and the 53rd Division on 27 October for Pheasant, XXX Corps and the 43rd Division on 18 November for Clipper); January 1945 `C1473` to `C1482` (the Ardennes counter-attack at Marche, Bure and La Roche, Blackcock from 16 January, 49th Division at Zetten); February and March `C1483` to `C1503` (Veritable, Goch, Udem, Kervenheim, Weeze, Alpen, Blockbuster, the end of the Rhineland battle); the Rhine crossing `C1504` to `C1510` (Plunder and Varsity); April and May `C1511` to `C1538` (Lingen, Osnabruck and Hannover, Celle and Belsen, Bremen, the Elbe at Lauenburg, Luebeck, Wismar, Travemuende, Hamburg and the surrender on Lueneburg Heath). Confidence 0.7 for 45, 0.5 for 22, 0.3 for 3 (`C1483` and `C1502`, XXX Corps headquarters on 7 February and 8 March, and `C1511`, Second Army on 28 March; all three are representative points), all from Ellis, one family.
- **By unit:** 15th Division 8, XXX Corps 7, 53rd Division 7, 11th Armoured 6, 43rd Division 6, 52nd Division 6, 51st Division 5, 7th Armoured 5, 6th Airborne 4, Guards Armoured 4, XII Corps 3, 3rd Division 3, 21st Army Group 2, VIII Corps 2, 49th Division 1, Second Army 1. No unit was activated (all were already active).

- **References `R669`, `R670`, `R671` (`data/references_meta.csv`, regenerated into `data/references.csv`):** Wikipedia, Operation Bluecoat; Ellis, *Victory in the West* vol. I (HMSO 1962; archive.org full text); Ellis vol. II (HMSO 1968).
- **Operations `OP-TRACTABLE` (14 to 21 August 1944, parent `OP-FALAISE`) and `OP-BLUECOAT` (30 July to 7 August, parent `OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE`)** appended to `data/operations.csv`. Tractable is the Canadian Batch 1 deferred item; the end follows the closing of the Falaise Gap and the Bluecoat end and name come from Wikipedia (Ellis does not name it); both are inferred values and say so in `notes`.

### Item 2: three Canadian rows re-pointed (changed values)

- **`C1291` (`CAN-COR-002C`), `C1303` (`CAN-INF-003D`), `C1334` (`CAN-ARM-004D`), column `operation_id`: changed.** Old value: `OP-FALAISE`. New value: `OP-TRACTABLE`. Reason: all three describe 14 August 1944 (the first day of Tractable, Stacey pp. 238-241 and Ellis I p. 430); the other Canadian Falaise rows were not changed. A `Review (British Batch 1, 28 October 2026; ...)` sentence in each note gives the old value, the new value and the reason.

### Items 3 to 6: claims and relations

- **Claims `C1408` to `C1468` (61):** July `C1408` to `C1433` (26: Charnwood, Jupiter, the Odon preliminaries, Goodwood, Bluecoat); August `C1434` to `C1456` (23: Bluecoat and Mont Pincon, 21st Army Group and XXX Corps command changes of 4 August, Tractable flank, the Falaise pursuit, the Seine crossings, Amiens and the Somme, Montgomery promoted Field-Marshal on 1 September); September to December `C1457` to `C1468` (12: Brussels and Antwerp, Le Havre, Market Garden with I Airborne Corps and the 1st Airborne Division, the 52nd Division at Walcheren, XXX Corps in the Ardennes). Confidence 0.7 for 40, 0.5 for 19, 0.3 for 2 (`C1423`, `C1456`); all from Ellis, one family.
- **Inferred values (all annotated in the claim or relation notes):** the claim dates are the days Ellis gives except `C1443` (6th Airborne at Troarn: Ellis I p. 448 gives no day; 21 August is the latest possible day), `C1468` (20 December is the day Montgomery took control of the northern battlefield; the order is earlier), `C1466` (the withdrawal from Arnhem at night, 25-26 September, Ellis II pp. 58 and 97 differ by a day), the closing of `CR0883` (29 August, Ellis I p. 467) and the start of `CR0891` (52nd Division attached to the First Canadian Army, claim date 3 November; Ellis II p. 106 has a brigade relieving Canadians from 18 October).
- **New relations `CR0873` to `CR0893` (21):** I Corps, XII Corps, VIII Corps, XXX Corps and Second Army standing relations of the divisions and corps (assigned, from the first British row in the new place), `CR0883` (7th Armoured Division attached to I Corps from 16 August to 29 August), `CR0888` (49th Division assigned to I Corps from 10 September), two attached relations of the Belgian and Netherlands brigades to the 6th Airborne Division (listed by `C1443`), the 1st Airborne Division, I Airborne Corps and the 52nd Division relations.
- **`CR0060`, `CR0063`, `CR0072`, `CR0074`, `CR0076`: closed as inferred values.** Old value: `valid_to` empty, basis `open_at_last_claim`. New value: `valid_to` the day before the first row of the next higher unit (for example `CR0060` 1944-07-18), basis `inferred_from_next_claim`. Reason: the unit's next row names another corps and the sources read do not date the change; the relation note carries the same text ("The old value is ... The new value is ... The reason is ...").
- **`CR0850` and `CR0851` (7th Armoured and Guards Armoured Divisions attached to II Canadian Corps from 20 July): closed.** Old value: `valid_to` empty, basis `open_at_last_claim`, end unknown. New value: `valid_to` 1944-07-30, `valid_to_earliest` 1944-07-25, basis `inferred_from_next_claim`, end unknown. Reason: Ellis I p. 378 has both divisions attacking with II Canadian Corps on 25 July and p. 388 puts them in XXX Corps and VIII Corps reserve for Bluecoat on 30 July; the day of the end is not dated, so the day of the next operation is the latest possible end.
- **Added to `data/command_relation_claims.csv`:** 64 evidence links. `CR0883` is evidenced by the I Corps row `C1442` through `listed_by_higher_unit` (`composing_units` of the 7th Armoured Division, start stated 16 August) and the two brigade relations by `C1443`.
- **Places:** 27 new, `PL0722` to `PL0748` (geocoded with Nominatim, place centres; precision 3 to 20 km), including Mont Pincon, Evrecy, Aunay-sur-Odon, Vernon, Amiens, Brussels, Valkenswaard, Wolfheze and Tienen.
- **Units activated (`data/units.csv`, `record_status` placeholder to active):** `UK-COR-012C` (XII Corps), `UK-ABN-001C` (I Airborne Corps), `UK-ABN-001D` (1st Airborne Division), `UK-INF-052D` (52nd Division).
- **Not written (stated scope):** the Polish Armoured Division to I Corps from 28 September (Stacey p. 367), the Polish Parachute Brigade at Arnhem and the Czechoslovak brigade at Dunkirk (no claim of those units exists to evidence the relations); the 43rd Division's move to VIII Corps on 2 September; the 243rd Division German row (deferred earlier); October 1944 to May 1945 for the British formations.
