## canadian-batch2-jan-may-1945: Canadian Batch 2, January to May 1945 (28 October 2026)

Branch `canadian-batch2-jan-may-1945`, cut from `main` (`92e5f82`, 1,342 claims, 367 units, 24 conflict groups, 221 semantic expectations); compare it with `main` (`https://github.com/scottstarsman/UnitLocationData/compare/main...canadian-batch2-jan-may-1945`). Task approved by Scott on 28 October 2026 (Canadian Batch 2: Canadian Army units on the Western Front, 1 January to 8 May 1945, division level and above; same method, scope, sources and rules as Canadian Batch 1; the 2nd Division at Boxtel of 29 December 1944 as a deferred first row). One source family only (Stacey, `R668`), so no row is at 0.9. Italy is not written: I Canadian Corps, the 1st Division and the 5th Armoured Division appear only from their arrival in the Western Front theatre.

### Item 1: operations and the scope of R668

- **Three operations** appended to `data/operations.csv`: `OP-ELEPHANT` (26 to 31 January 1945, parent `OP-CAMP-RHINELAND`), `OP-VERITABLE` (8 February to 10 March, parent `OP-CAMP-RHINELAND`; the end follows the casualty period of Stacey p. 522, no single closing day is named) and `OP-BLOCKBUSTER` (phase, 26 February to 10 March, parent `OP-VERITABLE`; the end follows Veritable, Stacey names no separate end). One row in `data/operation_relations.csv`: `OP-VERITABLE` concurrent with `OP-GRENADE`.
- **`R668` (`data/references.csv`), column `used_for`: changed.** Old value: the text ending "6 June 1944 to 31 December 1944" (scope as of Canadian Batch 1). New value: the same text ending "6 June 1944 to 8 May 1945". Reason: Stacey is now used for January to May 1945.

### Items 2 to 4: claims and relations

- **Claims `C1343` to `C1407` (65):** First Canadian Army `C1343` to `C1348` (6); II Canadian Corps `C1349` to `C1360` (12); I Canadian Corps `C1361` to `C1366` (6, from 15 March); 2nd Division `C1367` to `C1378` (12, including `C1367`, the deferred row of 29 December 1944: the 4th Brigade Group only, at Boxtel, confidence 0.3); 3rd Division `C1379` to `C1388` (10); 4th Armoured Division `C1389` to `C1396` (8); 1st Division `C1397` to `C1401` (5, from 3 April); 5th Armoured Division `C1402` to `C1407` (6, from the last days of February). New claim files `CAN-COR-001C.csv`, `CAN-INF-001D.csv`, `CAN-ARM-005D.csv`; the placeholders `CAN-COR-001C`, `CAN-INF-001D`, `CAN-ARM-005D` became active (260 active, 107 placeholders). Commanders from Appendix G (Crerar, Simonds, Foulkes, Matthews, Spry then Keefler, Vokes, Foster, Hoffmeister).

Polish, Belgian, Dutch and Czech attachments are not written (British and Polish batch).
- **`CR0845` (I Corps under the Army, assigned): closed.** Old value: `valid_to` empty, basis `open_at_last_claim`. New value: `valid_to` 1945-04-02, time 12:00, basis `narrative`. Reason: Stacey p. 545 (the 1st British Corps returned to General Dempsey command at noon on 2 April). Annotated in the relation note.
- **`CR0847` (II Canadian Corps under the Army, assigned): closed.** Old value: `valid_to` empty, basis `open_at_last_claim`. New value: `valid_to` 1945-03-20, no hour, basis `narrative`. Reason: Stacey p. 531 (the corps passed under the complete operational command of Second Army on 20 March; the hour is not given). Annotated in the relation note; the new relation `CR0860` starts at 23:59 on 1 April (p. 545).
- **`CR0857` (4th Armoured Division, Army Reserve): closed.** Old value: `valid_to` empty, basis `open_at_last_claim`, end unknown. New value: `valid_to` 1945-01-25, basis `inferred_from_next_claim`, end unknown, the end lying between 23 December 1944 and 25 January 1945 (the division was under I Corps again from 26 January). Reason: the next claim of the division, `C1389` of 26 January 1945 (Operation Elephant, Stacey pp. 452-453), places it under I Corps and not in Army Reserve; the day Army Reserve ended is not stated. Existing places reused: Nijmegen, Tilburg, Arnhem, Kleve, Rees, Oldenburg, Utrecht, Antwerp, Boxtel.

## canadian-batch1-jun-dec-1944: Canadian Batch 1, July to December 1944 (28 October 2026)

Branch `canadian-batch1-jun-dec-1944`, cut from `main` (`259f572`, 1,277 claims, 367 units, 24 conflict groups, 201 semantic expectations); compare it with `main` (`https://github.com/scottstarsman/UnitLocationData/compare/main...canadian-batch1-jun-dec-1944`). Task approved by Scott on 28 October 2026 ("Let's leave Italy out. We'll do that as a separate theater. Please proceed with the 1944 Canadians"). Scope: First Canadian Army, II Canadian Corps and the 2nd, 3rd and 4th Canadian Divisions (infantry and armoured) from 4 July to 31 December 1944. Not covered: I Canadian Corps, the 5th Canadian Armoured Division, the 1st Canadian Division, independent and armoured brigades, Italy. Attached British, Polish and US formations appear only as command relations.

### Item 1: reference and operations

- **Reference `R668`**: Stacey, The Victory Campaign (Official History of the Canadian Army, Vol. III, canada.ca PDF), source type `official_history`, family `canada_ca`, accessed and checked 28 October 2026. Printed page numbers are cited.
- **Six operations** appended to `data/operations.csv` (not re-sorted): `OP-ATLANTIC` (18 to 21 July, parent `OP-CAMP-NORMANDY`), `OP-SPRING` (25 July, `OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE`), `OP-TOTALIZE` (7 to 10 August, `OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE`), `OP-WELLHIT` (17 to 22 September, `OP-CAMP-RHINELAND`), `OP-UNDERGO` (25 September to 1 October, `OP-CAMP-RHINELAND`), `OP-SWITCHBACK` (6 October to 3 November, a phase of `OP-SCHELDT`). Three rows in `data/operation_relations.csv`: Atlantic concurrent with Goodwood, Spring follows Atlantic, Totalize follows Spring. No `OP-TRACTABLE`: the Tractable claims use `OP-FALAISE`.
- **`schema/vocabularies.json`** (`operation_date_basis`, `official_history`): old text "Dates from an official history: a US Army Green Book or CMH publication."; new text adds "or a national official history such as the Canadian Army official history (Stacey, The Victory Campaign)". Reason: the six new operations take their dates from Stacey.

### Item 2: First Canadian Army, II Canadian Corps and I Corps

- **Claims:** `C1279` to `C1285` (Army, 7), `C1286` to `C1295` (II Canadian Corps, 10), and `C1278` (I Corps, 23 July: a minimal command-change row that exists only so that a higher-unit claim ends `CR0067` and starts `CR0845`). Reason: Stacey p. 196 (the front held by the corps passed to First Canadian Army at noon on 23 July) and p. 198 (the corps served under the Army). Annotated in the relation note.

### Item 3: 3rd Canadian Infantry Division

- **Claims:** `C1296` to `C1315` (20 rows, 4 July to 13 November; Carpiquet, Caen, Colombelles, Tilly-la-Campagne, Rouvres, Point 168, Trun, Rouen, Boulogne, Calais, the Leopold Canal, Hoofdplaat, Breskens, Nijmegen). Reason: Stacey p. 166 (II Canadian Corps took over the Caen front at 15:00 on 11 July with the 3rd Division under command); the division passes to `CR0849`. Annotated in the relation note.

## cleanup-open-items-oct28: clean-up of open items (28 October 2026)

Branch `cleanup-open-items-oct28`, cut from `main` (`af8ae06`, 1,277 claims, 367 units, 24 conflict groups, 194 semantic expectations); compare it with `main` (`https://github.com/scottstarsman/UnitLocationData/compare/main...cleanup-open-items-oct28`). Task approved by Scott on 28 October 2026 (clean-up task 1: the open conflict groups `G021` to `G025`, the 243rd Division, the parent of the 353rd Division, the stray file `WorldWar2/before.txt`). Every change below lists old value, new value and reason; the claims were not deleted and no claim was added.

### Item 1: the open conflict groups `G021` to `G025`

Read: HANDOFF and roadmap entries, the claim rows of each group, and the sources again (Lexikon der Wehrmacht pages of the divisions, corps and Army Group B, the Nafziger file 944BGAA, Breakout and Pursuit ch. 7, Riviera to the Rhine ch. 4, Wikipedia). Rule used: a group is settled only where the sources clearly decide it; a status change is recorded with old value, new value and reason in the notes of every row concerned; no claim was deleted and no date, place, confidence or flag of any of the ten rows changed except where stated.

- **`G022` (Panzer Lehr under the LXXXIV Corps): settled for July.** `C0792` (Lexikon dated list of 15 July): `claim_status` disputed -> preferred. `C0790` (Lexikon table, June): disputed -> alternate. `C0791` (Feldgrau table, July): disputed -> alternate. Reason: the dated lists of the LXXXIV Corps on the Lexikon page of 15 and 21 June do not name the division; Breakout and Pursuit ch. 7 p. 128 has the division in the corps sector by 12 and 13 July; the existing relations keep it under the I SS Panzer Corps to 10 July and under the Seventh Army from 11 July. The day of the subordination is still not dated (between 10 and 15 July). `C0792` also cites `R591` now (source and locator extended).
- **`G024` (716th Division): settled for southern France.** `C0815` (Lexikon text: coastal sector at the Spanish border by 10 July, headquarters Thuir): disputed -> preferred. `C0816` (Lexikon table, July: Normandie): disputed -> alternate. Reason: Riviera to the Rhine ch. 4 p. 66 has the 198th and 716th Divisions under the IV Luftwaffe Field Corps between the Rhone delta and the Spanish border at the landing of 15 August (new reference `R667`), the August row of the Lexikon table also names that corps, and the English Wikipedia article (`R088`, not independent of the Lexikon) gives the removal from the line on 10 July. Date and confidence (0.5) of `C0815` unchanged.
- **`G021` (Army Group B, Kluge): stays open, preferred row unchanged.** `C0714` (17 July, CMH and Wikipedia) preferred, `C0767` (19 July, Schramm) alternate. New evidence: the Lexikon commander list (`R185`, added to both rows) gives 19 July for Kluge and ends Rommel on 17 July, so each date now rests on two families and the earlier reason for the preference (two against one) no longer holds. Kept: the CMH text states the takeover itself, the Lexikon a tenure date; the dates may be two event definitions (in fact from 17 July, listed from 19 July), which no source says. Review sentences on both rows; no value changed.
- **`G023` (12th SS Panzer Division in July): stays open, both rows disputed.** Nafziger (corps reserve of the I SS Panzer Corps) against the Lexikon table (LXXXVI Corps). The Lexikon text of the division (refit north of Falaise from 11 July; Kampfgruppen to the 272nd Division on 17 July and the 21st Panzer Division on 18 July) and the LXXXVI Corps page (Goodwood on 18 July) suggest that the two rows may describe different weeks, but no source names a corps for those days. Review sentences on both rows (`R252` added to `C0783`); no value changed.
- **`G025` (711th Division in July): stays open, both rows disputed; one wrong statement corrected.** `C0817` (Lexikon table: LXXXI Corps) against `C0818` (Nafziger: part of the division under the LXXXVI Corps). Old value: the Event date sentence of `C0817` said that the same table has an earlier July row "z. Vfg." under the Fifteenth Army; new value: the sentence is removed; reason: that row is in the 1941 table of the page, the 1944 table has one July row. New evidence: the Lexikon dated lists of the LXXXI Corps (15 June, `R247`) and the LXXXVI Corps (21 June, `R252`) both name the division, and the English Wikipedia article (`R087`) has its 731st Regiment at Troarn for Goodwood, so the rows may describe different parts of one division; no source says which corps held the whole division in July.
- **Reference:** `R667` added (Riviera to the Rhine ch. 4). No new claim, relation, place or conflict-group id; next free ids `C1278`, `CR0844`, `PL0665`, `R668`, `G028`.
- **Result for the five groups:** `G021` preferred/alternate (open), `G022` preferred/alternate/alternate (settled), `G023` disputed/disputed (open), `G024` preferred/alternate (settled), `G025` disputed/disputed (open). 24 conflict groups in all.
### Item 2: the 243rd Division (`C0197` against `C0799` and `C0757`)

Open question before: `C0197` (29 June 1944) had the division destroyed at Cherbourg (`destroyed` true, `disestablished` true) while the CMH rows `C0799` (3 July, parts in line) and `C0757` (24 July, battered remnants near Lessay) show it still fighting; no flag had been changed. Sources read again: the Lexikon der Wehrmacht page of the division (`R196`), the CMH (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 4 p. 60, ch. 12 p. 227) and the English Wikipedia article (`R043`).

- **`C0197`: five fields changed, with old and new values in its notes.** `event_type` destruction -> surrender; `destroyed` true -> false; `disestablished` true -> false; `location_represents` main_body -> sector_center, with a new `location_qualifier` (the 922nd Grenadier Regiment and the elements only; old value: empty); `current_activity` "surrendering in the Cherbourg fortress; destroyed" -> "elements of the division surrendering in the Cherbourg fortress". Date (29 June, approximate), place (Cherbourg), confidence (0.3) and references unchanged except that `R196` was added. Reason: the Lexikon page has the division largely smashed by early July with only the 922nd Grenadier Regiment pushed back to Cherbourg, its last remnants fighting north of Coutances in early August and its official dissolution on 12 September 1944; the CMH rows show it in line on 3 and 24 July; Wikipedia ("last elements lost in the fall of Cherbourg") does not date the end of the division as a whole.
- **`C0799`, `C0757`: Review sentence added (no value changed)** saying that the open point is settled by the change to `C0197`.
- **Not done, recommendation:** the Lexikon dissolution of 12 September 1944 (and the commander list to 26 September in Wikipedia, which disagrees) is not recorded as a row; a row would need a new claim id (`C1278`) with an approximate place (the remnants had been pulled back to the Somme) and confidence 0.3 or 0.5. The unit stays `active` and `CR0010` (LXXXIV Corps, assigned, open) is unchanged. Scott decides whether to add the row.
### Item 3: the parent of the 353rd Division (`CR0615`)

The question was recorded as LXXIV Corps (CMH Siegfried Line ch. 4 p. 87) against LXXXIV Corps (Nafziger 944GIAB, 16 September 1944); the data never had an LXXX Corps reading for September (the LXXX Corps is the parent from 15 October, `CR0657`).

- **`CR0615` note extended; no value changed (parent LXXIV Corps, 17 September to 14 October 1944, inferred).** Old value of the open question: annotated only. New: settled for the LXXIV Corps. Reason: the LXXXIV Corps staff was captured on 21 August 1944 and the corps dissolved on 2 November (Lexikon, `R248`); CMH ch. 4 p. 83 names the 347th and 89th Divisions in the LXXIV Corps and the Nafziger file puts the 347th and 353rd under its "LXXXIV", which fits a misprint of LXXIV; CMH ch. 4 p. 70 has the 353rd nominally under the LXXXI Corps before, and p. 87 and p. 92 have it transferred from the LXXXI to the LXXIV Corps. The Lexikon table (LXXXVIII Corps, First Parachute Army, Maastricht, September) is contradicted by the CMH and not followed. No row was added for the Nafziger reading; the start stays at 17 September (inferred; the CMH gives no day).
### Item 4: stray file `WorldWar2/before.txt`

- **Removed** (`before.txt` at the root of the working copy, `WorldWar2/before.txt` in the GitHub tree; 20,106 bytes). It is a saved text output of `who_controls.py` (Fourth Armored Division, July and August 1944) committed by accident with `02e7272` on 26 October 2026. Checked before removal: no script (`scripts/`, the tools of the publication step, the workflow), schema or document reads or names it; the only mention is the older changelog entry that says it was "left alone"; it is not in `.gitignore`, not in the build, and not listed in `docs/review`. Old value: tracked file; new value: removed. Reason: stray output, no function. No copy was in the Drive folder.
### Documents and tests

- `data/coordinate_exceptions.csv`, the reason of the `C0815`/`C0816` conflict: old text "both rows are kept disputed and no winner is chosen without a source"; new text: both rows are kept, `C0815` preferred and `C0816` alternate since 28 October 2026, with the CMH reference. Reason: the status change of `G024` (Item 1).
- `scripts/semantic_tests.py`: scenario 13 added (7 expectations: statuses of `G021` to `G025`, the flags of `C0197`, the parent of the 353rd Division on 20 September 1944); 201 expectations in all.
- `docs/HANDOFF.md`: state, conflict-group counts (preferred 1,242, alternate 19, disputed 16; the earlier figures 1,157, 16 and 21 were out of date), the conflict bullets and the open-item lists updated; `docs/roadmap.md`: open points marked as settled or still open. README counts unchanged (no claim, unit, relation, place or reference count moved; reference ids now run to `R667`).

## huertgen-roer-operations: operation records for the Hürtgen Forest and the Roer plain, and nine claim links (28 October 2026)

Branch `huertgen-roer-operations`, cut from `main` (`c1ebd61`, which contains German Batch 3 as PR #22); compare it with `main`. Scope approved by Scott on 28 October 2026 ("Yes to all"). Three commits.

- **Documentation only (decisions, no data change):** Scott confirmed the open points of German Batch 3: keep `GER-COR-KVOSG` and `GER-COR-FELDT`; keep both Army Group Oberrhein dates (2 and 10 December) and both Army Group H dates (10 and 11 November); Group Hoehne stays read as the LXXXIX Corps; the Utrecht and Tilburg points stay at 0.3; the Netherlands deception "15. Armee" stays mapped to `GER-ARMY-025A`; the VG and INF id naming stays. Recorded in the HANDOFF decision log.
- **Correction of my earlier wording:** the German Batch 3 roadmap said no Hürtgen or Roer operation existed and that those rows had a blank `operation_id`. No Batch 3 row was blank: they carried `OP-SIEGFRIED-LINE`, `OP-QUEEN` (the Roer offensive, already in the table with the short name "Roer") or `OP-CAMP-RHINELAND`. The roadmap line is corrected.
- **Operations (2 new, 51 in all):** `OP-HUERTGEN` (Battle of the Hürtgen Forest, battle, parent `OP-SIEGFRIED-LINE`, 1944-11-02 to 1944-12-14, `date_basis` derived: H Hour of the 28th Division's Schmidt attack was 0900 on 2 November, `R642` p. 348; on 14 December the 329th Infantry had put the forest behind and emerged on the Roer plain, `R655` p. 592; the Green Book's Part Five is titled The Huertgen Forest, `R510`) and `OP-ROER-PLAIN` (Battle of the Roer Plain, battle, parent `OP-QUEEN`, 1944-11-16 to 1944-12-09, `official_history`: Part Six title and Map VIII "Drive to the Roer, 16 November-9 December 1944", `R438` ch. 22, `R510`). Both are `Allied` scope, `western_europe`. The windows cover only the fighting dated in this follow-up; the wider Hürtgen fighting (September, and the Roer dams attack of 13 to 15 December, ch. 26) is outside them. No separate Roer dams record was made: no Batch 3 claim belongs to it (`C0977`, 16 December, is Wacht am Rhein).
- **Operation relation (1):** `OP-HUERTGEN` concurrent_with `OP-QUEEN`.
- **References (1):** `R655` (The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 25); its page 592 sentence and the ch. 22 map caption were checked on the live pages.
- **Claims relinked (9; only `operation_id` and an annotation in `notes` changed; each annotation says old value, new value and reason):** to `OP-HUERTGEN`: `C0960` (`OP-SIEGFRIED-LINE`), `C0964` (`OP-SIEGFRIED-LINE`), `C0965` (`OP-SIEGFRIED-LINE`), `C0966` (`OP-QUEEN`), `C0967` (`OP-QUEEN`); to `OP-ROER-PLAIN`: `C0963`, `C0968`, `C0969`, `C0972` (all `OP-QUEEN`). Reason in each case: the claim is a Huertgen Forest or Roer plain action inside the window of the narrower battle. No date fell outside a window, so no `operation_exceptions.csv` row was added.
- **Left as they were because membership is unclear (listed, not changed):** `C0958` and `C0961` (VII Corps front at Eschweiler and Stolberg, cited from ch. 18, which the Green Book puts in Part Five but which is not forest fighting), `C0959` (XII SS Corps at Geilenkirchen, overlapping Operation Clipper), `C0962` (47th Volksgrenadier at Eschweiler), `C0971` (3rd Fallschirmjäger at Düren, 26 November, forest edge and plain), `C0955`, `C0956`, `C0957`, `C0970` and `C1045` (before 16 November or month-level; `OP-CAMP-RHINELAND` or `OP-SIEGFRIED-LINE`), `C0977` (`OP-WACHT-AM-RHEIN`).
- **Check:** `validate` 6 warnings (the same as before), 159 semantic expectations, `build --check` and `build_references --check` clean, review sample regenerated, the two audits exit 0; the answer grid is unchanged (9,660 keys, 0 changed, 0 new).

## german-batch2-followup-model-lxxx: German Batch 2 follow-up, Model / Army Group B and the LXXX Corps (27 October 2026)

Branch `german-batch2-followup-model-lxxx`, cut from `german-batch2-sep-oct-1944`. **The compare is against `german-batch2-sep-oct-1944`** (`https://github.com/scottstarsman/UnitLocationData/compare/german-batch2-sep-oct-1944...german-batch2-followup-model-lxxx`); compared with `main` it also shows Batch 2. After Batch 2 is merged into `main`, the follow-up can be merged normally (its commits sit on top of the Batch 2 commits). Approved by Scott on 27 October 2026 ("Yes"). Every fact of the research note was read again on the cited page before it was recorded.

- **Claims:** 22 added, `C0933` to `C0954` (confidence 0.7 for 2, 0.5 for 14, 0.3 for 6). Army Group B (`GER-AG-00BG`): `C0933` (17 August 1944, arrival at La Roche-Guyon, 0.7), `C0934` (14 September, Oosterbeek, 0.5), `C0935` (27 October, Fichtenhain, 0.7), `C0936` (15 April 1945, Wuppertal, 0.3), `C0937` (17 April 1945, Haan, disestablished true / destroyed false, 0.3). LXXX Corps (`GER-COR-080C`): `C0938` (5 Sep, 0.5), `C0939` (14 Sep), `C0940` (16 Sep), `C0941` (18 Sep, `G026` preferred), `C0942` (13 Oct, `G026` alternate, 0.3), `C0943` (26 Nov), `C0944` (16 Dec), `C0946` (2 Mar 1945, 0.3), `C0947` (22 Mar), `C0948` (2 Apr), `C0949` (19 Apr, 0.3). Seventh Army `C0945` (2 March 1945, Army Group G, 0.5). Divisions: `C0950` Panzer Lehr and `C0951` 5th Fallschirmjäger (16 Sep 1944), `C0952` 353rd (26 November, 0.3), `C0953` 212th Volksgrenadier and `C0954` 276th Volksgrenadier (both 16 December, 0.5; the 212th is under the LXXX Corps from the NAF listing of 26 November, `CR0672`).
- **Units activated:** `GER-COR-080C`, `GER-VG-212D`, `GER-VG-276D` (placeholder to active via `promote_placeholders.py`).
- **Places:** 7 new (`PL0579` Fichtenhain, `PL0580` Wuppertal, `PL0581` Haan, `PL0582` Meuse front Sedan-Montmedy midpoint, `PL0583` Bitburg-Trier midpoint, `PL0584` Ludwigshafen-Speyer midpoint, `PL0585` Heilbronn); coordinates from OpenStreetMap Nominatim (`R002`); midpoints say so in `Location approximate` and carry a precision of 10 or 25 km.
- **References:** 12 new (`R629` to `R640`: EHRI, HistoryNet, battle-of-arnhem.com, Konfliktlandschaften, the two Nafziger files, English and German Wikipedia on Model, the English Wikipedia LXXX Corps page, CMH Ardennes ch. 2 and 9, Siegfried Line ch. 3). battle-of-arnhem.com and Konfliktlandschaften failed live (500, 404); the Internet Archive copies were read and the reference metadata says so. The Nafziger metadata records that the files cite T-410 and the OKW war diary (the research note said T-312).

No overlap rows were needed.

  - `CR0005` (Seventh Army under Army Group B): `valid_to` open, basis `open_at_last_claim` -> `1945-03-01`, basis `narrative`. Reason: CMH Last Offensive p. 198 (the Seventh Army moves to Army Group G, 2 March 1945); `C0945` is linked as `asserts_end`.

Reason: `C0951` (16 September) lists the division in the LXXX Corps; no source dates the change, so the day before is used (annotated in the relation note).

## german-batch2-sep-oct-1944: German Batch 2, 1 September to 31 October 1944 (27 October 2026)

German units at division level and above for the Seine retreat, the Siegfried Line, Aachen, Lorraine, the Netherlands and the Vosges. Branch `german-batch2-sep-oct-1944`, branched from `main` (`5da3a3c`, which holds Batch 5, German Batch 1 and German Batch 1b, merged by PR #18 and PR #19 on 27 October 2026); compare it with `main`. Approved by Scott on 27 October 2026 ("Sounds good. Let's to batch 2").

- **Claims:** 111 added, `C0822` to `C0932` (confidence 0.3 for 54, 0.5 for 49, 0.7 for 8; none higher), for 61 units; 33 placeholders became active (Army Group G, First Parachute Army, First, Fifteenth and Nineteenth Armies, LXIV, LXVI, LXXIV, LXXXII, LXXXVIII, XIII SS and XII SS Corps, IV Luftwaffe Field Corps, 3rd and 15th Panzer Grenadier, 11th Panzer, 12th, 246th, 553rd and 559th divisions, and others; the full list is in `docs/roadmap.md`). Rows: command level (OB West, Army Group B, Army Group G, armies), corps, CMH day-level division rows, Schramm rows and Lexikon month-level rows (15th of the month, confidence 0.3, `event_type` other).
- **Places:** 37 new (`PL0541` to `PL0578`), none without a source for its coordinate (Wikipedia coordinates `R001`, OpenStreetMap Nominatim `R002`; regions are stood for by one town with a precision of 25 or 50 km and say so in `Location approximate`).
- **References:** 24 new (`R605` to `R628`). The Lexikon rows cite the content page (`...-R.htm`); the spot check found two rows that cited the frameset page (`...48ID.htm`, `...64ID.htm`), which does not hold the table, and all 16 such references were replaced for the new rows only (older rows keep their references).
- **Relations:** 72 new (`CR0594` to `CR0665`). 24 earlier relations were closed with `valid_to_basis inferred_from_next_claim`, `valid_to` the day before the first row that lists a different higher unit, `valid_to_earliest` the last listing, and an annotated note (old value open, new value the date, the reason): `CR0007`, `CR0008`, `CR0015`, `CR0035`, `CR0038`, `CR0048`, `CR0050`, `CR0560`, `CR0561`, `CR0563`, `CR0564`, `CR0568` to `CR0574`, `CR0576`, `CR0579`, `CR0581`, `CR0582`, `CR0585`, `CR0593`. Of these, `CR0038` (21st Panzer Division under the I SS Panzer Corps, open since Batch 1b) is closed on 20 September because `C0878` (21 September, CMH ch. 5 p. 233) shows the division in the XLVII Panzer Corps; `CR0561` (Seventh Army under the Fifth Panzer Army from 20 August, no end) is closed on 8 September because `C0839` lists the Seventh Army under Army Group B; without that closure the units under the Seventh Army chained through the Fifth Panzer Army to Army Group G (found in the first grid run and fixed).
- **New relation without a corps or army row of its own:** the First Parachute Army to Army Group B (assigned from 4 September, narrative; Lexikon: first combat action "im Verband der Heeresgruppe B"; CMH ch. 8 p. 193), linked to `C0826` to `C0828`; the chains of its units now reach OB West.
- **Operations:** `OP-METZ` added (battle, parent `OP-LORRAINE`, 27 September to 13 December 1944, Wikipedia infobox, `R612`); no Batch 2 claim carries it.
- **Semantic tests:** scenario 8 (`scripts/semantic_tests.py`), 15 expectations: the 21st Panzer Division's parent change on 20/21 September, the 9th and 10th SS under the II SS Panzer Corps on 17 September, the 3rd Panzer Grenadier, 59th, 559th, 116th and 246th Divisions.
- **Grid:** 6,820 answers before, 8,100 after (1,280 new keys); 1,702 changed, explained in `grid_german_batch2.md` (77 text-only, 1,625 with a changed parent, chain level or certain/possible; no answer of a non-German unit changed).
- **Stray file removed:** running `wc_grid.py --help` in the repository root wrote a file named `--help` into the commit "semantic_tests scenario 8"; a later commit removes it (the older `before.txt` from commit `02e7272` is left alone).
- **Tooling notes:** a relation linked to a claim of another unit makes the claim list its own unit as parent (validator error "the unit is listed as its own parent"): use a claim of the subject with role `asserts_start` and `effective_from`; an overlong `current_activity` (over 120 characters) stops the batch scripts; `precision_km` takes only 1, 3, 5, 10, 25 and 50.
- **Checks:** `validate.py` (OK: 193 claim files, 932 claims, 359 units, 22 conflict groups; 4 known warnings), `semantic_tests.py` (108 expectations hold), `build.py --check`, `build_references.py --check`, `review_sample.py --check`, `check_coordinates.py` (3 older warnings), the two audits, `check_claim_ids.py --base main` (no id reused or dropped).

Reason: the CMH ETO-OB table of the 4th Armored Division lists "X" in the Corps column in the row of 9 Apr 45 and the Combat Chronicle repeats it; the unit record gives that table entry an id. The `formed_date` is the activation date the text of the Wikipedia page gives (15 May 1942, Sherman, Texas); the infobox gives 1 May 1942 as the start of the active span and is not used.
- **`US-COR-014C` (XIV Corps), new row:** `record_status` placeholder, `theater` pacific, `formed_date` blank (no source). Old value: no row. Reason: the CMH ETO-OB table of the 95th Infantry Division lists "XIV" in the Corps column in the row of 4 Apr 45. The Wikipedia page gives 1 October 1933 only as the constitution date of the reserve headquarters and the sentence that dates the start of the wartime history is garbled in the page ("from J 1942"), so no activation date is stated and none is inferred.
- **Finding, reported to Scott:** the sources read (Wikipedia, X Corps and XIV Corps) place both corps only in the Pacific in the Second World War, so the two table entries are not confirmed for Europe and may be misprints. The `theater` of both records is therefore `pacific` (the value the sources give, not an inference about Europe), and the `unit_note` of each says so. No source read says where the headquarters stood in April 1945; nothing is invented. **Open for Scott:** whether to keep them as identity-only records (done), or to remove them once a source identifies the corps the table meant.
- **Relations:** none to X Corps or XIV Corps existed (checked: no `US-COR-010C` or `US-COR-014C` in `data/command_relations.csv` or `data/command_relation_claims.csv`), so no placeholder relation needed fixing; none was added. The table rows (4th Armored Division, 9 to 16 April; 95th Division, 4 to 8 April) remain unrecorded; the 95th Division relations stay as decided (Combat Chronicle: XIX Corps to 8 April, XVI Corps from 9 April).
- **`US-INF-095D` C0647, `notes`:** old clause "XIV Corps has no unit record in this dataset, so no relation to it is recorded, and the table-based relation..."; new clause "no relation to XIV Corps is recorded, and the table-based relation..." plus a `Review` sentence with old and new text and the reason (a unit record now exists; the sources read place the corps only in the Pacific).
- **Derived files:** `build/coverage.csv` (2 rows), `docs/coverage.md` (US corps: 2 placeholders, 17 units, 7 with formed_date; all: 217 placeholders, 358 units, 236 with formed_date), `build/unit_references.csv` (1 row), `data/references.csv` (R585), `build/all_claims.csv` (the C0647 note), `docs/review/README.md` (counts only). `scripts/semantic_tests.py`: no expectation changed.
- **Checked:** `validate.py` (OK, 141 claim files, 712 claims, 358 units, 14 conflict groups; the three known warnings), `build.py --check`, `build_references.py --check`, `review_sample.py --check`.

## batch5-apr-may-1945: relations closed by the CMH table end (27 October 2026)

Seventh commit of Batch 5, found by a check after the three claim commits. **`data/command_relations.csv`: 9 existing open relations closed with the end the CMH ETO-OB table gives; `data/command_relation_claims.csv`: 10 links changed to carry the end; the claim notes that print the relation dates and the build files were regenerated. No claim, place or unit was added or removed.** The relation planner closed an open relation only when a new claim listed a replacement of the same kind; these 9 had no replacement in the dataset (the unit moved to a higher unit that has no record, or the table simply stops listing it), so they would have stayed open past the table end (for example the 100th Division's VI Corps relation after the table's row of 25 April 1945, which lists no corps). Rule applied: the end is the day before the first table row that no longer lists the entry (the table-end rule used for `CR0447`); where a Batch 5 claim of the unit lists the relation on a date up to the end, that claim's link carries `asserts_end` (or `asserts_start_and_end`) with `stated_effective_to` and basis `assignment_table` (the same pattern as `CR0447` in the corps follow-up), `end_unknown` false; where none does, the end is recorded as `inferred_from_next_claim` with `valid_to_earliest` the last claim that listed it. Each relation carries the old, new and reason in its own note. Where a table lists an entry in more than one run (for example the 2nd Division's V Corps), the relation is closed at the last end and the note says the gaps are not modeled, as for the other table relations. The relations changed:
  - `CR0130` 3rd Armored Division to First Army (assigned): valid_to was open (end_unknown false); now 1945-04-30 (assignment_table, end_unknown false); found while adding C0664; reason: the CMH ETO-OB table lists it until 30 April 1945 (first row without it 1 May 45); C0664 states the end through a link (asserts_end, stated_effective_to 1945-04-30); it is read from the table, not stated by a narrative source.
  - `CR0203` 1st Infantry Division to First Army (assigned): valid_to was open (end_unknown false); now 1945-05-05 (assignment_table, end_unknown false); found while adding C0675; reason: the CMH ETO-OB table lists it until 5 May 1945 (first row without it 6 May 45); C0675 states the end through a link (asserts_end, stated_effective_to 1945-05-05); it is read from the table, not stated by a narrative source.

  - `CR0417` 2nd Infantry Division to First Army (assigned): valid_to was open (end_unknown false); now 1945-05-05 (assignment_table, end_unknown false); found while adding C0667; reason: the CMH ETO-OB table lists it until 5 May 1945 (first row without it 6 May 45); C0667 states the end through a link (asserts_end, stated_effective_to 1945-05-05); it is read from the table, not stated by a narrative source.

## batch4-jan-mar-1945: six operation rows for Batch 4 (26 October 2026)

`data/operations.csv`: six rows added, **no claim points at them yet** (the claims follow in the next four commits). `OP-NORDWIND` (31 December 1944 to 25 January 1945, parent Ardennes-Alsace; R012), `OP-COLMAR-POCKET` (20 January to 9 February 1945; R552), `OP-GRENADE` (23 February to 10 March 1945, parent Rhineland; R553), `OP-REMAGEN` (7 to 25 March 1945; R556), `OP-UNDERTONE` (8 to 24 March 1945, also called the Saar-Palatinate Offensive; R555) and `OP-VARSITY` (24 March 1945, parent Central Europe; R549). Dates are secondary (`date_basis` secondary: Wikipedia infoboxes); the Colmar, Remagen and Undertone rows span two campaign streamers (Rhineland ends 21 March, Ardennes-Alsace 25 January) and so have no parent; the reason is in each row's `notes`. Rows are added only for operations that a claim needs: Lumberjack, the Roer dams and the Rhine crossing (Plunder) were not added (claims on those use the campaign row, as the checklist says). The row `OP-NORDWIND` is the Allied front of the German operation; the German codename row is not needed (no German claims). Operation names in the claims are derived from these rows.

## open-items-oct26: the five undated German parent changes of June 1944 (26 October 2026)

Open item 7 (second sub-item), read in Cross-Channel Attack ch. 8 (R448), ch. 9 (R449) and ch. 10 (HyperWar pages). One commit. Result: 1 change dated (as a range), 2 narrowed to a window in the notes, 1 finding for Scott, 1 unresolved.

- **I SS Panzer Corps, Seventh Army to Panzer Group West (`CR0047`, `CR0048`): dated.** C0037 says "transferred to Panzer Group West late 7 June"; ch. 9 p. 347 has Rundstedt decide on 7 June to put Panzer Group West (Geyr, attached to Seventh Army) in charge of the Caen sector, Geyr arriving on the night of 8-9 June, and p. 372 has him "took over command in the Caen sector on 9 June". Old values: `CR0047` `valid_to` 1944-06-07 (`inferred_from_next_claim`), `CR0048` `valid_from` 1944-06-08 (`claim_date`), `change_undated` true on both. New values: `CR0047` `valid_to` 1944-06-09 with `valid_to_earliest` 1944-06-07 (`narrative`); `CR0048` `valid_from` 1944-06-08 with `valid_from_latest` 1944-06-09 (`narrative`); `change_undated` false on both. The link rows (C0037, C0051) carry the stated range. New `transfer_dates_differ` overlap `CR0047` / `CR0048` (8 to 9 June). Reason in each note: the claim and the narrative do not agree on the day, so both are kept as the ends of the range.
- **12th SS Panzer Division (`CR0053`, `CR0054`) and Panzer Lehr (`CR0040`, `CR0041`), OKW reserve to I SS Panzer Corps: window documented, no value changed.** Ch. 8 p. 332-333: Hitler gave the word to move at 1600 on 6 June (so the end of the OKW reserve is dated), the plan "developed on D Day" put both under I SS Panzer Corps, but the date on which the corps took command is not given; ch. 9 p. 347: the 12th SS arrived on 7 June, I SS Panzer Corps attacked on 8 June with the 12th SS, the 21st Panzer and a Kampfgruppe of Panzer Lehr. The change lies between 6 June (1600) and 7 June (12th SS) or 8 June (Panzer Lehr); the existing rows lie inside it, so nothing changes and `change_undated` stays true.
- **21st Panzer Division (`CR0036`, `CR0038`): finding for Scott, no value changed.** Ch. 8 p. 333, ch. 9 p. 347 and 372 put the division under I SS Panzer Corps (and Panzer Group West) from 7 or 8 June, not from 28 June (the first claim that lists it), and not under Seventh Army to 12 June (an end inferred from the next claim). Moving the start of `CR0038` to 8 June would overlap the placeholder `CR0037` (13 to 27 June, "parent not verified"), which would have to be shortened or removed, so it is left for Scott's decision (see `docs/review/verification_results.md`, item 5).
- **II SS Panzer Corps, Seventh Army to Panzer Group West (`CR0049`, `CR0050`): unresolved, no value changed.** Ch. 10 p. 442-444 has plans (Panzer Group West to take four corps including II SS Panzer Corps), Rommel's order to speed the corps' assembly, and Hausser (commander of II SS Panzer Corps) taking Seventh Army and temporarily the whole front on Dollmann's death; none gives the date on which the corps changed headquarters. Both notes say so.
- **Checked.** Validator 0 errors, same 3 warnings; 68 `semantic_tests` expectations hold; `who_controls`: 5,020 grid answers compared before and after, 1 changed: Panzer Lehr on 8 June, where the chain above I SS Panzer Corps read "Panzer Group West (assigned, certain)" and now reads "UNKNOWN at this level: Seventh Army or Panzer Group West (hour of the change not documented)", the expected effect of the range.

### Commit 2: `who_controls.py` staleness and `last_listed_date`

- **Fix (R1-N-001).** `scripts/who_controls.py` printed `[certain]` for a relationship that has no recorded end (`open_at_last_claim`) on any date after its last listing, for example the 29th Infantry Division's assignment to First Army on 31 December 1944 (last listed 29 September). Now a date after the last listing is `possible`, with the last listing and the number of days in the reason; the operational chain applies the same rule. Rule (in `schema/README.md`, "Reading a command interval"): certain only up to the last listing, at any distance after it possible, no threshold, because a threshold would invent a duration. It is the rule that already applied to ends inferred from the next claim.
- **Label.** Every interval whose end is not sourced now prints `[last listed DATE; no end recorded]` or `[last listed DATE; end inferred from next claim]`, whatever its status (before, the label appeared only inside a `possible` interval).
- **Build.** `build/command_relations.csv` has a new last column `last_listed_date` (derived: the date of the latest preferred claim that lists the relation; equal to `valid_to_earliest` for all 143 inferred ends). It is derived in `scripts/command_relations.py` and checked by `build.py --check`; the master tables are unchanged.
- **Effect on a 48-query sample** (12 units chosen by a seeded hash from the units that have a relationship, four dates each: first claim, middle claim, last claim, last claim plus 45 days; the list is in the commit message): 22 of 48 answers changed, all in the same direction: 18 interval lines went from `certain` to `possible` and the operational chain went from certain to possible at the levels that rest on a relationship past its last listing. No answer changed in any other way.

### Commit 3: semantic regression tests

- **`scripts/semantic_tests.py`** (new, standard library only, 68 expectations) asserts what `scripts/who_controls.py` answers for four representable scenarios, plus the staleness rule: the First Army operational-control change of 20 December 1944; the VIII Corps transfer to Third Army on 20 December with the hour undocumented; the 84th Infantry Division's temporary corps-level attachment and transfer; and an administrative parent against the operational headquarters. It reads `build/command_relations.csv`, so run `python scripts/build.py` first. The CI step fails the build when an answer changes.
- **What the data says (and where it differs from what a reader might assume).** (1) First Army: the change is an `operational_control` overlay from 20 December to 17 January; the assignment to 12th Army Group is not ended by it. (2) VIII Corps: First Army and Third Army both cover 20 December and the army level is UNKNOWN that day, with or without an hour, because no source gives the hour; from 21 December the answer is `possible` and not `certain`, because the relation was last listed on 20 December (the relation's note says 21 December is certainly Third Army; the tables have no field for that). (3) 84th Division: the XVIII Airborne Corps attachment runs 20 to 23 December (end between 22 and 23); the move to VII Corps is recorded as `unspecified_subordination` (the CMH table does not say assigned or attached) with a start range 20 to 23 December, although the relation's note says control passed between 22 and 23 December; an attachment to First Army and one to 21st Army Group (both from the assignment table, 20 December onward) outrank it, so VII Corps never appears in the operational chain. (4) `administrative_control` (two relations) is listed by the tool but is not in the operational chain, which is by design. No data was changed to fit the expectations.
- **Scenario 5, not tested.** An inferred position replaced by a sourced one cannot be represented yet: there is no supersession or version field, and `location_basis` marks only three claims as inferred.

## review-packet (26 October 2026)

An independent-review packet for an outside reviewer who has read access to the repository and nothing else. No claim, table, schema or validator rule changed; the three commits add documents and one read-only script.

- **`scripts/review_sample.py`** (standard library only) draws a seeded, stratified sample and computes the counts quoted in the brief. Seed 20261026. Claims: 40, with a quota per nationality proportional to the square root of its claims (Canada 2 of 4, Germany 9 of 75, UK 8 of 60, US 21 of 427), then coverage-first inside each nationality over echelon group, event type, confidence and claim status (all 18 event types, all four confidence levels, all three statuses and all five echelon groups are in the sample). Relations: 20 of 375, coverage-first over relationship, start and end basis, status, the two flags, subject nationality, overlap membership and whether a higher unit is named. Ranks are SHA-256 hashes of the seed and the row id, so the draw does not depend on the Python version. `--check` fails when the sample or the counts block of the brief is stale; `--seed`, `--claims` and `--relations` draw another sample.

## integrity-rules (26 October 2026)

Three data integrity rules, one commit each: the claim key (this section's first item), claim-id allocation, and the controlled set of note labels. Validator warnings stay the same three; no claim was changed.

### Rule 1: unit, date and event type identify one claim

- **Rule.** `(unit_id, date, event_type)` is unique across the claims (`uniqueTogether` in `schema/claims.schema.json`, enforced by `scripts/validate.py`). A repeat is allowed only inside one conflict group, or when the pair is listed with a reason in the new hand-maintained table `data/claim_key_exceptions.csv` (`claim_id, other_claim_id, reason`: several actions of one kind by one unit on one day). An exception that is not needed is an error, so the list cannot go stale. The error names both claims and the three ways out. Described in `schema/README.md` ("Claim key") and `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Claim identity", checklist).
- **Audit before the rule.** 566 claims, 566 distinct keys: **0 violations**, so no claim was deleted, merged or edited and the exception table is empty. Looked at for context: 7 pairs of claims share a unit and a date but differ in event type (C0015/C0016, C0199/C0200, C0284/C0483, C0484/C0485, C0333/C0496, C0217/C0481, C0220/C0482: a landing or attack beside a headquarters move, and so on); they are different events and stay as they are. The 14 conflict groups all differ in date or event type (sources disagree about the date), so none needed the group exemption either.
- **Table.** `claim_key_exceptions` is declared in `schema/relations.schema.json` (primary key `claim_id, other_claim_id`, both foreign keys to `claims.claim_id`).

### Rule 2: claim ids

- **State first.** 566 claims, C0001 to C0566, every id once, no gap; every claim id that appears in any of the 38 revisions of the working history is still a claim (no retired id exists). So the new table starts empty.
- **Rule** (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, "Claim ids"): format `C` + at least four digits; next id = highest id in use (claims and retired) + 1; an id that was on `main` stays with its claim, is never reused and never renumbered (a branch renumbers only its own unmerged new ids if two branches took the same number); gaps are allowed (an id that was never used); a claim that has to leave the data is retired in the new hand-maintained table `data/retired_claims.csv` (`claim_id, replaced_by_claim_id, reason`) in the same change; a merely wrong claim is corrected or contradicted, not retired.
- **Validator.** Ids are unique (as before); `data/retired_claims.csv` is checked (header, sorted, no repeated id, a retired id is not a claim, the replacement is a claim, the reason is not blank); a gap that is not retired is printed as a NOTE (none today). Declared in `schema/relations.schema.json` (`retired_claims`, foreign key `replaced_by_claim_id`).
- **History check.** `scripts/check_claim_ids.py [--base REV]` (default `origin/main`) compares with an earlier revision and fails when a claim id of that revision is gone without a retired row, now belongs to another unit, or when a retired id was forgotten or reused. A single checkout cannot show this and CI checks out one commit, so it is run by hand before a pull request (listed in the checklist).

### Rule 3: the note labels are a controlled set

- **Set found.** Sentence-initial `Label: ` phrases of label shape (a capital letter, then at most two lower-case words) in the `notes` of the 566 claims: 19 labels, 632 uses in 118 claims: Event date 108, Event definition 106, Relationship 102 (two with the qualifier `(sequence)`), Location 100, Event support 70, Location support 70, Coordinates 55, Objective check 8 (five with `(Batch 2 review)`), Location caveat 3, and one each of Location approximate, Location support fallback, Coordinate check, Command support, Opponents, Commander, Context, Later, Search, Review. It is the set that `scripts/migrate_claim_references.py` already read, plus `Review` (C0484). Lead-ins that name a source, a batch or an id (`CMH ETO-OB chronology:` 17, `Wikipedia:` 15, `Batch 2 review:` 10, `Breakout-NN pNNN:` and others) are prose, not labels, and stay unchecked; no note was changed.
- **Vocabulary and check.** New vocabulary `note_label` in `schema/vocabularies.json` (value = definition and the frozen count). `scripts/validate.py` (`check_note_labels`) rejects a sentence-initial phrase of label shape that is not in the vocabulary (`unknown label`), and a known label with the wrong case or spelling; a qualifier in parentheses is free. `Wikipedia` (a source name of label shape) is exempted by name. Zero errors on the current data.
- **Process.** Adding a label is one commit: the vocabulary entry with its definition, the table in `schema/README.md` ("Note labels", which also describes the rule and the process), a line here, and at least one row that uses it (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, rule 9).

## place-merges (26 October 2026)

Item 8 of the review in [unit_references_review.md](unit_references_review.md): the five place merges of [places_review.md](places_review.md) (section 7). Aliases added: `Caumont`, `Mantes-Gassicourt`, `Recouvrance`. All five pairs had the same `coord_reference_id`, so provenance did not change.

## review-items-1-7 (26 October 2026)

Items 1 to 7 of the review in [unit_references_review.md](unit_references_review.md) (the decisions listed there; item 8, the five place merges, is not part of this branch and stays open). One commit per item. Applied with `scripts/migrate_review_items.py` (run once per item; every edit asserts the old value).

### Item 1: the six former `attached:` entries

- **GER-FJR-006 with the 91st Luftlande Division (C0010) is now a relation, `CR0372`** (`attached`, from 6 June 1944, `end_unknown`). The source is the CMH volume Cross-Channel Attack (Harrison): ch. VII p. 237-238 says the 91st Division went into combat with an attached parachute regiment and p. 259-260 that Seventh Army ordered the division to take over command of the 6th Parachute Regiment on arrival; ch. VIII p. 292-293 has the regiment "under control of the 91st Division" on 6 June, and note 47 says the subordination ordered by Seventh Army was apparently not effected (von der Heydte directed the regiment without orders from the division). It is recorded as ordered, with that caveat in the relation's note; the start is the claim date because no source dates the order. References R447 and R448 (already in the table) are added to C0010 (`reference_ids`, `source`, `source_locator`, role `command_relationship` in `data/claim_reference_roles.csv`).
- **New evidence role `listed_by_higher_unit`** (vocabulary `relation_claim_role`, `data/command_relation_claims.csv`). A relation is evidenced by claims of its subject unit; the 6th Fallschirmjäger Regiment has no claim of its own, so the claim of the higher unit that lists it (C0010) is the evidence. Such a link is evidence only: it is not one of the listing claim's own relationships (the claim's rebuilt `command_relationships` does not change), the subject must be listed in the claim's `composing_units`, the link's `stated_note` keeps what the claim said, and a claim that lists a relation before it starts must state that start. `scripts/command_relations.py` and `scripts/validate.py` know the role.
- **The other five are not units of the table** (the 56th Infantry Brigade C0017, the 1st Canadian Parachute Battalion C0018, the 116th Infantry Regiment C0025, the 2nd and 5th Ranger Battalions C0031, the 2nd Irish Guards C0217; scope is division and above), so no unit and no relation was added. The word `(attached)` is removed from their `composing_text` entries and each relationship is kept, with the claim's date and source as stated, in the new [deferred_relations.md](deferred_relations.md) (rows D01 to D06). `scripts/validate.py` checks that file (claim exists and belongs to the claim unit, higher unit is a unit, relationship is in the vocabulary, the entry is still in the claim's `composing_text`).

### Item 2: the word "attached" is prohibited in the composition and engagement text

- **Rule.** `unit_refs.check` (run by `validate.py`) rejects the whole word `attach`, `attached`, `attaches`, `attaching`, `attachment` or `attachments` (any case, also after a hyphen) in `composing_text` (every entry and every qualifier in parentheses) and in `engaged_note`. The id columns carry no words. `detached` is a different word and is not caught. The former `attached:` prefix rule is covered by it.
- **17 claims converted** (the 12 plain entries of the review plus the 5 embedded ones; the 8 former `attached:` entries were done before and in item 1). Each claim's source was checked first. Recorded in `data/command_relations.csv` or as extra evidence of an existing relation (the claim of the higher unit, role `listed_by_higher_unit`, the claim's earlier wording kept in `stated_note`): C0105 (new relation, the 30th Division attached to XIX Corps from 13 June, CMH ch. IX p. 376-377, closed on 14 June by the division's next claim), C0089 (new relation, Kampfgruppe Heintz attached to the 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division, CMH ch. IX p. 378-379, start = claim date), and C0120 (CR0100), C0490 (CR0277), C0161 (CR0032), C0493 (CR0177), C0127 (CR0020), C0170 (CR0023), C0173 (CR0030) as additional evidence of relations that already existed (C0100, Combat Command A with the 101st Airborne Division, belongs to the 2nd Armored Division and not to the higher unit of CR0175, so it only loses the word). Not a unit of the table, moved to `docs/deferred_relations.md` (D07 to D11): C0506 (Combat Command B, 3rd Armored Division), C0507 (22nd Infantry Regiment), C0493 (the 22nd Infantry with Combat Command A), C0164 (C Squadron, 2nd County of London Yeomanry), C0211 (2nd Battalion, 915th Regiment, to the 916th Regiment, CMH ch. VIII). Relationship wording removed with no relation: C0037 (`GER-PZ-LEHRD (planned)`: the Panzer Lehr Division was only planned to join, CMH), C0030 (VII Corps with the 82nd and 101st Airborne Divisions; both divisions already have their relation with VII Corps), C0094 (4th Armoured Brigade, now `UK-ARM-004B (for Operation Epsom)`: the claim dates 13 June, the relation CR0059 starts 26 June, so the claim is not linked). C0094, C0161 and C0493 also gain an id in `composing_units` (UK-ARM-004B, GER-KG-WEIDINGER, US-CCA-002D); the five embedded ones get theirs in item 3.
- **Nothing else changed.** `who_controls` answers are the same on the 48-query sample; only the list of supporting claims of two lines grew (GER-KG-FREY gains C0170, US-CCA-002D gains C0493). The validator warnings are the same three.
- **Other words.** `notes` (140 claims `assign*`, 19 `operational control`/OPCON, 71 `attach*`, 7 placed/came under, 2 `subordinat*`, 1 under command), `current_activity`, `location_qualifier` and `strength_json` keep the word `attached` where it is the source's own description of a fact; they are free narrative and not parsed. Not banned: `composing_text` and `engaged_note` contain one `assigned` (C0052 `GER-SSPG-017D (assigned for blocking mission near Carentan)`, a task and not a command relation) and four `reinforced`. Recommendation: keep the ban to `composing_text` and `engaged_note` (the fields that were turned into ids), do not ban the narrative columns; the relationship words that matter are in the relations table.

Each is now `<unit_id> (qualifier)` with the id in `composing_units`, like the other 25 qualified entries; the qualifier keeps the wording of the source minus the name that the id now supplies and minus the word "attached" (item 2). Nine ids are new in `composing_units` (GER-KG-MEYER twice, GER-KG-BOEHM, GER-KG-HEINTZ, GER-KG-ROHRBACH twice, GER-KG-FREY, GER-KG-WEIDINGER, GER-KG-VONLUCK; US-CCA-002D was already listed in C0100).
- **Validator.** An id inside an unqualified free-text entry of `composing_text` is now an error (it had to exist before): write `<unit_id> (qualifier)`.
- The relationships behind these entries are the relations of item 2 and the existing ones (see the evidence links of CR0020, CR0023, CR0030, CR0374).

### Item 4: "First Army" in C0039

- **Checked, left as text.** C0039 (21st Army Group, 7 June 1944) cites two pages about Montgomery's headquarters at Creullet (actu.fr, dday-overlord.com, read on 26 October 2026): neither mentions a First Army or any army (they give the dates of the visits, 7 to 22 June at Creullet and the move to Blay on 23 June). The claim's `composing_text` is `First Army` and the source does not decide which one. The US First Army was under the operational control of the 21st Army Group from 6 June (CR0166) and the First Canadian Army belonged to its order of battle (it was not yet in Normandy), so the name alone does not decide it; the evidence is not conclusive and the entry stays text (no id is guessed). If a source naming the army is found, replace it with the id (probably `US-ARMY-001A`) and add the claim to CR0166.

### Item 5: the 8th Armoured Brigade under the 50th Division (CR0061)

- **Sources checked** (read on 26 October 2026): Wikipedia, Gold Beach (the 50th Division order of battle lists the 8th Armoured Brigade under "Formations attached for assault phase"; the invasion section says the division was "supported by the 8th Armoured Brigade"); Wikipedia, 8th Armoured Brigade (it became an independent brigade in November 1942 and landed on 6 June supporting the 50th Division); British Military History, Independent Armoured Brigades, p. 7 (the brigade "landed in Normandy on 6 June 1944, supporting the 50th Infantry Division" and took part in the battle of "The Oden" (the Odon) from 25 June "under command of XXX Corps"); Pegasus Archive, XXX Corps (the brigade is listed as attached to the corps headquarters, with the 56th Infantry Brigade and elements of the 79th Armoured Division). None supports `organic`.
- **Fix.** CR0061 is `attached` (was `organic`), `end_unknown` true, start 6 June 1944 (the claim date, the landing; no source dates the end), with the three new references R512 (Gold Beach), R513 (British Military History PDF, p. 7) and R514 (Pegasus XXX Corps) as `command_relationship` evidence of C0020, a note stating the sources and the one disagreement (Pegasus puts the attachment at corps level; it is consistent with the corps holding the brigade and attaching it to the division for the assault). The 50th Division's claim C0017, which lists the brigade in `composing_units`, is added as evidence (`listed_by_higher_unit`). The standing parent is not named by a source, so there is an `unknown` placeholder for the brigade (CR0375, the same pattern as the 4th Armoured Brigade, CR0058) and the validator does not gain a warning. C0020's `parent_unit_id` (the 50th Division) is unchanged and its notes carry a review remark.

The brigade itself changes: `who_controls.py UK-ARM-008B 1944-06-06` answered "no relationship interval" (organic is not an interval of the derived table) and now answers attached to the 50th Division, with the corps and army chain. The interval is open (no source dates the end; the same behaviour as the other open `attached` relations), so a later date such as 1 September 1944 gets the same answer: this follows the data, and a dated end would need a source.

- **`battalion` added** to the `echelon` vocabulary (`schema/vocabularies.json`, `schema/README.md`); its rank (1) was already in `echelon_rank`, and it is in `display_order` between `regiment/battle_group` and `other` (so `docs/coverage.md` has a `battalion` row). **No separate `regiment` value**: the existing `regiment/battle_group` covers a regiment and a regiment-sized battle group (minimal change; a split can be made later if a regiment needs different handling).

- **Claim files.** The `command_relationships` column is removed from all 114 claim files (776,126 to 559,083 bytes); `parent_unit_id` stays and is validated against the claim's relations. `common.load_all_claims()` rebuilds the text for the scripts and `build/all_claims.csv` carries it as a derived column in its old position, so the combined file has the same 42 columns. The rebuilt text equals the old one in meaning for all 566 claims (450 identical, 116 differ only in key order inside the entries: the order is now canonical).
- **Absorbed.** 31 claim entries with no named higher unit (the former `unit_id` null entries and the `unknown` sentinels) are 21 explicit `unknown` placeholder relations (blank `higher_unit_id`, note kept). 53 temporary relations (attached 37, operational_control 11, reserve 3, administrative_control 2) whose end no source dates have `end_unknown` true (38 with an end inferred from the next claim, 15 still open at the unit's last claim). The five undated German parent changes of June 1944 (21st Panzer, 12th SS Panzer, Panzer Lehr, I SS Panzer Corps, II SS Panzer Corps) are flagged `change_undated` (10 relation rows); no date was moved or invented.
- **Scripts.** `build.py` derives `build/command_relations.csv` from the master (all nationalities and dates, placeholders included: 356 rows instead of 315; the 315 old rows are identical), `who_controls.py` reads it (identical answers on every query that had one; a placeholder or a change-undated relation is now reported), `validate.py` checks the three tables (header, values, keys, foreign keys, roles against the stated dates, the interval rules, the evidence against the master, every contradictory overlap documented or an error) and validates the rebuilt per-claim entries as before, `audit_temporal_relationships.py` has three checks more (`master_overlap`, `end_unknown`, `change_flagged`). New library `scripts/command_relations.py`. The historical migration scripts that read the column carry a note.
- **Derived outputs.** `build/all_claims.csv`: only `command_relationships` changes (116 rows, key order). `build/command_relations.csv`: new `relation_id`, `end_unknown`, `change_undated` columns, 41 more rows (20 named relations outside the old window or nations, and the 21 placeholders). All other generated files are byte-identical.
- **Not changed.** The places table, `engaged_with` / `composing_units` ids, the branch/echelon split and the derived columns repeated from `units.csv` are untouched (they depend on this step only through `parent_unit_id`).

## normalize-cheap-fixes (26 October 2026)

Follows the review in [normalization_review.md](normalization_review.md) (items F1 small step, and the "cheap fixes" of its recommendation 4). Applied with `scripts/migrate_normalize.py`.

- **Command relationships.** The redundant `name` is dropped from all 1,061 `command_relationships` entries (the name comes from `units.csv`). The 16 entries with `unit_id` null (formations that are not units: "standing parent not identified" 14, "Army not shown in CMH table" 2) keep their wording as `note`; `unit_id` null is now only allowed with relationship `unknown` and a note. The `unknown` sentinel is gone from `parent_unit_id` (15 claims, now blank) and from `command_relationships` (the same 15 claims, now one entry `{"unit_id": null, "relationship": "unknown", "note": "parent not verified"}`).
- **units.csv.** The column `parent_only` (identical to `record_status = placeholder` on 354 of 354 rows) is removed; 16 columns remain.
- **Nationalities.** New `data/nationalities.csv` (10 rows: code, name, adjective, alt_adjectives, alliance, kind, note). Units, claims and operations refer to its `name`; the validator checks the references and that each unit id starts with the nation's code. The 3 `Allied` units keep the explicit multinational value. `operations.nationality_scope` `German` (2 rows) is now `Germany`.
- **Single-source vocabularies.** Echelon rank and display order, relationship groups (standing, active), `higher_than_organic` and `source_type` are new entries of `schema/vocabularies.json`; `validate.py`, `build.py`, `audit_temporal_relationships.py` and `who_controls.py` read them through `scripts/common.py`. `operations.py` and `build_references.py` read their vocabularies from the same file; the `nationality` and `operation_scope` entries were removed (the table replaces them).
- **Foreign keys.** `foreignKeys` in `claims.schema.json` and `units.schema.json`, the new `relations.schema.json` for the side tables, enforced by `validate.py`; `theater` is now one of the repeated unit columns checked on every claim.
- **Derived outputs.** `build/all_claims.csv`: columns `command_relationships` (all 566 rows) and `parent_unit_id` (15 rows) changed. `build/command_relations.csv`: `higher_name` normalised to `<adjective> <unit_name>` in 64 of 315 rows (it was inconsistent between claims, for example "First Army" and "US First Army"); no other column changed. `build/operations.csv`: `nationality_scope` in 2 rows. All other generated files are byte-identical.

### Unit lineage table (2 November 2026)

Scott approved on 2 November 2026 ("Let's create the linkage table and update our documentation"). New hand-maintained table `data/unit_lineage.csv` (schema `schema/unit_lineage.schema.json`, vocabulary `lineage_kind`: `redesignation`, `reconstitution_from_remnants`, `absorbed_into`, `formed_from_remnants`), checked by `scripts/validate.py` through `scripts/lineage.py` (units exist, kind and date basis valid, real dates within 1939-1945 and not before the predecessor's formed_date, references exist, no duplicate pair, no cycle, both units' unit_note names the other). New build outputs `build/units.csv` and `build/units.json` (data/units.csv plus `predecessor_unit_ids` and `successor_unit_ids`); no existing column changed. Semantic scenario 94. Roadmap point 216.

Rows `UL001` to `UL009`, each checked against the Lexikon der Wehrmacht pages (which follow Tessin) or the cited sources:
- **Reconstitution from remnants:** 47th (`UL001`, 17 Sep 1944), 272nd (`UL002`, 17 Sep 1944), 277th (`UL003`, 4 Sep 1944), 352nd (`UL005`, 21 Sep 1944; a US archival unit history gives 14 Sep), 363rd (`UL006`, 17 Sep 1944) Infantry Division to Volksgrenadier Division.
- **Redesignation:** 347th ID to VGD (`UL004`, 7 May 1945), 462nd ID to VGD (`UL007`, November 1944), Panzer Group West to Fifth Panzer Army (`UL009`, 5 August 1944; 1 August in Wikipedia, conflict group G020).
- **Formed from remnants:** 25th Panzergrenadier Division to Panzer Brigade 107 (`UL008`, 28 July 1944; 1 August in Lexikon). The brigade's return to the division in November 1944 is not a row (it would be a cycle).
- **Not linked (a new division reusing the number, no remnants named):** 276th (from the 580th VGD), 326th (from the 579th VGD), 361st (from the 569th VGD after the 361st ID was dissolved on 5 August 1944; the 361st ID was itself re-formed from the destroyed VGD in March 1945), 708th (the 573rd VGD renamed; Lexikon: the ID "was replaced"). The Reserve Corps renamings (LXII, LXIV, LXVI) are not linked because the Reserve Corps have no unit record.

`data/units.csv` `unit_note`, 18 units: GER-INF-047D, GER-VG-047D, GER-INF-272D, GER-VG-272D, GER-INF-277D, GER-VG-277D, GER-INF-347D, GER-VG-347D, GER-INF-352D, GER-VG-352D, GER-INF-363D, GER-VG-363D, GER-INF-462D, GER-VG-462D, GER-PG-025D: old value blank, new value a "Lineage: ..." sentence naming the linked record and row; GER-PZB-107B, GER-PZG-WESTA, GER-PZA-005A: old value the existing note, new value the same note with a "Lineage: ..." sentence appended. Reason: Scott approved the lineage table on 2 November 2026; the methodology asks for a unit_note on each linked record.

## fms-fold3-netherlands: FMS B-156, Reinhard, LXXXVIII Corps from the Albert Canal to the lower Maas (3 November 2026)

FMS B-156 (Hans W. Reinhard, commanding general of LXXXVIII Corps, Allendorf, 8 June 1946; subject index by Gustav Hoehne, about 1950; NARA M1035 fiche 0150G, 43 images, German only) was read in full in the Fold3 viewer on 3 November 2026 and added as reference `R811` (`fms_german_manuscript`). It covers the corps from June 1944 (the Dutch sea front) and in detail from 4 September to 21 December 1944. It agrees with the dataset on the command post sequence (Bilthoven, Moergestel, Dongen, Genderen, Almkerk, Noordeloos, Geldermalsen, Houten, Bilthoven) and on the handover to Schwalbe on 24 December (roadmap 258 updated). The differences, all dates: Herpt at the end of September against 27 October (roadmap 260); the attack on 's-Hertogenbosch in the first third of October against 22-28 October (roadmap 260, no new row); Chill to Bergen op Zoom on 20/21 October against 7-8 October (roadmap 261); the 6th Parachute Division under the corps at the end of November against 19 December (roadmap 262); the 245th Division at Bladel about 16 September against South Beveland on 17 September (roadmap 263).

- **Source family:** B-156 is one family with B-475, B-717, B-774 and B-762 (all FMS manuscripts written in Allied custody in 1946-47, partly by officers of the same staff), so it raises no row supported only by FMS manuscripts.
- **New claims:** `C7849`-`C7897` (49: 45 German, 4 Allied from the German account; blank parents): Reinhard on the Dutch sea front (June); the 347th Division leaving for the Charleville-Namur area; the Bilthoven order of 4 September; the 719th Division over the Moerdijk bridges, at Beringen, at Merksem (with the British armoured attack there, identification uncertain) and the loss of Beringen; Chill's decision at Turnhout (2 September), his counter-attack from Tessenderlo, Geel and the Aart crossing (with the 15th Scottish Division); Division Erdmann at Hechtel; the withdrawal to the Herentals canal line; the 245th Division at Bladel, Reusel and Best; the corps at Moergestel on 17 September; the 101st Airborne at Best; the 59th Division at Son, Veghel, Koevering and west of the Best-Sint-Oedenrode road; the command posts Dongen (19-20 September), Herpt (end of September, as dated), Genderen (end of October); the corps under the Fifteenth Army (about 20 September); Chill at Goirle, Dinther and his move of 20/21 October; the 712th Division at Nuland, Zaltbommel, Tiel and Ochten; the Hedel bridgehead (held from early October, given up at the end of November); the lines of end October and early November; the Maas crossing; the 256th Volksgrenadier Division command post at Almkerk; the three-division line at the end of November (711th, 712th, 6th Parachute).
- **Inferred values:** `C7858` (719th Division, loss of Beringen): date old value none, new value 1944-09-07, reason: the text dates the event 6 September forenoon and the unit already has a row on 6 September (Merksem).  `C7866` (245th Division at Reusel-Middelbeers): date old value 1944-09-17 (first entry on this branch), new value 1944-09-20, reason: the text gives no day ("soon" after about 16 September). `C7876` (59th Division at Koevering): date old value none, new value 1944-09-24, reason: the text gives no day; placed in its sequence.
- **New places:** `PL3573` Tessenderlo, `PL3574` Geel, `PL3575` Herentals, `PL3576` Bladel, `PL3577` Reusel (coordinates old value 51.4571, 5.1770, the Nominatim hit, new value 51.3620, 5.1650, the village centre, reason: the text means the village), `PL3578` Koevering, `PL3579` Sint-Oedenrode, `PL3580` Loon op Zand, `PL3581` Capelle, `PL3582` Zaltbommel, `PL3583` Ochten (OpenStreetMap Nominatim, `R002`).
- **Uncertain readings (kept in the notes of the rows):** Infantry Regiment "743" at Merksem; "Tenderloo" (Tessenderlo) "west of Baden"; the crossing "Aart"; the panzer formation "102"; "Gorindon" (Gorinchem); "Hoesselt" (probably Heesselt); "Gent" (probably Gendt); "Honten" (Houten); "Halderen" (Haalderen); the date "4." or "A." September on p.36.
- **Corroborations:** B-156 appended on 51 rows (reference_ids, source and source_locator; old and new values in each row's notes).

## fms-fold3-german-2: run_checks exits non-zero on any failing step (4 November 2026)

- **Fix:** the local verification script, old value `UnitLocationData-tools/run_checks.sh` (outside the repo; piped every step through `grep`/`tail`, so it exited 0 even when `validate.py` reported errors), new value `scripts/run_checks.sh` in the repo (`set -u -o pipefail`; each step's own exit status is recorded and any failure ends with `CHECKS FAILED: ...` and exit 1). Steps: validate, check_json_fields, semantic_tests, build --check, build_references --check, review_sample --check, check_coordinates, audit_command_location, audit_temporal_relationships, check_claim_ids (when origin/main is available). The tools copy is now a wrapper that calls it.
- **Proof:** a temporary row dated 1938-05-15 (`C8214`) made validate, semantic_tests and build --check fail and the script exit 1; after reverting the row it prints `ALL CHECKS PASSED` and exits 0. No data changed.

## air-naval-pilot: air and naval pilot (13 November 2026)

- **Scope (Scott, 13 November 2026, "Go ahead with the pilot"):** a small pilot to test whether the data structures need changes before the data is opened up. Findings and proposals are in `docs/air_naval_pilot.md` (confirmed against theoretical problems, recommended fixes, the open decision on `GER-MAA-260`). Only the minimum needed to store the rows was changed.
- **Build fix (confirmed bug):** `scripts/build.py` and `scripts/command_relations.py`. Old value: the main `command_relations.csv` was derived with only the ground units, so a relation whose subject or higher unit is an air or naval unit raised `KeyError` (and a higher unit of another domain lost its name). New value: `derived_rows(..., subjects=None)` takes the full unit table and an optional set of subjects; the main file still lists ground subjects only, and a new `build/other_domains/command_relations.csv` lists the air and naval ones. Reason: the first pilot relation (II Jagdkorps under Luftflotte 3) crashed the build. Main outputs for existing data are unchanged (the only differences are added rows and the claim count of `PL0089` Cherbourg, 9 to 10, from `C9438`).
- **References:** `R896`-`R911` (Wikipedia 366th Fighter Group, Saint-Pierre-du-Mont Airfield, Johnson USAF Continental Airfields PDF, 6juin1944.com A-1, anciens-aerodromes.com, NHHC DANFS Texas, NHHC Operation NEPTUNE ch. 9, Wikipedia USS Texas, HMS Warspite, Bevrijdingsmuseum Zeeland, Wikipedia ORP Ślązak, Muzeum Marynarki Wojennej, Wikipedia Crisbecq Battery, II. - **Places:** `PL4160`-`PL4176` (Chantilly, Flammersfeld, Cormeilles in the Oise, Guyancourt, Villacoublay, Creil, RAF Thruxton, Saint-Pierre-du-Mont (A-1), Dreux/Vernouillet (A-41), Laon/Couvron (A-70), two hand-worked offshore areas at Pointe du Hoc, the Villerville battery, Portsmouth, Harwich, Newcastle upon Tyne, Crisbecq Battery).

## air-naval-pilot: submarines in scope and standing rule 22 (13 November 2026)

- **Docs only; no schema, vocabulary, script or data file changed.**
- `docs/air_naval_pilot.md` section 6 (proposals): old value, open question whether submarines and other hull codes are in scope; new value, closed by Scott (13 November 2026): every commissioned submarine is a unit (6.1); `ship_type` list extended with CVL, SS, PG, CM and AM (6.3); U-boat and other submarine types handled through `ship_classes` (Type VIIC, IXC, XXI and their sub-types as rows); no `SSK` (not a WWII type); U-boat flotillas `naval_division`. Reason: Scott's decision.
- **New standing rule 22 (Scott, 13 November 2026):** record a claim even when its unit is outside the current scope (any domain, front or period), because it will help as scope grows; builds on rule 19. Such claims stay out of the main outputs and the grid (as `build/other_domains/` does for air and naval units), and coverage and balance figures for out-of-scope areas are labelled incidental, not surveyed. Added to `docs/HANDOFF.md` (rule 22 and the decision log), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/methodology.md` and `docs/air_naval_pilot.md` section 7. Old value: out-of-scope facts other than before-June-1944 rows stayed in the private notes (rule 19); new value: they are recorded as claims once the separation exists. **Not built:** today only the unit `domain` separates claims, so the rule applies in practice to air, naval and similar domain rows only; a `scope` marker is proposed (section 7, roadmap 375 (k)).
- Next free ids unchanged.
